```code
[100%]
7 passed in 0.03s
```

**P4.12 Error handling**

| Situation | Behaviour |
| Invalid row | Collected as ValidationError with location and all problems; processing continues |
| Malformed JSON or XML | Message with position, exit 2 |
| Unsupported extension | Message, exit 2 |
| Missing file | OSError message, exit 2 |
| Invalid rows with --strict | Report printed, exit 1 |

**P4.13 Logging and reporting** The console report lists counts per file, every invalid row and status totals. For CI, --strict makes data problems visible as a failed step, and the JUnit output lets Jenkins display merged results from tools that cannot produce JUnit themselves.

**P4.14 How to run**

```code
$ cd p4
$ python3 -m dataio samples/rack12.csv -o rack12.json
$ python3 -m dataio samples/*.csv samples/*.json samples/*.xml -o
merged.xml --strict
$ python3 -m pytest -q
Windows: py -m dataio samples\rack12.csv -o rack12.json.
```

**P4.15 Extensions**

1. Add a YAML reader with yaml.safe_load (never yaml.load, Chapter 34).

2. Add --dedupe: when the same test and device appear twice, keep the latest (add a timestamp field).

3. Suggest the closest valid field name for unknown fields `(difflib.get_close_matches).`

4. Replace the hand-written validation with Pydantic (Chapter 22) and compare the code size and messages.

5. Stream very large CSV files without loading all rows (generators, P3).

6. Add per-device and per-firmware totals to the report.

**P4.16 Interview questions**

1. **Why collect all problems of a row before raising?** The user fixes the data in one pass.

2. **Why utf-8-sig for CSV?** It removes the BOM that Excel adds; otherwise the first column name is wrong.

3. **How do you reject NaN durations?** Compare in a way that NaN fails (not x >= 0) or use math.isnan.

4. **How do you avoid broken XML from arbitrary messages?** Build XML with a library that escapes values.

5. **What is a dispatch table?** A dict mapping keys (extensions) to functions, replacing long if/elif chains.

**P4.17 Portfolio description** “P4 dataio (learning project): Python tool that loads test results from CSV, JSON and JUnit XML into one validated record type, reports every invalid row with its location, and converts merged results to CSV, JSON or JUnit XML for CI; covered by round-trip and malformed-input tests.”

lessons.title: Automated Test-Result Reporting System
lessons.body:
**Portfolio note:** a learning project; the result data is invented. **P5.1 Overview** labreport turns the results JSON produced by P4 (or any tool using the same shape) into a **run summary** with a verdict, pass rate, per-device table, list of failures and errors, and a **comparison with the previous run** (new failures, fixed tests, missing tests). It writes JSON, CSV and HTML reports and returns an exit code that distinguishes test failures from infrastructure errors. It is an installable package with a testreport command. Label: **Essential**. Do it after Chapters 18 and 23. Uses classes and dataclasses, an abstract base class with three implementations, logging, argparse, HTML escaping, and packaging with pyproject.toml. Builds on P3 (log summaries) and P4 (validated results). **P5.2 Learning objectives** 1. Model data with dataclasses and computed properties. 2. Use an abstract base class so different report formats share one interface (polymorphism). 3. Compare two runs with set operations. 4. Generate safe HTML (escaping) and machine-readable outputs. 5. Package a tool with pyproject.toml, an editable install and a console script. 6. Configure logging in the CLI and keep libraries free of print statements. **P5.3 Real-world relevance** The morning question after every nightly run is “what changed?”. A report that leads with the verdict and the **new** failures, and separates infrastructure errors from product failures, is what managers and developers actually read. Producing the same data as JSON and CSV feeds dashboards and spreadsheets without extra work. **P5.4 Requirements** 1. Input: {"results": [...]} with test, device, status, optional duration_s, firmware, message. Invalid entries are skipped with a warning. 2. Verdict: INFRA ERRORS if any error, else FAILED if any failure, else PASSED (or EMPTY with no results). 3. Pass rate = passed / (total − skipped), one decimal. 4. Optional --previous: list new failures, fixed tests, still-failing tests, added and missing tests. 5. Outputs selectable with --formats json,csv,html, written to --out. 6. HTML must escape all text from results. 7. Exit codes: 0 passed, 1 failed, 2 infrastructure errors, 3 empty, 4 cannot read input (usage errors: 2, from argparse). 8. Installable: pip install -e . provides the testreport command. **P5.5 Design** ```code load_results() ──> RunSummary (counts, pass_rate, verdict, per_device, problems) │ ▲ │ compare_runs(previous, current) ▼ Reporter (abstract: render, write) ── JsonReporter | CsvReporter | HtmlReporter ▲ cli.main() ── logging, argparse, exit codes ``` Adding a Markdown or JUnit reporter means one new subclass; the CLI picks reporters from a dictionary. **P5.6 Folder structure** ```code p5/ ├── pyproject.toml ├── src/reporting/ │ ├── __init__.py │ ├── model.py # TestResult, RunSummary, load_results │ ├── compare.py │ ├── reporters.py # Reporter ABC and three implementations │ └── cli.py # testreport command ├── samples/ # two nightly runs (invented) └── tests/test_reporting.py ``` **P5.7 Step-by-step build** 1. Write TestResult and load_results (validate, skip and log bad entries). 2. Write RunSummary with counts, pass_rate, verdict, per_device, problems. 3. Write compare_runs using dictionaries keyed by (device, test) and set differences. 4. Write the Reporter base class and the JSON, CSV and HTML reporters. 5. Write the CLI with logging and exit codes. 6. Add pyproject.toml, install in a virtual environment, run testreport. 7. Write tests for verdicts, pass rate, comparison, escaping, reporters and CLI exit codes. **P5.8 Complete code** ```code # pyproject.toml [build-system] requires = ["setuptools>=69"] build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta" [project] name = "labreport" version = "0.1.0" description = "Turn test-result JSON into JSON, CSV and HTML summaries (learning project P5)" requires-python = ">=3.11" dependencies = [] [project.optional-dependencies] dev = ["pytest>=8"] [project.scripts] testreport = "reporting.cli:main" [tool.setuptools.packages.find] where = ["src"] [tool.pytest.ini_options] testpaths = ["tests"] pythonpath = ["src"] # file: src/reporting/__init__.py """reporting - summarise test results and render JSON, CSV and HTML reports (P5).""" from .model import TestResult, RunSummary, load_results from .compare import compare_runs from .reporters import CsvReporter, HtmlReporter, JsonReporter, Reporter __all__ = ["TestResult", "RunSummary", "load_results", "compare_runs", "Reporter", "JsonReporter", "CsvReporter", "HtmlReporter"] __version__ = "0.1.0" # file: src/reporting/model.py """Data model: individual results and the summary of one run.""" import json import logging from collections import Counter, defaultdict from dataclasses import dataclass, field from pathlib import Path log = logging.getLogger(__name__) STATUSES = ("passed", "failed", "error", "skipped") @dataclass(frozen=True) class TestResult: __test__ = False # tell pytest this is not a test class despite its name test: str device: str status: str duration_s: float = 0.0 firmware: str = "" message: str = "" @property def key(self): return (self.device, self.test) def load_results(path): """Load {"results": [...]} as written by P4's dataio. Skips and logs invalid entries.""" data = json.loads(Path(path).read_text(encoding="utf-8")) results = [] for i, item in enumerate(data.get("results", [])): try: r = TestResult(**{k: item[k] for k in item if k in TestResult.__dataclass_fields__}) except TypeError as e: log.warning("%s[%d]: skipped (%s)", path, i, e) continue if r.status not in STATUSES: log.warning("%s[%d]: skipped (unknown status %r)", path, i, r.status) continue results.append(r) log.info("loaded %d results from %s", len(results), path) return results @dataclass class RunSummary: name: str results: list[TestResult] counts: Counter = field(init=False) def __post_init__(self): self.counts = Counter(r.status for r in self.results) @property def total(self): return len(self.results) @property def pass_rate(self): """Passed / (total - skipped), in percent. None if nothing ran.""" ran = self.total - self.counts["skipped"] return round(100 * self.counts["passed"] / ran, 1) if ran else None @property def verdict(self): if self.counts["error"]: return "INFRA ERRORS" if self.counts["failed"]: return "FAILED" return "PASSED" if self.total else "EMPTY" def per_device(self): table = defaultdict(Counter) for r in self.results: table[r.device][r.status] += 1 return {d: dict(c) for d, c in sorted(table.items())} def firmware_versions(self): return sorted({r.firmware for r in self.results if r.firmware}) def problems(self): order = {"error": 0, "failed": 1} return sorted((r for r in self.results if r.status in order), key=lambda r: (order[r.status], r.device, r.test)) def slowest(self, n=3): return sorted(self.results, key=lambda r: r.duration_s, reverse=True)[:n] # file: src/reporting/compare.py """Compare two runs: what broke, what was fixed, what is new or missing.""" def compare_runs(previous, current): prev = {r.key: r.status for r in previous.results} curr = {r.key: r.status for r in current.results} bad = {"failed", "error"} return { "new_failures": sorted(k for k, s in curr.items() if s in bad and prev.get(k) == "passed"), "fixed": sorted(k for k, s in curr.items() if s == "passed" and prev.get(k) in bad), "still_failing": sorted(k for k, s in curr.items() if s in bad and prev.get(k) in bad), "added": sorted(curr.keys() - prev.keys()), "missing": sorted(prev.keys() - curr.keys()), } # file: src/reporting/reporters.py """Reporters share one interface: render(summary, comparison) -> text, and write(path).""" import csv import html import io import json from abc import ABC, abstractmethod from pathlib import Path class Reporter(ABC): extension = "" @abstractmethod def render(self, summary, comparison=None) -> str: ... def write(self, summary, out_dir, comparison=None) -> Path: out = Path(out_dir) / f"{summary.name}{self.extension}" out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) out.write_text(self.render(summary, comparison), encoding="utf-8") return out class JsonReporter(Reporter): extension = ".json" def render(self, summary, comparison=None): return json.dumps({ "run": summary.name, "verdict": summary.verdict, "total": summary.total, "counts": dict(sorted(summary.counts.items())), "pass_rate": summary.pass_rate, "firmware": summary.firmware_versions(), "per_device": summary.per_device(), "problems": [{"device": r.device, "test": r.test, "status": r.status, "message": r.message} for r in summary.problems()], "comparison": {k: [list(x) for x in v] for k, v in (comparison or {}).items()}, }, indent=2) class CsvReporter(Reporter): extension = ".csv" def render(self, summary, comparison=None): buf = io.StringIO() writer = csv.writer(buf, lineterminator="\n") writer.writerow(["device", "passed", "failed", "error", "skipped"]) for device, counts in summary.per_device().items(): writer.writerow([device] + [counts.get(s, 0) for s in ("passed", "failed", "error", "skipped")]) return buf.getvalue() class HtmlReporter(Reporter): extension = ".html" COLORS = {"PASSED": "#1b7f3a", "FAILED": "#b42318", "INFRA ERRORS": "#b54708", "EMPTY": "#555"} def render(self, summary, comparison=None): e = html.escape rows = "".join( f"{e(r.device)}{e(r.test)}" f"{r.status.upper()}{e(r.message)}" for r in summary.problems()) devices = "".join( f"{e(d)}" + "".join(f"{c.get(s, 0)}" for s in ("passed", "failed", "error", "skipped")) + "" for d, c in summary.per_device().items()) changes = "" if comparison: items = [f"
  • {e(label)}: {', '.join(e(f'{d}/{t}') for d, t in comparison[key]) or 'none'}
    • " for key, label in (("new_failures", "New failures"), ("fixed", "Fixed"), ("still_failing", "Still failing"), ("missing", "Missing tests"))] changes = "

    Compared with previous run

      " + "".join(items) + "
    " rate = "n/a" if summary.pass_rate is None else f"{summary.pass_rate}%" return f""" {e(summary.name)} test report

    {e(summary.name)} {summary.verdict}

    {summary.total} tests, pass rate {rate} (skipped tests excluded). Firmware: {e(', '.join(summary.firmware_versions()) or 'unknown')}

    Failures and errors

    {rows or ''}
    DeviceTestStatusMessage
    none

    Per device

    {devices}
    DevicePassedFailedErrorSkipped
    {changes} """ # file: src/reporting/cli.py """testreport CURRENT.json [--previous PREV.json] [--out DIR] [-- formats json,csv,html]""" import argparse import logging import sys from pathlib import Path from . import CsvReporter, HtmlReporter, JsonReporter, RunSummary, compare_runs, load_results REPORTERS = {"json": JsonReporter, "csv": CsvReporter, "html": HtmlReporter} EXIT = {"PASSED": 0, "FAILED": 1, "INFRA ERRORS": 2, "EMPTY": 3} def main(argv=None): p = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="testreport", description="Summarise test results") p.add_argument("current", help="results JSON of this run") p.add_argument("--previous", help="results JSON of the previous run, for comparison") p.add_argument("--name", help="run name (default: file name without extension)") p.add_argument("--out", default="reports") p.add_argument("--formats", default="json,csv,html") p.add_argument("-v", "--verbose", action="store_true") args = p.parse_args(argv) logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO if args.verbose else logging.WARNING, format="%(levelname)s %(name)s: %(message)s") formats = [f.strip() for f in args.formats.split(",") if f.strip()] unknown = sorted(set(formats) - REPORTERS.keys()) if unknown: p.error(f"unknown format(s): {', '.join(unknown)}") try: current = RunSummary(args.name or Path(args.current).stem, load_results(args.current)) comparison = None if args.previous: comparison = compare_runs(RunSummary("previous", load_results(args.previous)), current) except (OSError, ValueError) as e: print(f"error: {e}", file=sys.stderr) return 4 print(f"{current.name}: {current.verdict} - {current.total} tests, " f"pass rate {current.pass_rate}% ({dict(sorted(current.counts.items()))})") for r in current.problems(): print(f" {r.status.upper():<6} {r.device} {r.test}: {r.message}") if comparison: for key in ("new_failures", "fixed", "missing"): if comparison[key]: print(f" {key.replace('_', ' ')}: " + ", ".join(f"{d}/{t}" for d, t in comparison[key])) for fmt in formats: print(f"wrote {REPORTERS[fmt]().write(current, args.out, comparison)}") return EXIT[current.verdict] if __name__ == "__main__": sys.exit(main()) ``` Sample runs (invented): ```code # samples/nightly_1012.json {"results": [ {"test": "power_cycle_x10", "device": "rack12-u07", "status": "passed", "duration_s": 412.5, "firmware": "2.14.3"}, {"test": "sensor_thresholds", "device": "rack12-u07", "status": "passed", "duration_s": 3.0, "firmware": "2.14.3"}, {"test": "redfish_login", "device": "rack12-u09", "status": "passed", "duration_s": 1.2, "firmware": "2.14.3"}, {"test": "nvme_smart", "device": "rack12-u09", "status": "failed", "duration_s": 5.0, "firmware": "2.14.3", "message": "media_errors increased 0 -> 2"}, {"test": "fan_curve", "device": "rack12-u09", "status": "passed", "duration_s": 61.0, "firmware": "2.14.3"} ]} # samples/nightly_1013.json {"results": [ {"test": "power_cycle_x10", "device": "rack12-u07", "status": "passed", "duration_s": 409.8, "firmware": "2.14.4"}, {"test": "sensor_thresholds", "device": "rack12-u07", "status": "failed", "duration_s": 3.1, "firmware": "2.14.4", "message": "CPU0_Temp 97.0 C > 95.0 C "}, {"test": "redfish_login", "device": "rack12-u09", "status": "error", "duration_s": 30.0, "firmware": "2.14.4", "message": "ConnectionError: BMC unreachable"}, {"test": "nvme_smart", "device": "rack12-u09", "status": "passed", "duration_s": 5.2, "firmware": "2.14.4"}, {"test": "fw_rollback", "device": "rack12-u07", "status": "skipped", "duration_s": 0.0, "firmware": "2.14.4", "message": "needs dual-image board"}, {"test": "bad_entry", "device": "rack12-u07", "status": "unknown"} ]} ``` **P5.9 Code walkthrough** - __test__ = False in TestResult: pytest collects classes whose names start with Test. Without this line, pytest warned “cannot collect test class ‘TestResult’ because it has a __init__ constructor” when the tests imported it. Renaming the class (Result) is the other fix. - load_results keeps only known fields (TestResult.__dataclass_fields__), and a missing required field raises TypeError in the constructor, which is caught and logged with the entry’s index. - RunSummary.counts is computed once in __post_init__; derived values are @property so they can never get out of date. - pass_rate excludes skipped tests from the denominator and returns None when nothing ran, instead of dividing by zero or claiming 0%. - verdict gives errors priority over failures: if the BMC was unreachable, the run says nothing reliable about the product. - compare_runs maps (device, test) to status for both runs; curr.keys() - prev.keys() uses dictionary key views as sets. - Reporter is an abstract base class: render must be implemented by subclasses; write is shared. HtmlReporter uses html.escape on every value from the data (device names, test names and messages may contain < and &). - In the CLI, logging.basicConfig is called in main only; library modules use logging.getLogger(__name__). -v shows INFO messages. - p.error(...) prints usage and exits with code 2, the standard for usage errors. - [project.scripts] testreport = "reporting.cli:main" creates a testreport executable that calls main() and uses its return value as the exit code. **P5.10 Sample run** Installed in a fresh virtual environment as an editable package: ```code $ rm -rf .venv reports && python -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/python -m pip install -q --disable-pip-version-check -e ".[dev]" && .venv/bin/testreport --help usage: testreport [-h] [--previous PREVIOUS] [--name NAME] [--out OUT] [--formats FORMATS] [-v] current Summarise test results positional arguments: current results JSON of this run options: -h, --help show this help message and exit --previous PREVIOUS results JSON of the previous run, for comparison --name NAME run name (default: file name without extension) --out OUT --formats FORMATS -v, --verbose ``` Comparing two nightly runs: ```code $ .venv/bin/testreport samples/nightly_1013.json --previous samples/nightly_1012.json -v; echo "exit=$?" WARNING reporting.model: samples/nightly_1013.json[5]: skipped (unknown status 'unknown') INFO reporting.model: loaded 5 results from samples/nightly_1013.json INFO reporting.model: loaded 5 results from samples/nightly_1012.json nightly_1013: INFRA ERRORS - 5 tests, pass rate 50.0% ({'error': 1, 'failed': 1, 'passed': 2, 'skipped': 1}) ERROR rack12-u09 redfish_login: ConnectionError: BMC unreachable FAILED rack12-u07 sensor_thresholds: CPU0_Temp 97.0 C > 95.0 C new failures: rack12-u07/sensor_thresholds, rack12-u09/redfish_login fixed: rack12-u09/nvme_smart missing: rack12-u09/fan_curve wrote reports/nightly_1013.json wrote reports/nightly_1013.csv wrote reports/nightly_1013.html exit=2 $ cat reports/nightly_1013.csv; head -16 reports/nightly_1013.json device,passed,failed,error,skipped rack12-u07,1,1,0,1 rack12-u09,1,0,1,0 { "run": "nightly_1013", "verdict": "INFRA ERRORS", "total": 5, "counts": { "error": 1, "failed": 1, "passed": 2, "skipped": 1 }, "pass_rate": 50.0, "firmware": [ "2.14.4" ], "per_device": { "rack12-u07": { ``` The HTML report, rendered in a browser (Chromium screenshot): HTML report for run nightly_1013: verdict INFRA ERRORS, failures table, per-device table and comparison with the previous run The message appears as text because it was escaped; without escaping, the browser would have treated it as an unknown tag and hidden it. **P5.11 Tests** ```code # file: tests/test_reporting.py import json import pytest from reporting import (CsvReporter, HtmlReporter, JsonReporter, RunSummary, TestResult, compare_runs, load_results) from reporting.cli import main def results(*specs): return [TestResult(test=t, device=d, status=s, message=m) for d, t, s, m in specs] def test_summary_counts_rate_and_verdict(): s = RunSummary("r", results(("u1", "a", "passed", ""), ("u1", "b", "failed", "x"), ("u2", "c", "skipped", ""), ("u2", "d", "passed", ""))) assert s.total == 4 and s.pass_rate == 66.7 and s.verdict == "FAILED" assert s.per_device() == {"u1": {"passed": 1, "failed": 1}, "u2": {"skipped": 1, "passed": 1}} @pytest.mark.parametrize("statuses, verdict", [ (["passed"], "PASSED"), (["passed", "failed"], "FAILED"), (["failed", "error"], "INFRA ERRORS"), ([], "EMPTY"), (["skipped"], "PASSED")]) def test_verdict(statuses, verdict): s = RunSummary("r", results(*[("u", f"t{i}", st, "") for i, st in enumerate(statuses)])) assert s.verdict == verdict def test_pass_rate_none_when_nothing_ran(): assert RunSummary("r", results(("u", "t", "skipped", ""))).pass_rate is None def test_compare_runs(): prev = RunSummary("p", results(("u", "a", "passed", ""), ("u", "b", "failed", ""), ("u", "c", "passed", ""))) curr = RunSummary("c", results(("u", "a", "failed", ""), ("u", "b", "passed", ""), ("u", "d", "passed", ""))) diff = compare_runs(prev, curr) assert diff["new_failures"] == [("u", "a")] and diff["fixed"] == [("u", "b")] assert diff["added"] == [("u", "d")] and diff["missing"] == [("u", "c")] def test_html_escapes_device_text(): s = RunSummary("r", results(("u<1>", "t", "failed", ""))) page = HtmlReporter().render(s) assert "

lessons.title: Pytest-Based Reusable Test Framework
lessons.body:
**Portfolio note:** a learning project. The device is a simulator; P7 and P10 add real-protocol adapters.

**P6.1 Overview** labtest packages the infrastructure every lab test suite repeats (configuration loading, a device fixture with guaranteed cleanup, threshold settings, custom markers, safety rules for destructive and hardware tests, and a results file) into a **pytest plugin**. Any suite gets all of it by installing the package; the tests themselves stay short. At the end of a run the plugin writes results in the format of P5, so testreport turns them into JSON, CSV and HTML reports. Label: **Intermediate**. Do it after Chapters 25, 26 and 30. Uses pytest fixtures, hooks, markers and options, pytester for testing the plugin, mocking, coverage and configuration loading. Builds on P5’s report format.

**P6.2 Learning objectives**

1. Write a pytest plugin: options, markers, fixtures and hooks in one module.

2. Distribute it with a pytest11 entry point so it loads automatically.

3. Enforce safety rules (destructive, hardware) centrally with collection hooks.

4. Record results from pytest_runtest_makereport and write them at session end.

5. Test the plugin itself with pytester.

6. Keep secrets out of configuration files and object representations.

**P6.3 Real-world relevance** Teams with several suites (BMC, BIOS, storage, network) copy-paste conftest.py files until they diverge. A shared plugin gives every suite the same options, safety rules and reporting, and one place to fix bugs. The pattern (pytest11 entry point, central hooks) is how pytest-cov, pytest-xdist and pytest-playwright work.

**P6.4 Requirements**

1. Options: --lab-config FILE, --run-destructive, --results-json FILE.

2. Markers smoke, hardware, destructive, slow registered automatically.

3. Destructive tests run only with --run-destructive **and** allow_destructive = true in the configuration; hardware tests skip on simulated targets. Skips state the reason.

4. Fixtures: lab_config (session), device (function scope, powered off and closed afterwards), thresholds (defaults overridden by configuration).

5. Configuration errors (missing file, unknown device kind, missing password) stop the run as a pytest usage error.

6. The password comes only from LABTEST_PASSWORD and never appears in repr().

7. --results-json writes {"results": [...]} compatible with P5’s testreport.

8. The report header shows the target and whether destructive tests are enabled.

**P6.5 Design**

```code
pytest ──loads──> labtest.plugin (via pytest11 entry point or
pytest_plugins)
   pytest_addoption      -> --lab-config, --run-destructive, --
results-json
   pytest_configure      -> markers, load_config() (UsageError on
problems)
   pytest_collection_modifyitems -> skip destructive / hardware
according to rules
   fixtures              -> lab_config, device (connect -> yield ->
power_off/close), thresholds
   pytest_runtest_makereport (wrapper) -> append result dicts
   pytest_sessionfinish  -> write results JSON  ──> P5 testreport
```

**P6.6 Folder structure**

```code
p6/
├── pyproject.toml            # pytest11 entry point
├── src/labtest/
│   ├── __init__.py
│   ├── config.py             # LabConfig, load_config
│   ├── devices.py            # SimulatedDevice, connect()
│   └── plugin.py             # options, markers, fixtures, hooks
├── configs/                  # sim.toml, rack12.toml
├── suite/                    # an example test suite using the plugin
│   ├── conftest.py
│   └── test_bench.py
└── tests/                    # tests of the plugin itself (pytester)
    ├── conftest.py
    └── test_plugin.py
```

**P6.7 Step-by-step build**

1. Write LabConfig and load_config with validation and the password from the environment.

2. Write SimulatedDevice and connect().

3. Write the plugin: options and markers first, then the configuration in `pytest_configure.`

4. Add the safety rules in pytest_collection_modifyitems.

5. Add the fixtures, with cleanup after yield.

6. Record results in a pytest_runtest_makereport wrapper and write them in `pytest_sessionfinish.`

7. Write an example suite, then plugin tests with pytester.

8. Add the pytest11 entry point and measure coverage.

**P6.8 Complete code**

```code
# pyproject.toml
[build-system]
requires = ["setuptools>=69"]
build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta"
[project]
name = "labtest"
version = "0.1.0"
description = "Reusable pytest plugin for lab test suites (learning
project P6)"
requires-python = ">=3.11"
dependencies = ["pytest>=8"]
[project.optional-dependencies]
dev = ["pytest-cov"]
[project.entry-points.pytest11]
labtest = "labtest.plugin"
[tool.setuptools.packages.find]
where = ["src"]
[tool.pytest.ini_options]
testpaths = ["tests"]
pythonpath = ["src"]
# file: src/labtest/config.py
"""Load lab configuration from TOML with environment overrides for
secrets."""
import os
import tomllib
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path
class ConfigError(ValueError):
    pass
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class LabConfig:
    name: str
    device_kind: str = "simulated"
    host: str = ""
    user: str = ""
    password: str = field(default="", repr=False)       # never shown
in repr/logs
    allow_destructive: bool = False
    thresholds: dict = field(default_factory=dict)
def load_config(path=None, env=os.environ):
    data = {"name": "default-sim"}
    if path:
        p = Path(path)
        if not p.is_file():
            raise ConfigError(f"config file not found: {p}")
        data = tomllib.loads(p.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    device = data.get("device", {})
    kind = device.get("kind", "simulated")
    if kind not in ("simulated", "redfish"):
        raise ConfigError(f"unknown device kind {kind!r}")
    password = env.get("LABTEST_PASSWORD", "")
    if kind != "simulated" and not password:
        raise ConfigError("LABTEST_PASSWORD must be set for real
devices")
    return LabConfig(name=data.get("name", "unnamed"),
device_kind=kind, host=device.get("host", ""),
                     user=device.get("user", ""), password=password,
allow_destructive=bool(data.get("allow_destructive", False)),
                     thresholds=dict(data.get("thresholds", {})))
# file: src/labtest/devices.py
"""Device adapters. Only the simulator is implemented in this project;
P7/P10 add real ones."""
import random
class SimulatedDevice:
    """A tiny DUT model: power state, sensors, firmware version, event
log."""
    def __init__(self, seed=0, firmware="2.14.3"):
        self.rng = random.Random(seed)
        self.power, self.firmware, self.events = "Off", firmware, []
    def power_on(self):
        self.power = "On"
        self.events.append("power on")
    def power_off(self):
        self.power = "Off"
        self.events.append("power off")
    def sensors(self):
        if self.power != "On":
            return {}
        return {"CPU0_Temp": round(45 + self.rng.uniform(-3, 3), 1),
                "Inlet_Temp": round(24 + self.rng.uniform(-1, 1), 1),
                "FAN2_RPM": round(3200 + self.rng.uniform(-150, 150))}
    def close(self):
        self.events.append("closed")
def connect(cfg, seed=0):
    if cfg.device_kind == "simulated":
        return SimulatedDevice(seed=seed)
    raise NotImplementedError(f"{cfg.device_kind} adapter is added in
project P7")
# file: src/labtest/plugin.py
"""pytest plugin: options, markers, fixtures, safety rules and a
results JSON for P5."""
import json
import logging
import time
from pathlib import Path
import pytest
from .config import ConfigError, load_config
from .devices import connect
log = logging.getLogger("labtest")
MARKERS = {
    "smoke": "fast checks run on every change",
    "hardware": "needs a real device (skipped on the simulator)",
    "destructive": "changes firmware, data or power in a risky way",
    "slow": "takes more than a minute",
}
def pytest_addoption(parser):
    group = parser.getgroup("labtest")
    group.addoption("--lab-config", default=None, help="TOML file
describing the lab target")
    group.addoption("--run-destructive", action="store_true",
help="allow tests marked destructive")
    group.addoption("--results-json", default=None, help="write
results in labreport (P5) format")
def pytest_configure(config):
    for name, text in MARKERS.items():
        config.addinivalue_line("markers", f"{name}: {text}")
    try:
        config._lab_config = load_config(config.getoption("--lab-
config"))
    except ConfigError as e:
        raise pytest.UsageError(f"labtest: {e}") from None
    config._lab_results = []
def pytest_report_header(config):
    cfg = config._lab_config
    return f"labtest: target={cfg.name} kind={cfg.device_kind}
destructive={'on' if _destructive_ok(config) else 'off'}"
def _destructive_ok(config):
    return config.getoption("--run-destructive") and
config._lab_config.allow_destructive
def pytest_collection_modifyitems(config, items):
    cfg = config._lab_config
    for item in items:
        if "destructive" in item.keywords and not
_destructive_ok(config):
            item.add_marker(pytest.mark.skip(
                reason="destructive: needs --run-destructive and
allow_destructive=true in config"))
        if "hardware" in item.keywords and cfg.device_kind ==
"simulated":
            item.add_marker(pytest.mark.skip(reason=f"hardware test,
target {cfg.name} is simulated"))
@pytest.fixture(scope="session")
def lab_config(pytestconfig):
    return pytestconfig._lab_config
@pytest.fixture
def device(lab_config, request):
    dev = connect(lab_config, seed=len(request.node.nodeid))
    log.info("connected to %s for %s", lab_config.name,
request.node.name)
    yield dev
    dev.power_off()                      # always leave the DUT in a
known state
    dev.close()
@pytest.fixture
def thresholds(lab_config):
    defaults = {"CPU0_Temp": 85.0, "Inlet_Temp": 35.0, "FAN2_RPM_min":
1200}
    return {**defaults, **lab_config.thresholds}
@pytest.hookimpl(wrapper=True)
def pytest_runtest_makereport(item, call):
    report = yield
    is_result = report.when == "call" or (report.when == "setup" and
report.outcome != "passed")
    if is_result:
        if report.skipped:
            status = "skipped"
        elif report.when == "setup":
            status = "error"
        else:
            status = "passed" if report.passed else "failed"
        message = ""
        if report.failed and hasattr(report.longrepr, "reprcrash"):
            message = report.longrepr.reprcrash.message.splitlines()
[0]
        elif report.skipped and isinstance(report.longrepr, tuple):
            message = report.longrepr[2]
        cfg = item.config._lab_config
        item.config._lab_results.append({
            "test": item.name, "device": cfg.name, "status": status,
            "duration_s": round(report.duration, 3), "firmware":
getattr(item.funcargs.get("device"), "firmware", ""),
            "message": message})
    return report
def pytest_sessionfinish(session, exitstatus):
    path = session.config.getoption("--results-json")
    if path:
        Path(path).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        Path(path).write_text(json.dumps({"generated":
time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S"),
                                          "results":
session.config._lab_results}, indent=2))
def pytest_terminal_summary(terminalreporter, exitstatus, config):
    path = config.getoption("--results-json")
    if path:
        terminalreporter.write_line(f"labtest:
{len(config._lab_results)} results written to {path}")
# configs/sim.toml
name = "sim-bench-1"
allow_destructive = true
[device]
kind = "simulated"
[thresholds]
CPU0_Temp = 50.0
# configs/rack12.toml
name = "rack12-u07"
allow_destructive = false
[device]
kind = "redfish"
host = "10.0.0.42"
user = "tester"
# password comes from the LABTEST_PASSWORD environment variable
```

The example suite:

```code
# file: suite/conftest.py
# The plugin is loaded automatically when labtest is installed
(pytest11 entry point).
# Without installing, load it explicitly:
pytest_plugins = ["labtest.plugin"]
# file: suite/test_bench.py
"""An example suite that uses the labtest plugin's fixtures and
markers."""
from unittest.mock import patch
import pytest
@pytest.mark.smoke
def test_power_on(device):
    device.power_on()
    assert device.power == "On"
@pytest.mark.smoke
def test_sensors_within_limits(device, thresholds):
    device.power_on()
    readings = device.sensors()
    assert readings["CPU0_Temp"] < thresholds["CPU0_Temp"],
f"CPU0_Temp {readings['CPU0_Temp']}"
    assert readings["FAN2_RPM"] >= thresholds["FAN2_RPM_min"]
def test_no_sensors_when_off(device):
    assert device.sensors() == {}
def test_fan_failure_detected(device, thresholds):
    device.power_on()
    with patch.object(device, "sensors", return_value={"CPU0_Temp":
47.0, "FAN2_RPM": 0}):
        assert device.sensors()["FAN2_RPM"] <
thresholds["FAN2_RPM_min"]
@pytest.mark.hardware
def test_bmc_reboot_real():
    pass
@pytest.mark.destructive
def test_firmware_downgrade(device):
    device.firmware = "2.13.0"
    assert device.firmware == "2.13.0"
def test_deliberately_failing_threshold(device):
    device.power_on()
    assert device.sensors()["Inlet_Temp"] > 40, "inlet below 40 C
(this test is wrong on purpose)"
```

**P6.9 Code walkthrough**

- field(default="", repr=False) keeps the password out of the dataclass repr, so printing a configuration or a failing assertion that includes it does not leak the secret.

- pytest_configure loads configuration once and stores it on the config object; pytest.UsageError makes pytest stop with exit code 4 and a clean message instead of a traceback.

- config.addinivalue_line("markers", ...) registers markers, so suites can use --strict-markers (Chapter 25).

- pytest_collection_modifyitems adds skip markers after collection. Doing this centrally means no test author can forget the destructive-test rule.

- The device fixture yields the device and then powers it off and closes it even if the test failed (Chapter 25). The seed depends on the test ID, so sensor values are reproducible per test.

- thresholds merges defaults with configuration ({**defaults, **cfg}): a lab can tighten one limit without repeating the others.

- The pytest_runtest_makereport **wrapper** sees every report. It records the call phase, plus setup failures (as error) and setup skips, so skipped tests also appear in the results. item.funcargs gives access to fixture values, here the device’s firmware version.

- pytest_sessionfinish writes the JSON once at the end; pytest_terminal_summary prints where it went.

- The pytest11 entry point makes pytest load labtest.plugin in every project where the package is installed. suite/conftest.py shows the alternative for uninstalled `use: pytest_plugins = ["labtest.plugin"].`

**P6.10 Sample run** Default configuration (simulator), with skip reasons and a results file:

```code
$ rm -rf results && PYTHONPATH=src python -m pytest suite -rs --
results-json results/run1.json | grep -v "^device = \|^$"

        device.power_on()

(this test is wrong on purpose)"
```

With the bench configuration (tighter CPU limit, destructive tests allowed) and --run-

```code
destructive:
$ PYTHONPATH=src python -m pytest suite -q -rs --lab-config
configs/sim.toml --run-destructive --tb=line
....s.F
[100%]
============================================= FAILURES

    assert 24.1 > 40
suite/test_bench.py:44: AssertionError: inlet below 40 C (this test is
```

A real-device configuration without the password environment variable stops before any test runs:

```code
$ PYTHONPATH=src python -m pytest suite -q --lab-config
configs/rack12.toml; echo "exit=$?"
ERROR: labtest: LABTEST_PASSWORD must be set for real devices
exit=4
```

The results file feeds P5’s testreport:

```code
$ testreport results/run1.json --out results --formats html,csv; echo
"exit=$?"; cat results/run1.csv
run1: FAILED - 7 tests, pass rate 80.0% ({'failed': 1, 'passed': 4,
'skipped': 2})
  FAILED default-sim test_deliberately_failing_threshold:
AssertionError: inlet below 40 C (this test is wrong on purpose)
wrote results/run1.html
wrote results/run1.csv
exit=1
device,passed,failed,error,skipped
default-sim,4,1,0,2
```

**P6.11 Tests** The plugin is tested with pytester, which creates temporary test projects and runs pytest on them in isolation:

```code
# file: tests/conftest.py
pytest_plugins = ["pytester"]
# file: tests/test_plugin.py
"""Tests of the plugin itself, using pytest's own `pytester`
fixture."""
import json
import pytest
from labtest.config import ConfigError, load_config
SUITE = """
import pytest
def test_ok(device):
    device.power_on()
    assert device.power == "On"
@pytest.mark.destructive
def test_flash(device):
    pass
def test_fail(device):
    assert device.sensors() == {"x": 1}
"""
@pytest.fixture
def run(pytester):
    pytester.makeconftest('pytest_plugins = ["labtest.plugin"]')
    pytester.makepyfile(test_suite=SUITE)
    return pytester
def test_markers_registered(run):
    result = run.runpytest("--markers")
    result.stdout.fnmatch_lines(["@pytest.mark.hardware: *",
"@pytest.mark.destructive: *"])   # in registration order
def test_destructive_skipped_by_default(run):
    result = run.runpytest("-rs")
    result.assert_outcomes(passed=1, failed=1, skipped=1)
    result.stdout.fnmatch_lines(["*destructive: needs --run-
destructive*"])
def test_destructive_needs_option_and_config(run):
    run.makefile(".toml", lab='name = "bench"\nallow_destructive =
true\n[device]\nkind = "simulated"\n')
    run.runpytest("--lab-config",
"lab.toml").assert_outcomes(passed=1, failed=1, skipped=1)
    result = run.runpytest("--lab-config", "lab.toml", "--run-
destructive")
    result.assert_outcomes(passed=2, failed=1)
    result.stdout.fnmatch_lines(["labtest: target=bench kind=simulated
destructive=on"])
def test_results_json_for_labreport(run):
    run.runpytest("--results-json", "out/results.json")
    data = json.loads((run.path / "out" / "results.json").read_text())
    statuses = {r["test"]: r["status"] for r in data["results"]}
    assert statuses == {"test_ok": "passed", "test_flash": "skipped",
"test_fail": "failed"}
    failed = next(r for r in data["results"] if r["test"] ==
"test_fail")
    assert failed["message"].startswith("AssertionError") and
failed["firmware"] == "2.14.3"
def test_bad_config_is_a_usage_error(run):
    result = run.runpytest("--lab-config", "missing.toml")
    assert result.ret == pytest.ExitCode.USAGE_ERROR
    result.stderr.fnmatch_lines(["*labtest: config file not found:
missing.toml*"])
def test_config_password_from_env_and_hidden(tmp_path):
    cfg_file = tmp_path / "rack.toml"
    cfg_file.write_text('name = "rack12"\n[device]\nkind = "redfish"\
nhost = "10.0.0.42"\n')
    with pytest.raises(ConfigError, match="LABTEST_PASSWORD"):
        load_config(cfg_file, env={})
    cfg = load_config(cfg_file, env={"LABTEST_PASSWORD": "s3cret"})
    assert cfg.password == "s3cret" and "s3cret" not in repr(cfg)
$ PYTHONPATH=src python -m pytest -q --cov=labtest --cov-report=term-
missing
......
[100%]
========================================== tests coverage
==========================================
_________________________ coverage: platform linux, python 3.14.6-
final-0 __________________________
Name                      Stmts   Miss  Cover   Missing
-------------------------------------------------------
src/labtest/__init__.py       1      0   100%
src/labtest/config.py        29      1    97%   33
src/labtest/devices.py       21      2    90%   23, 34
src/labtest/plugin.py        75      4    95%   54, 73-74, 85
-------------------------------------------------------
TOTAL                       126      7    94%
6 passed in 0.82s
```

Coverage is measured for the plugin’s own tests only. The uncovered lines are: the unknown-device-kind error in config.py; the powered-on sensor readings and the NotImplementedError for real devices in devices.py (the plugin tests never power on or use a real kind); and in plugin.py the hardware skip, the thresholds fixture, and the error status for setup failures. The example suite exercises several of these, but it is not part of the plugin’s test run. Extension 1 adds a test for setup errors.

**P6.12 Error handling**

| Situation | Behaviour |
| Missing config file, unknown kind, missing | UsageError, exit 4, no tests run |

password

| Destructive test without both permissions | Skipped with reason |
| Hardware test on simulator | Skipped with reason |
| Test fails | Device still powered off and closed by the fixture |
| Fixture setup fails | Recorded as error in results JSON |

**P6.13 Logging and reporting** The plugin logs connections at INFO under the labtest logger (visible with --log-cli-level=INFO). Reporting is delegated: the plugin writes a neutral results file; P5 renders it. Separating “collect results” from “present results” lets each evolve independently.

**P6.14 How to run**

```code
$ cd p6
$ python3 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
(.venv) $ pip install -e ".[dev]"            # registers the plugin
via the pytest11 entry point
(.venv) $ pytest suite -rs --lab-config configs/sim.toml --results-
json results/run.json
(.venv) $ pytest -q --cov=labtest             # tests of the plugin
```

Without installing: PYTHONPATH=src pytest suite (Windows PowerShell:

```code
$env:PYTHONPATH="src"; pytest suite).
```

**P6.15 Extensions**

1. Add a pytester test where the device fixture raises during setup, and assert the results file records error.

2. Add --lab-config discovery from an environment variable (LABTEST_CONFIG).

3. Attach the device’s event log to failed test reports (report.sections, Chapter 25 solution 7).

4. Add a --max-temp option that overrides the configured threshold for one run.

5. Add the context-variable logging filter from Chapter 30 so every log line shows the test name and target.

6. Publish the plugin to a private package index and use it from two different suites.

**P6.16 Interview questions**

1. **How does pytest discover plugins?** Built-ins, pytest11 entry points of installed `packages, -p name, and pytest_plugins in conftest.py.`

2. **How do you enforce a rule for all tests, such as skipping destructive ones?** In `pytest_collection_modifyitems, centrally.`

3. **How do you test a pytest plugin?** With pytester: create files, run pytest in-process, check outcomes and output.

4. **How do you collect results for a custom report?** A pytest_runtest_makereport hook wrapper, then write in pytest_sessionfinish.

5. **How do you keep passwords out of logs and failure output?** Environment variables, repr=False fields or secret wrappers, never print configuration.

**P6.17 Portfolio description** “P6 labtest (learning project): reusable pytest plugin distributed via a pytest11 entry point, providing lab configuration loading, device fixtures with guaranteed cleanup, central safety rules for destructive and hardware tests, and a results file consumed by a separate HTML/CSV reporter; plugin behaviour tested with pytester at 94% coverage.”

lessons.title: REST API Automation Framework (Redfish)
lessons.body:
**Portfolio note:** a learning project. All tests run against a mock Redfish-like service written for this handbook; the same suite is designed to run against a real BMC by setting environment variables, but that was not done here.

**P7.1 Overview** apitest is an API test framework for Redfish-style management services. It has a **client layer** (session login and logout, retries for transient errors on idempotent requests only, typed errors with Redfish MessageId, secret-safe logging), **project JSON schemas**, an extended **mock BMC** (sessions with a limit, thermal sensors, a chassis tree, injectable 503 errors), and a pytest suite covering service discovery, schema validation, power actions, negative cases, session handling and resilience. The same tests target the mock by default and a real BMC when `BMC_URL, BMC_USER and BMC_PASSWORD are set.`

Label: **Intermediate**. Do it after Chapter 27. Builds on P6 (fixture and plugin design) and reuses the mock service from Chapter 27.

**P7.2 Learning objectives**

1. Design an API client that hides protocol details and exposes domain operations.

2. Retry only what is safe to retry, with back-off and Retry-After support.

3. Validate responses with JSON Schema and crawl a hypermedia API.

4. Write negative, session and resilience tests, including “secrets never appear in logs”.

5. Run the same suite against a mock or a real target through configuration.

**P7.3 Real-world relevance** BMC firmware teams and server validation labs run exactly these checks on every build: is every resource reachable and schema-valid, do actions work, are invalid requests rejected properly, are sessions cleaned up, does the client survive a BMC that is still booting. Session leaks and token leaks in logs are real, common findings.

**P7.4 Requirements**

1. RedfishClient(base_url, user, password, timeout, retries, backoff_s, verify, sleep); context manager that logs in and always logs out.

2. request() retries 502/503/504 and connection errors for GET, PATCH, DELETE and HEAD; never for POST unless explicitly requested. Honours Retry-After.

3. Errors raise RedfishError with HTTP status and MessageId.

4. Logging never contains the password or the session token; repr(client) hides the password.

5. Domain helpers: system(), reset(type) (validated against AllowableValues), `temperatures().`

6. Tests: discovery and schema, link crawl, power reset matrix, negative cases, token invalid after logout, session limit and cleanup, retry behaviour, no POST retry, no secrets in logs.

7. Tests needing to manipulate the server skip themselves on a real BMC.

**P7.5 Design**

```code
tests ──> fixtures (bmc: mock or real; client: logged-in
RedfishClient; mock_state)
  │
  └──> RedfishClient.request() ──> requests.Session ──> mock_bmc
(http.server) or real BMC
          retries / back-off / RedfishError / logging (no secrets)
schemas.py ──> schema_errors(document, schema)
```

**P7.6 Folder structure**

```code
p7/
├── pyproject.toml
├── src/apitest/
│   ├── __init__.py
│   ├── client.py
│   ├── schemas.py
│   └── mock_bmc.py       # extended from Chapter 27
└── tests/
    ├── conftest.py
    ├── test_service.py
    ├── test_power.py
    ├── test_negative.py
    └── test_resilience.py
```

**P7.7 Step-by-step build**

1. Copy the Chapter 27 mock; add a session limit, a chassis tree with a thermal resource, and a request counter.

2. Write RedfishClient.request() with expected status codes, retries and logging.

3. Add login/logout and the context manager; then domain helpers.

4. Write the schemas and schema_errors().

5. Write fixtures that choose mock or real BMC from the environment.

6. Write tests group by group: service, power, negative, resilience.

7. Run them; investigate every failure (one found a bug in the mock, see P7.9).

**P7.8 Complete code**

```code
# pyproject.toml
[project]
name = "apitest"
version = "0.1.0"
requires-python = ">=3.11"
dependencies = ["requests>=2.32", "jsonschema>=4"]
[tool.pytest.ini_options]
testpaths = ["tests"]
pythonpath = ["src"]
log_level = "INFO"
# file: src/apitest/__init__.py
"""apitest - REST/Redfish API automation framework (P7)."""
from .client import RedfishClient, RedfishError
__all__ = ["RedfishClient", "RedfishError"]
# file: src/apitest/client.py
"""A small Redfish client: session login/logout, retries on transient
errors, secret-safe logging."""
import logging
import time
import requests
log = logging.getLogger("apitest.client")
TRANSIENT = {502, 503, 504}
class RedfishError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, method, path, response):
        self.status = response.status_code
        try:
            info = response.json()["error"]["@Message.ExtendedInfo"]
[0]
            self.message_id = info.get("MessageId")
        except (ValueError, KeyError, IndexError, TypeError):
            self.message_id = None
        super().__init__(f"{method} {path} -> HTTP {self.status}
{self.message_id or ''}".strip())
class RedfishClient:
    def __init__(self, base_url, user, password, *, timeout=10.0,
retries=3, backoff_s=0.5,
                 verify=True, sleep=time.sleep):
        self.base = base_url.rstrip("/")
        self.user, self._password = user, password
        self.timeout, self.retries, self.backoff_s, self.sleep =
timeout, retries, backoff_s, sleep
        self.http = requests.Session()
        self.http.headers.update({"Accept": "application/json",
"OData-Version": "4.0"})
        self.verify = verify
        self._session_uri = None
    def __repr__(self):
        return f"RedfishClient({self.base!r}, user={self.user!r},
logged_in={self._session_uri is not None})"
    # -- context manager: always log out
-------------------------------------------------------
    def __enter__(self):
        self.login()
        return self
    def __exit__(self, *exc):
        self.logout()
    # -- low level
----------------------------------------------------------------------
--------
    def request(self, method, path, *, expected=(200,), retry=None,
**kwargs):
        """Send a request; retry transient errors for idempotent
methods; raise RedfishError."""
        retry = method in ("GET", "PATCH", "DELETE", "HEAD") if retry
is None else retry
        attempts = self.retries if retry else 1
        for attempt in range(1, attempts + 1):
            started = time.monotonic()
            try:
                r = self.http.request(method, self.base + path,
timeout=self.timeout, verify=self.verify, **kwargs)
            except requests.ConnectionError as e:
                if attempt == attempts:
                    raise
                log.warning("%s %s: connection error (%s), retry
%d/%d", method, path, type(e).__name__,
                            attempt, attempts - 1)
                self.sleep(self.backoff_s * 2 ** (attempt - 1))
                continue
            elapsed_ms = (time.monotonic() - started) * 1000
            log.debug("%s %s -> %d in %.0f ms", method, path,
r.status_code, elapsed_ms)
            if r.status_code in TRANSIENT and attempt < attempts:
                delay = float(r.headers.get("Retry-After", 0)) or
self.backoff_s * 2 ** (attempt - 1)
                log.warning("%s %s: HTTP %d, retry %d/%d in %.1f s",
method, path, r.status_code,
                            attempt, attempts - 1, delay)
                self.sleep(delay)
                continue
            if r.status_code not in expected:
                raise RedfishError(method, path, r)
            return r
        raise AssertionError("unreachable")
    def get(self, path):
        return self.request("GET", path).json()
    # -- sessions
----------------------------------------------------------------------
-----------
    def login(self):
        r = self.request("POST",
"/redfish/v1/SessionService/Sessions", expected=(201,),
                         json={"UserName": self.user, "Password":
self._password})
        self.http.headers["X-Auth-Token"] = r.headers["X-Auth-Token"]
        self._session_uri = r.headers["Location"]
        log.info("logged in as %s (session %s)", self.user,
self._session_uri.rsplit("/", 1)[-1])
    def logout(self):
        if self._session_uri:
            try:
                self.request("DELETE", self._session_uri,
expected=(200, 204))
            finally:
                log.info("logged out (session %s)",
self._session_uri.rsplit("/", 1)[-1])
                self._session_uri = None
                self.http.headers.pop("X-Auth-Token", None)
        self.http.close()
    # -- domain helpers
----------------------------------------------------------------------
-------
    def system_uri(self):
        root = self.get("/redfish/v1")
        return self.get(root["Systems"]["@odata.id"])["Members"][0]
["@odata.id"]
    def system(self):
        return self.get(self.system_uri())
    def reset(self, reset_type):
        action = self.system()["Actions"]["#ComputerSystem.Reset"]
        allowed = action.get("ResetType@Redfish.AllowableValues", [])
        if allowed and reset_type not in allowed:
            raise ValueError(f"ResetType {reset_type!r} not supported;
allowed: {allowed}")
        self.request("POST", action["target"], expected=(200, 202,
204), json={"ResetType": reset_type})
    def temperatures(self):
        return {t["Name"]: t for t in
self.get("/redfish/v1/Chassis/1/Thermal")["Temperatures"]}
# file: src/apitest/schemas.py
"""Project-level JSON Schemas (stricter, smaller subsets of the
official DMTF schemas)."""
from jsonschema import Draft202012Validator
SERVICE_ROOT = {
    "type": "object",
    "required": ["@odata.id", "RedfishVersion", "Systems",
"SessionService"],
    "properties": {"RedfishVersion": {"type": "string", "pattern":
r"^\d+\.\d+\.\d+$"}},
}
SYSTEM = {
    "type": "object",
    "required": ["@odata.id", "Id", "PowerState", "Status",
"Actions"],
    "properties": {
        "PowerState": {"enum": ["On", "Off", "PoweringOn",
"PoweringOff", "Paused"]},
        "AssetTag": {"type": "string", "maxLength": 32},
        "Status": {"type": "object", "required": ["State", "Health"],
                   "properties": {"Health": {"enum": ["OK", "Warning",
"Critical"]}}},
    },
}
THERMAL = {
    "type": "object",
    "required": ["Temperatures"],
    "properties": {"Temperatures": {"type": "array", "minItems": 1,
"items": {
        "type": "object", "required": ["Name", "ReadingCelsius",
"UpperThresholdCritical"],
        "properties": {"ReadingCelsius": {"type": "number", "minimum":
-40, "maximum": 150}}}}},
}
def schema_errors(document, schema):
    """Return a list of 'path: message' strings (empty when valid)."""
    v = Draft202012Validator(schema)
    return [f"{'/'.join(map(str, e.path)) or '(root)'}: {e.message}"
            for e in sorted(v.iter_errors(document), key=lambda e:
list(e.path))]
# file: src/apitest/mock_bmc.py
"""A Redfish-like mock BMC for learning (from Chapter 27, extended for
P7). NOT a real Redfish service."""
import base64
import json
import secrets
import threading
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer
USER, PASSWORD = "admin", "simulated"
SYSTEM = "/redfish/v1/Systems/1"
RESET = SYSTEM + "/Actions/ComputerSystem.Reset"
RESET_TYPES = ["On", "ForceOff", "GracefulShutdown", "ForceRestart"]
class State:
    def __init__(self):
        self.power = "Off"
        self.asset_tag = ""
        self.sessions = {}        # session id -> token
        self.fail_next = 0        # answer this many requests with 503
        self.etag_version = 1
        self.max_sessions = 4
        self.temps = {"CPU0": 45.0, "Inlet": 24.0}
        self.requests = 0
def redfish_error(message_id, message):
    return {"error": {"code": "Base.1.0.GeneralError", "message":
message,
                      "@Message.ExtendedInfo": [{"MessageId":
message_id, "Message": message}]}}
def make_handler(state):
    class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
        def log_message(self, *args):          # keep test output
quiet
            pass
        def _send(self, code, body=None, headers=None):
            data = json.dumps(body).encode() if body is not None else
b""
            self.send_response(code)
            if body is not None:
                self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
            self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(data)))
            for k, v in (headers or {}).items():
                self.send_header(k, v)
            self.end_headers()
            self.wfile.write(data)
        def _body(self):
            length = int(self.headers.get("Content-Length", 0))
            try:
                return json.loads(self.rfile.read(length) or b"{}")
            except json.JSONDecodeError:
                return None
        def _authorized(self):
            token = self.headers.get("X-Auth-Token")
            if token and token in state.sessions.values():
                return True
            auth = self.headers.get("Authorization", "")
            if auth.startswith("Basic "):
                user, _, pw =
base64.b64decode(auth[6:]).decode().partition(":")
                return (user, pw) == (USER, PASSWORD)
            return False
        def _gate(self, public=False):
            state.requests += 1
            if state.fail_next > 0:
                state.fail_next -= 1
                self._send(503,
redfish_error("Base.1.0.ServiceTemporarilyUnavailable",
                                              "BMC is starting"),
{"Retry-After": "1"})
                return False
            if not public and not self._authorized():
                self._send(401,
redfish_error("Base.1.0.InsufficientPrivilege", "Authentication
required"),
                           {"WWW-Authenticate": 'Basic realm="mock"'})
                return False
            return True
        def _system(self):
            return {"@odata.id": SYSTEM, "@odata.type":
"#ComputerSystem.v1_20_0.ComputerSystem",
                    "Id": "1", "Name": "Mock System", "PowerState":
state.power,
                    "AssetTag": state.asset_tag,
                    "Status": {"State": "Enabled", "Health": "OK"},
                    "Actions": {"#ComputerSystem.Reset": {
                        "target": RESET,
"ResetType@Redfish.AllowableValues": RESET_TYPES}}}
        def do_GET(self):
            if self.path == "/redfish/v1":
                if self._gate(public=True):
                    self._send(200, {"@odata.id": "/redfish/v1", "Id":
"RootService",
                                     "RedfishVersion": "1.17.0",
                                     "Systems": {"@odata.id":
"/redfish/v1/Systems"},
                                     "Chassis": {"@odata.id":
"/redfish/v1/Chassis"},
                                     "SessionService": {"@odata.id":
"/redfish/v1/SessionService"}})
                return
            if not self._gate():
                return
            if self.path == "/redfish/v1/Systems":
                self._send(200, {"@odata.id": "/redfish/v1/Systems",
"Name": "Systems",
                                 "Members": [{"@odata.id": SYSTEM}],
"Members@odata.count": 1})
            elif self.path == "/redfish/v1/SessionService":
                self._send(200, {"@odata.id": self.path, "Id":
"SessionService", "ServiceEnabled": True,
                                 "Sessions": {"@odata.id":
"/redfish/v1/SessionService/Sessions"}})
            elif self.path == "/redfish/v1/Chassis":
                self._send(200, {"@odata.id": self.path, "Members":
[{"@odata.id": "/redfish/v1/Chassis/1"}],
                                 "Members@odata.count": 1})
            elif self.path == "/redfish/v1/Chassis/1":
                self._send(200, {"@odata.id": self.path, "Id": "1",
"ChassisType": "RackMount",
                                 "Thermal": {"@odata.id":
"/redfish/v1/Chassis/1/Thermal"}})
            elif self.path == "/redfish/v1/Chassis/1/Thermal":
                self._send(200, {"@odata.id": self.path, "Id":
"Thermal", "Temperatures": [
                    {"Name": name, "ReadingCelsius": value,
"UpperThresholdCritical": 95.0 if name == "CPU0" else 45.0,
                     "Status": {"State": "Enabled", "Health": "OK" if
value < 85 else "Critical"}}
                    for name, value in state.temps.items()]})
            elif self.path == SYSTEM:
                self._send(200, self._system(), {"ETag":
f'W/"{state.etag_version}"'})
            else:
                self._send(404,
redfish_error("Base.1.0.ResourceMissingAtURI", f"{self.path} not
found"))
        def do_PATCH(self):
            if not self._gate():
                return
            if self.path != SYSTEM:
                self._send(405,
redfish_error("Base.1.0.OperationNotAllowed", "PATCH not allowed
here"))
                return
            body = self._body()
            if body is None:
                self._send(400,
redfish_error("Base.1.0.MalformedJSON", "Body is not valid JSON"))
                return
            unknown = set(body) - {"AssetTag"}
            if unknown:
                self._send(400,
redfish_error("Base.1.0.PropertyUnknown", f"Unknown property
{sorted(unknown)[0]}"))
                return
            match = self.headers.get("If-Match")
            if match and match != f'W/"{state.etag_version}"':
                self._send(412,
redfish_error("Base.1.0.PreconditionFailed", "ETag does not match"))
                return
            state.asset_tag = str(body["AssetTag"])[:32]
            state.etag_version += 1
            self._send(200, self._system(), {"ETag":
f'W/"{state.etag_version}"'})
        def do_POST(self):
            if self.path == "/redfish/v1/SessionService/Sessions":
                if not self._gate(public=True):
                    return
                body = self._body() or {}
                if (body.get("UserName"), body.get("Password")) !=
(USER, PASSWORD):
                    self._send(401,
redfish_error("Base.1.0.NoValidSession", "Invalid credentials"))
                    return
                if len(state.sessions) >= state.max_sessions:
                    self._send(503,
redfish_error("Base.1.0.SessionLimitExceeded", "Too many sessions"))
                    return
                sid = str(max(map(int, state.sessions), default=0) +
1)
                state.sessions[sid] = secrets.token_hex(16)
                location =
f"/redfish/v1/SessionService/Sessions/{sid}"
                self._send(201, {"@odata.id": location, "Id": sid,
"UserName": USER},
                           {"X-Auth-Token": state.sessions[sid],
"Location": location})
                return
            if not self._gate():
                return
            if self.path != RESET:
                self._send(404,
redfish_error("Base.1.0.ResourceMissingAtURI", f"{self.path} not
found"))
                return
            reset_type = (self._body() or {}).get("ResetType")
            if reset_type not in RESET_TYPES:
                self._send(400,
redfish_error("Base.1.0.ActionParameterValueNotInList",
                                              f"ResetType {reset_type!
r} not supported"))
                return
            state.power = "Off" if reset_type in ("ForceOff",
"GracefulShutdown") else "On"
            self._send(204)
        def do_DELETE(self):
            prefix = "/redfish/v1/SessionService/Sessions/"
            if not self._gate():
                return
            sid = self.path.removeprefix(prefix)
            if self.path.startswith(prefix) and sid in state.sessions:
                del state.sessions[sid]
                self._send(204)
            else:
                self._send(404,
redfish_error("Base.1.0.ResourceMissingAtURI", f"{self.path} not
found"))
    return Handler
def start(port=0):
    """Start the mock in a background thread. Returns (server, state,
base_url)."""
    state = State()
    server = ThreadingHTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", port),
make_handler(state))
    threading.Thread(target=server.serve_forever, daemon=True).start()
    return server, state, f"http://127.0.0.1:{server.server_port}"
if __name__ == "__main__":
    srv, _, url = start(8000)
    print(f"Mock Redfish service on {url} (user {USER!r}); Ctrl+C to
stop")
    try:
        threading.Event().wait()
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        srv.shutdown()
```

**P7.9 Code walkthrough**

- request(..., expected=(200,), retry=None): callers state which status codes count as success. retry=None means “decide from the method”: idempotent methods are retried, POST is not, because repeating a POST can repeat an action.

- Back-off doubles each attempt (backoff_s * 2 ** (attempt - 1)) unless the server sends Retry-After. sleep is injectable, so tests run instantly (the client fixture passes sleep=lambda s: None).

- Logging: log.debug records method, path, status and time, never headers or bodies. Login logs only the session number. A dedicated test (test_password_and_token_never_logged) captures DEBUG logs from all libraries and asserts the password and token are absent.

- RedfishError extracts MessageId defensively: error bodies from proxies or crashed services may not be Redfish JSON.

- __exit__ always logs out, even when a test fails inside the with block; logout() clears the token in a finally.

- reset() reads the action target and allowed values from the resource and refuses unsupported types **before** sending anything.

- schema_errors() returns a list of readable path: message strings, so a failing assertion shows every problem at once.

- **A bug found by the tests:** while building this project,

```code
test_every_link_from_root_resolves failed with GET
```

/redfish/v1/SessionService -> HTTP 404. The Chapter 27 mock advertised a SessionService link in its service root but never served that resource. A real BMC with such a dangling link would fail Redfish conformance checks; the crawler test is cheap and finds this class of bug immediately. The mock was fixed, and a chassis tree was added so the crawler also reaches the thermal resource.
