**P7.12 Error handling**

| Situation | Behaviour |
| 502/503/504 on GET/PATCH/DELETE | Retried with back-off; RedfishError after the last attempt |
| Same on POST | Not retried; RedfishError immediately |
| Connection error | Retried for idempotent methods, then re-raised |
| Unexpected status | RedfishError with status and MessageId |
| Unsupported reset type | ValueError before any request |
| Test failure inside with | Session still deleted |

```code
RedfishClient(...)
```

**P7.13 Logging and reporting** INFO: login/logout with session numbers; WARNING: every retry with status and delay; DEBUG: each request with timing. JUnit XML from pytest feeds Jenkins (Chapter 32) or P5’s report via P4’s converter.

**P7.14 How to run**

```code
$ cd p7
$ python3 -m pip install requests jsonschema pytest
$ python3 -m pytest -q                                   # against the
mock
$ BMC_URL=https://10.0.0.42 BMC_USER=tester BMC_PASSWORD=... python3 -
m pytest -q   # real BMC (lab only)
```

Against a real BMC: run first on a dedicated test system, because the power tests power-cycle the host. Lab BMCs with self-signed certificates need verify= pointing at the lab CA (Chapter 34); add that to the bmc fixture configuration.

**P7.15 Extensions**

1. Add a verify option (CA bundle path) to the fixtures for real BMCs.

2. Validate every crawled resource against the official DMTF schema named in its `@odata.type.`

3. Add ETag/If-Match tests for concurrent PATCH (Chapter 27).

4. Add a firmware-inventory test that compares versions with an expected manifest.

5. Measure response times per resource and report the slowest (honestly labelled as mock or real).

6. Package the fixtures as a P6-style pytest plugin so other suites can use client directly.

**P7.16 Interview questions**

1. **Which requests do you retry automatically?** Idempotent ones on transient errors; never POST actions blindly.

2. **How do you make sure tests never leak sessions?** Context manager or fixture teardown that always deletes the session; a test for the session limit.

3. **How do you prove secrets are not logged?** Capture logs at DEBUG and assert the secret strings are absent.

4. **Why crawl the service from the root?** Finds dangling links and unreachable resources; avoids hard-coded paths.

5. **How do you run the same tests against a mock and a real BMC?** Fixtures choose the target from configuration; tests that need mock control skip on real hardware.

**P7.17 Portfolio description** “P7 apitest (learning project): Redfish API test framework with a session-managing client (safe retries, typed errors, secret-free logging), JSON Schema validation, a hypermedia crawler, and 17 pytest tests covering discovery, actions, negative cases, session limits and resilience against a mock BMC; designed to switch to a real BMC through environment configuration.”

lessons.title: Linux Command Execution and System Health Checker
lessons.body:
**Portfolio note:** a learning project. The “remote” host in the sample run is an OpenSSH server on the same machine (port 2222), and the “dead” host is a port where nothing listens; both stand in for lab machines.

**P8.1 Overview** healthcheck runs a set of health checks (disk, memory, load, required processes, required tools) on many Linux hosts at once, locally or over SSH, with a timeout on every command. Results are graded OK/WARN/CRIT/UNKNOWN, printed as a table, written as P5-compatible JSON, and summarised in a Nagios-style exit code. Commands go through an **executor interface**, so checks do not know whether they run locally, over SSH or against a fake in tests. Label: **Intermediate**. Do it after Chapter 28. Uses subprocess, exit codes, SSH, safe quoting, threads and dependency injection. Builds on P6 (structure, configuration) and P5 (report format).

**P8.2 Learning objectives**

1. Define an executor interface and implement local and SSH executors.

2. Handle timeouts, missing commands and SSH failures as distinct, reportable outcomes.

3. Separate command execution from parsing so that parsing is unit-testable.

4. Run checks on many hosts in parallel and report one clear result for unreachable hosts.

5. Quote remote arguments safely.

6. Use conventional exit codes (Nagios: 0 OK, 1 WARN, 2 CRIT, 3 UNKNOWN).

**P8.3 Real-world relevance** Before a nightly run, labs check that every agent and DUT host is healthy: disk space for logs, memory, load from leftover processes, required daemons and tools installed. Failing fast with “rack12 unreachable” or “disk 95% on agent-3” saves a night of misleading test failures. The executor pattern is also the base for hardware command execution in P9 and P10.

**P8.4 Requirements**

1. Configuration (TOML): hosts (local or SSH with port, user, key, known-hosts file), required processes and tools, warning/critical limits.

2. Checks: disk usage of /, memory used (from MemAvailable), 5-minute load per CPU, pgrep -x for processes, command -v for tools.

3. Every command has a timeout; timeouts and SSH errors produce UNKNOWN with the reason.

4. An unreachable host produces **one** UNKNOWN result, not one per check.

5. Remote arguments are quoted with shlex.join.

6. Output: table, optional JSON in labreport (P5) format, exit code = worst status (0/1/2/3).

7. Checks run in parallel across hosts (thread pool).

**P8.5 Design**

```code
runner.main ──> config ──> make_executor(host) ──> LocalExecutor |
SshExecutor | (FakeExecutor in tests)
     │                                    ▲
     └── ThreadPoolExecutor ── run_checks(executor, cfg) ──
check_reachable, check_disk, check_memory, ...
                                              │                    │
                                              │             parse_df,
parse_meminfo, parse_loadavg (pure)
                                              └──> CheckResult ──>
table / to_labreport() / exit code
```

**P8.6 Folder structure**

```code
p8/
├── pyproject.toml
├── lab.toml                       # sample configuration
├── src/healthcheck/
│   ├── __init__.py
│   ├── executors/
│   │   ├── __init__.py
│   │   ├── base.py                # CommandResult, Executor protocol
│   │   ├── local.py
│   │   └── ssh.py
│   ├── checks.py
│   └── runner.py
└── tests/test_healthcheck.py
```

**P8.7 Step-by-step build**

1. Define CommandResult and the Executor protocol.

2. Implement LocalExecutor with timeouts and “command not found” handling.

3. Implement SshExecutor with BatchMode, ConnectTimeout, key and known-hosts options and shlex.join for the remote command.

4. Write pure parsers (parse_df, parse_meminfo, parse_loadavg) and test them with sample text.

5. Write checks that use an executor and the parsers; map failures to UNKNOWN.

6. Add the reachability probe and the parallel runner with table, JSON and exit code.

7. Test with a FakeExecutor, plus a few real local-executor tests.

**P8.8 Complete code**

```code
# file: src/healthcheck/executors/__init__.py
"""Executors run commands somewhere and return a CommandResult. Checks
never call subprocess directly."""
from .base import CommandResult, Executor
from .local import LocalExecutor
from .ssh import SshExecutor
__all__ = ["CommandResult", "Executor", "LocalExecutor",
"SshExecutor"]
# file: src/healthcheck/executors/base.py
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Protocol
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class CommandResult:
    command: str
    returncode: int          # -1 = timed out, 127 = not found, 255 =
SSH connection problem
    stdout: str
    stderr: str
    duration_s: float
    @property
    def ok(self):
        return self.returncode == 0
class Executor(Protocol):
    name: str
    def run(self, argv: list[str], timeout: float = 30.0) ->
CommandResult: ...
# file: src/healthcheck/executors/local.py
import shlex
import subprocess
import time
from .base import CommandResult
class LocalExecutor:
    def __init__(self, name="localhost"):
        self.name = name
    def run(self, argv, timeout=30.0):
        start = time.monotonic()
        try:
            r = subprocess.run(argv, capture_output=True, text=True,
timeout=timeout,
                               stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL)
            code, out, err = r.returncode, r.stdout, r.stderr
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
            code, out, err = -1, "", f"timed out after {timeout} s"
        except FileNotFoundError:
            code, out, err = 127, "", f"command not found: {argv[0]}"
        return CommandResult(shlex.join(argv), code, out, err,
round(time.monotonic() - start, 3))
# file: src/healthcheck/executors/ssh.py
import shlex
import subprocess
import time
from .base import CommandResult
class SshExecutor:
    """Runs commands with the OpenSSH client. Arguments are quoted for
the remote shell."""
    def __init__(self, name, host, user, port=22, key_file=None,
known_hosts=None, connect_timeout=5):
        self.name = name
        self.base = ["ssh", "-p", str(port), "-o", "BatchMode=yes", "-
o", f"ConnectTimeout={connect_timeout}"]
        if key_file:
            self.base += ["-i", key_file]
        if known_hosts:
            self.base += ["-o", f"UserKnownHostsFile={known_hosts}"]
        self.base.append(f"{user}@{host}")
    def run(self, argv, timeout=30.0):
        remote = shlex.join(argv)                    # safe even if
arguments contain spaces or ;
        start = time.monotonic()
        try:
            r = subprocess.run(self.base + [remote],
capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout,
                               stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL)
            code, out, err = r.returncode, r.stdout, r.stderr
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
            code, out, err = -1, "", f"timed out after {timeout} s"
        return CommandResult(remote, code, out, err,
round(time.monotonic() - start, 3))
# file: src/healthcheck/checks.py
"""Health checks. Each takes an executor and limits, returns a
CheckResult. Pure parsing is separate."""
from dataclasses import dataclass
OK, WARN, CRIT, UNKNOWN = "OK", "WARN", "CRIT", "UNKNOWN"
SEVERITY = {OK: 0, WARN: 1, CRIT: 2, UNKNOWN: 3}          # Nagios-
style exit codes
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class CheckResult:
    host: str
    check: str
    status: str
    value: str
    message: str = ""
def grade(value, warn, crit):
    return CRIT if value >= crit else WARN if value >= warn else OK
def parse_df(text):
    """`df -P <path>` -> used percent of the last line."""
    return int(text.strip().splitlines()[-1].split()[4].rstrip("%"))
def parse_meminfo(text):
    """/proc/meminfo -> used percent based on MemAvailable."""
    kv = {line.split(":")[0]: int(line.split()[1]) for line in
text.splitlines() if line.strip()}
    return round(100 * (1 - kv["MemAvailable"] / kv["MemTotal"]), 1)
def parse_loadavg(text, cpus):
    """/proc/loadavg -> 5-minute load per CPU."""
    return round(float(text.split()[1]) / cpus, 2)
def _unknown(ex, name, result):
    detail = result.stderr.strip().splitlines()[-1] if
result.stderr.strip() else f"exit {result.returncode}"
    return CheckResult(ex.name, name, UNKNOWN, "-", detail)
def check_disk(ex, path="/", warn=80, crit=90):
    r = ex.run(["df", "-P", path], timeout=10)
    if not r.ok:
        return _unknown(ex, f"disk {path}", r)
    used = parse_df(r.stdout)
    return CheckResult(ex.name, f"disk {path}", grade(used, warn,
crit), f"{used}%", f"limits {warn}/{crit}%")
def check_memory(ex, warn=85, crit=95):
    r = ex.run(["cat", "/proc/meminfo"], timeout=10)
    if not r.ok:
        return _unknown(ex, "memory", r)
    used = parse_meminfo(r.stdout)
    return CheckResult(ex.name, "memory", grade(used, warn, crit),
f"{used}%", f"limits {warn}/{crit}%")
def check_load(ex, warn=1.5, crit=3.0):
    cpus = ex.run(["nproc"], timeout=10)
    load = ex.run(["cat", "/proc/loadavg"], timeout=10)
    if not (cpus.ok and load.ok):
        return _unknown(ex, "load", cpus if not cpus.ok else load)
    per_cpu = parse_loadavg(load.stdout, int(cpus.stdout))
    return CheckResult(ex.name, "load/cpu", grade(per_cpu, warn,
crit), f"{per_cpu}", f"5-min, limits {warn}/{crit}")
def check_process(ex, name):
    r = ex.run(["pgrep", "-x", name], timeout=10)
    if r.returncode == 0:
        return CheckResult(ex.name, f"process {name}", OK,
f"{len(r.stdout.split())} running")
    if r.returncode == 1:                              # pgrep: 1 = no
process matched
        return CheckResult(ex.name, f"process {name}", CRIT, "0
running", "required process missing")
    return _unknown(ex, f"process {name}", r)
def check_reachable(ex):
    r = ex.run(["true"], timeout=15)
    if r.ok:
        return None
    return _unknown(ex, "reachable", r)
def check_command(ex, command):
    r = ex.run(["sh", "-c", 'command -v "$1"', "sh", command],
timeout=10)
    if r.returncode == 0:
        return CheckResult(ex.name, f"tool {command}", OK,
r.stdout.strip())
    if r.returncode in (-1, 255):                      # timeout or
SSH problem: we learned nothing
        return _unknown(ex, f"tool {command}", r)
    # POSIX only says "non-zero" for a missing command: dash returns
127, bash returns 1
    return CheckResult(ex.name, f"tool {command}", WARN, "missing",
"install it or adjust the test plan")
# file: src/healthcheck/runner.py
"""Run all checks on many hosts in parallel; print a table; write P5-
compatible JSON; Nagios exit code."""
import argparse
import json
import sys
import tomllib
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
from .checks import (SEVERITY, check_command, check_disk, check_load,
check_memory, check_process,
                     check_reachable)
from .executors import LocalExecutor, SshExecutor
def run_checks(ex, cfg):
    unreachable = check_reachable(ex)
    if unreachable:
        return [unreachable]                           # one clear
result instead of N identical failures
    limits = cfg.get("limits", {})
    results = [
        check_disk(ex, "/", *limits.get("disk", (80, 90))),
        check_memory(ex, *limits.get("memory", (85, 95))),
        check_load(ex, *limits.get("load", (1.5, 3.0))),
    ]
    results += [check_process(ex, p) for p in cfg.get("processes",
[])]
    results += [check_command(ex, c) for c in cfg.get("tools", [])]
    return results
def make_executor(host):
    if host.get("kind", "local") == "local":
        return LocalExecutor(host["name"])
    return SshExecutor(host["name"], host["address"], host["user"],
host.get("port", 22),
                       host.get("key_file"), host.get("known_hosts"))
def to_labreport(results):
    status_map = {"OK": "passed", "WARN": "failed", "CRIT": "failed",
"UNKNOWN": "error"}
    return {"results": [{"test": r.check, "device": r.host, "status":
status_map[r.status],
                         "message": f"{r.status} {r.value}
{r.message}".strip()} for r in results]}
def main(argv=None):
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="healthcheck")
    p.add_argument("config", help="TOML file with [[hosts]] and check
settings")
    p.add_argument("--json", help="write results in labreport (P5)
format")
    p.add_argument("--workers", type=int, default=8)
    args = p.parse_args(argv)
    with open(args.config, "rb") as f:
        cfg = tomllib.load(f)
    executors = [make_executor(h) for h in cfg["hosts"]]
    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=args.workers) as pool:
        per_host = list(pool.map(lambda ex: run_checks(ex, cfg),
executors))
    results = [r for host_results in per_host for r in host_results]
    for r in results:
        print(f"{r.host:<14} {r.check:<16} {r.status:<8} {r.value:<12}
{r.message}")
    worst = max(results, key=lambda r: SEVERITY[r.status]).status
    print(f"overall: {worst} ({len(results)} checks on
{len(executors)} hosts)")
    if args.json:
        with open(args.json, "w") as f:
            json.dump(to_labreport(results), f, indent=2)
    return SEVERITY[worst]
if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
# lab.toml
processes = ["sshd"]
tools = ["ipmitool", "python3", "nvme"]
[limits]
disk = [30, 90]          # deliberately low warning limit so the demo
shows a WARN
memory = [85, 95]
load = [1.5, 3.0]
[[hosts]]
name = "localhost"
kind = "local"
[[hosts]]
name = "lab-ssh"
kind = "ssh"
address = "127.0.0.1"
port = 2222
user = "tester"
key_file = "/root/.ssh/lab_ed25519"
known_hosts = "/root/.ssh/known_hosts_lab"
[[hosts]]
name = "rack12-dead"
kind = "ssh"
address = "127.0.0.1"
port = 2299               # nothing listens here: simulates an
unreachable host
user = "tester"
```

**P8.9 Code walkthrough**

- CommandResult.returncode uses conventions: -1 for our timeout, 127 for “not found” (the shell’s convention), 255 for SSH’s own errors. Checks use these to distinguish “the host said no” from “we could not ask”.

- stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL makes any command that unexpectedly asks for input (a password prompt, a confirmation) fail immediately instead of hanging until the timeout.

- SshExecutor passes the remote command as one string built with shlex.join, because OpenSSH hands it to the remote user’s shell. The test `test_ssh_executor_quotes_remote_arguments proves that "/tmp/report` dir; rm -rf /" arrives as a single quoted argument.

- The parsers take text and return numbers; they never run commands. Memory uses MemAvailable (what applications can still get, including reclaimable cache) rather than MemFree, which is misleadingly low on any busy Linux host.

- check_process relies on pgrep’s exit codes: 0 found, 1 not found, anything else is an error.

- **A bug found while building:** the first version of check_command treated exit code 1 as “tool missing”. In the sample run, missing tools showed as UNKNOWN with “exit 127”, because sh on this system is dash, whose command -v returns 127 for an unknown command (bash returns 1; POSIX only requires non-zero). The fixed version treats any non-zero code except timeouts and SSH errors as “missing”, and a parametrized test now covers 0, 1, 127, 255 and -1.

- check_reachable runs true once per host. If that fails, the host gets a single UNKNOWN result with SSH’s message, instead of seven identical connection errors (the circuit-breaker idea from Chapter 34).

- ThreadPoolExecutor.map runs hosts in parallel; within a host, checks run in order so that the load average is not inflated by our own parallel commands.

- to_labreport maps OK→passed, WARN/CRIT→failed, UNKNOWN→error, so P5 shows unreachable hosts as infrastructure errors.

**P8.10 Sample run**

```code
$ PYTHONPATH=src python -m healthcheck.runner lab.toml --json
health.json; echo "exit=$?"
localhost      disk /           WARN     33%          limits 30/90%
localhost      memory           OK       7.1%         limits 85/95%
localhost      load/cpu         OK       0.07         5-min, limits
1.5/3.0
localhost      process sshd     OK       2 running
localhost      tool ipmitool    WARN     missing      install it or
adjust the test plan
localhost      tool python3     OK       /usr/bin/python3
localhost      tool nvme        WARN     missing      install it or
adjust the test plan
lab-ssh        disk /           WARN     33%          limits 30/90%
lab-ssh        memory           OK       6.9%         limits 85/95%
lab-ssh        load/cpu         OK       0.07         5-min, limits
1.5/3.0
lab-ssh        process sshd     OK       8 running
lab-ssh        tool ipmitool    WARN     missing      install it or
adjust the test plan
lab-ssh        tool python3     OK       /usr/bin/python3
lab-ssh        tool nvme        WARN     missing      install it or
adjust the test plan
rack12-dead    reachable        UNKNOWN  -            ssh: connect to
host 127.0.0.1 port 2299: Connection refused
overall: UNKNOWN (15 checks on 3 hosts)
exit=3
```

localhost and lab-ssh are the same machine reached two ways, which is why their values are nearly identical (memory moves slightly between the two runs, and the SSH session itself adds sshd processes). The WARN on disk comes from the deliberately low 30% limit in lab.toml; ipmitool and nvme are not installed on this machine. The overall status is UNKNOWN because one host is unreachable, and the exit code is 3. The JSON goes straight into P5:

```code
$ testreport health.json --formats csv --out reports; cat
reports/health.csv
health: INFRA ERRORS - 15 tests, pass rate 53.3% ({'error': 1,
'failed': 6, 'passed': 8})
  ERROR  rack12-dead reachable: UNKNOWN - ssh: connect to host
127.0.0.1 port 2299: Connection refused
  FAILED lab-ssh disk /: WARN 33% limits 30/90%
  FAILED lab-ssh tool ipmitool: WARN missing install it or adjust the
test plan
  FAILED lab-ssh tool nvme: WARN missing install it or adjust the test
plan
  FAILED localhost disk /: WARN 33% limits 30/90%
  FAILED localhost tool ipmitool: WARN missing install it or adjust
the test plan
  FAILED localhost tool nvme: WARN missing install it or adjust the
test plan
wrote reports/health.csv
device,passed,failed,error,skipped
lab-ssh,4,3,0,0
localhost,4,3,0,0
rack12-dead,0,0,1,0
```

**P8.11 Tests**

```code
# file: tests/test_healthcheck.py
import subprocess
from unittest.mock import patch
import pytest
from healthcheck.checks import (CRIT, OK, UNKNOWN, WARN,
check_command, check_disk, check_load,
                                check_memory, check_process, grade,
parse_df, parse_meminfo)
from healthcheck.executors import CommandResult, LocalExecutor,
SshExecutor
from healthcheck.runner import run_checks, to_labreport
MEMINFO = "MemTotal:       8000000 kB\nMemFree:         500000 kB\
nMemAvailable:    2000000 kB\n"
class FakeExecutor:
    """Returns canned results keyed by the command's first word
(dependency injection, Chapter 26)."""
    def __init__(self, name="fake", outputs=None):
        self.name, self.outputs, self.calls = name, outputs or {}, []
    def run(self, argv, timeout=30.0):
        self.calls.append(argv)
        code, out, err = self.outputs.get(argv[0], (0, "", ""))
        return CommandResult(" ".join(argv), code, out, err, 0.0)
@pytest.mark.parametrize("value, expected", [(79, OK), (80, WARN),
(89.9, WARN), (90, CRIT)])
def test_grade_boundaries(value, expected):
    assert grade(value, 80, 90) == expected
def test_parsers():
    assert parse_df("Filesystem 1024-blocks Used Available Capacity
Mounted on\n/dev/sda1 100 91 9 91% /\n") == 91
    assert parse_meminfo(MEMINFO) == 75.0
def test_checks_with_fake_executor():
    ex = FakeExecutor(outputs={
        "df": (0, "h\n/dev/sda1 100 95 5 95% /\n", ""),
        "cat": (0, MEMINFO, ""),
        "nproc": (0, "4\n", ""),
        "pgrep": (1, "", ""),
    })
    assert check_disk(ex).status == CRIT
    assert check_memory(ex).status == OK
    ex.outputs["cat"] = (0, "3.10 6.20 5.00 1/200 999\n", "")
    load = check_load(ex)
    assert (load.status, load.value) == ("WARN", "1.55")
    proc = check_process(ex, "phosphor-fan")
    assert (proc.status, proc.message) == (CRIT, "required process
missing")
@pytest.mark.parametrize("code, status", [(0, OK), (1, WARN), (127,
WARN), (255, UNKNOWN), (-1, UNKNOWN)])
def test_tool_check_exit_codes(code, status):
    ex = FakeExecutor(outputs={"sh": (code, "/usr/bin/x\n" if code ==
0 else "", "ssh: error" if code == 255 else "")})
    assert check_command(ex, "x").status == status
def test_unreachable_host_gives_one_result():
    ex = FakeExecutor(name="dead", outputs={"true": (255, "", "ssh:
connect to host x port 22: No route to host")})
    results = run_checks(ex, {"processes": ["sshd"], "tools":
["ipmitool"]})
    assert [(r.check, r.status) for r in results] == [("reachable",
UNKNOWN)]
    assert ex.calls == [["true"]]
def test_ssh_executor_quotes_remote_arguments():
    ex = SshExecutor("h", "10.0.0.5", "tester", port=2222)
    with patch("healthcheck.executors.ssh.subprocess.run") as run:
        run.return_value = subprocess.CompletedProcess([], 0, "", "")
        ex.run(["ls", "/tmp/report dir; rm -rf /"])
    argv = run.call_args.args[0]
    assert argv[-1] == "ls '/tmp/report dir; rm -rf /'"
    assert argv[:3] == ["ssh", "-p", "2222"] and "BatchMode=yes" in
argv
def test_local_executor_timeout_and_missing_command():
    ex = LocalExecutor()
    assert ex.run(["sleep", "5"], timeout=0.2).returncode == -1
    missing = ex.run(["no-such-tool-xyz"])
    assert (missing.returncode, missing.stderr) == (127, "command not
found: no-such-tool-xyz")
def test_labreport_mapping():
    from healthcheck.checks import CheckResult
    data = to_labreport([CheckResult("h", "disk /", WARN, "85%",
"limits 80/90%"),
                         CheckResult("h", "reachable", UNKNOWN, "-",
"refused")])
    assert [r["status"] for r in data["results"]] == ["failed",
"error"]
$ python -m pytest -q
...............
[100%]
15 passed in 0.24s
```

**P8.12 Error handling**

| Situation | Result |
| Command exceeds timeout | UNKNOWN, “timed out after N s” (process killed by subprocess.run) |
| Command not installed locally | Local executor returns 127 with “command not found” |
| SSH connection refused, auth failure, host | Host reported once as UNKNOWN with SSH’s |
| key mismatch | message |
| Required process missing | CRIT |
| Required tool missing | WARN |
| Unexpected output format | Parsing error: extension 4 turns it into UNKNOWN instead of a crash |

**P8.13 Logging and reporting** The table is for people, the exit code for monitoring and CI, the JSON for P5 reports and history. For daily use, add per-host log files with every command, its exit code and duration (never secrets), so a WARN can be investigated later.

**P8.14 How to run**

```code
$ cd p8
$ PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m healthcheck.runner lab.toml --json
health.json
$ PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m pytest -q
```

For real lab hosts, set up key-based SSH access for a dedicated account and a known-hosts file (Chapter 28), then list the hosts in the TOML file. On Windows, run the tool from WSL or a Linux agent; the checks assume Linux hosts.

**P8.15 Extensions**

1. Add checks: NTP sync (timedatectl show -p NTPSynchronized), failed systemd units, kernel errors since boot (journalctl -k -p err -b), NIC link state.

2. Add per-check timeouts and retries for flaky networks.

3. Add a Paramiko executor (Chapter 28) that reuses one connection for all checks on a host, and compare run times.

4. Catch parsing errors in each check and report UNKNOWN with the raw output attached.

5. Add --only disk,memory and --hosts rack12* filters.

6. Export metrics in Prometheus text format for long-term trends (Chapter 30).

**P8.16 Interview questions**

1. **Why an executor interface?** Checks stay the same for local, SSH and fake targets; testing needs no real hosts.

2. **How do you tell “check failed” from “could not check”?** Distinct statuses (CRIT/WARN vs UNKNOWN) based on exit codes 255/-1/127.

3. **Why quote remote commands even though subprocess uses a list?** SSH passes the remote command to a shell on the other side.

4. **Why MemAvailable instead of MemFree?** Linux uses free memory for cache; MemAvailable estimates what applications can actually use.

5. **What are Nagios exit codes?** 0 OK, 1 WARNING, 2 CRITICAL, 3 UNKNOWN; widely understood by monitoring and CI tools.

**P8.17 Portfolio description** “P8 healthcheck (learning project): parallel Linux health checker with pluggable local and SSH executors, per-command timeouts, safe remote quoting, OK/WARN/CRIT/UNKNOWN grading, single-result handling of unreachable hosts, Nagios-style exit codes and JSON output for reporting; 15 tests using an injected fake executor.”

lessons.title: UART / Serial Automation Simulator
lessons.body:
**Portfolio note:** a learning project. The “device” is a simulator on a Linux pseudo-terminal; boot messages and command outputs are invented to resemble an OpenBMC console.

**P9.1 Overview** uartsim provides three things: a **virtual serial device** on a Linux pty that boots like a BMC and can inject faults (kernel panic, hang, garbage output from a wrong baud rate, slow boot); a

**pattern-driven console** on top of pySerial with timestamped capture files; and a **boot checker** that matches the boot log against ordered milestones with time limits and produces a report. A SerialExecutor runs shell commands over the console with exit codes, compatible with P8’s executor interface, so P8’s checks could run over a serial line. Label: **Advanced**. Do it after Chapter 33. Uses pySerial, ptys, threads, regular expressions, timeouts and simulators. Builds on P8’s executor interface.

**P9.2 Learning objectives**

1. Build a realistic serial-device simulator for tests that need no hardware.

2. Automate a console with expect/send, failure patterns and timeouts.

3. Check a boot sequence against milestones with per-step limits.

4. Get exit codes from a console that has no status channel.

5. Diagnose typical console problems: lost early output, wrong baud rate, hangs.

**P9.3 Real-world relevance** Boot validation, power-cycle campaigns and firmware-update tests all depend on the serial console: it is the only witness of bootloader and early-kernel problems. A simulator lets you develop and test this automation on a laptop and in CI, then switch the port name to /dev/ttyUSB0 or a console server (socket://consoles:7004) for the real board.

**P9.4 Requirements**

1. Virtual device: pty-based, boots with timed lines, accepts root/simulated, answers known commands, returns -sh: X: not found otherwise, supports an exit-code marker.

2. Faults: panic (kernel panic line, then nothing), hang (stops after init), garbage (unreadable bytes), slow (10 times slower).

3. Console: expect(pattern, timeout) returning text and elapsed time; failure patterns checked while waiting; timeout errors include the last output; every line captured with a timestamp.

4. Boot checker: milestones bootloader → kernel → init → BMC ready → login prompt with time limits; verdict, times and failure reason; hint when output looks like a baud-rate problem.

5. SerialExecutor.run(argv) returns CommandResult with exit code via a marker.

6. CLI python -m uartsim SCENARIO... prints a report per scenario; exit 1 if any fails.

**P9.5 Design**

```code
VirtualSerialDevice (thread writes to pty master)  <── pty ──>
SerialConsole (pySerial on pty slave)
        Scenario: fault, speed, responses
expect / send / login / run (+ capture file)
│
                                       check_boot(milestones)
────────────┤
                                       SerialExecutor (P8 interface)
─────┘
```

**P9.6 Folder structure**

```code
p9/
├── pyproject.toml
├── src/uartsim/
│   ├── __init__.py
│   ├── __main__.py      # scenario runner
│   ├── device.py        # VirtualSerialDevice, Scenario
│   ├── console.py       # SerialConsole
│   ├── bootcheck.py     # milestones, BootReport, baud heuristic
│   └── executor.py      # SerialExecutor
└── tests/test_uartsim.py
```

**P9.7 Step-by-step build**

1. Create a pty pair, put the slave in raw mode, and write lines to the master from a thread; open the slave with pySerial and read them.

2. Add login handling and command responses with terminal-style echo (and no echo for passwords).

3. Add fault injection in the boot sequence.

4. Write SerialConsole.expect with failure patterns, deadlines and capture.

5. Write check_boot with milestones and the baud-rate heuristic.

6. Add the exit-code marker to run() and the SerialExecutor.

7. Write the scenario CLI and tests for every fault.

**P9.8 Complete code**

```code
# file: src/uartsim/device.py
"""A virtual serial device on a Linux pty, driven by a scenario.
Simulation only."""
import os
import threading
import time
import tty
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
NORMAL_BOOT = [
    (0.00, "U-Boot 2019.04-sim (Oct 10 2026)"),
    (0.02, "DRAM:  512 MiB"),
    (0.03, "Hit any key to stop autoboot:  0"),
    (0.05, "Starting kernel ..."),
    (0.10, "[    0.000000] Booting Linux on physical CPU 0x0"),
    (0.15, "[    1.802011] mmcblk0: p1 p2 p3"),
    (0.20, "[    3.114501] systemd[1]: Detected architecture arm."),
    (0.30, "[    9.871002] phosphor-state-manager: BMC state Ready"),
    (0.32, ""),
    (0.33, "Phosphor OpenBMC (simulated) sim-bmc ttyS4"),
]
RESPONSES = {
    "uname -r": "6.6.30-sim",
    "cat /etc/os-release": 'ID=openbmc-phosphor\nVERSION_ID=2.14.3-
sim\nOPENBMC_TARGET_MACHINE="sim-board-a"',
    "fw_printenv bootcount": "bootcount=7",
    "cat /sys/class/hwmon/hwmon0/temp1_input": "45250",
}
@dataclass
class Scenario:
    """What the virtual device does. fault: None, 'panic', 'hang',
'garbage' or 'slow'."""
    fault: str | None = None
    speed: float = 1.0                     # >1 makes the boot faster
(time scale)
    password: str = "simulated"
    responses: dict = field(default_factory=lambda: dict(RESPONSES))
class VirtualSerialDevice:
    def __init__(self, scenario: Scenario | None = None):
        self.scenario = scenario or Scenario()
        self.master, slave = os.openpty()
        tty.setraw(slave)
        self.port = os.ttyname(slave)
        self._slave = slave
        self._stop = threading.Event()
        self._thread = threading.Thread(target=self._run, daemon=True)
    def __enter__(self):
        return self
    def power_on(self):
        """Start the boot sequence. Attach the console first, as on
real hardware."""
        self._thread.start()
    def __exit__(self, *exc):
        self._stop.set()
        os.close(self.master)
        os.close(self._slave)
    def _w(self, text):
        try:
            os.write(self.master, text.encode("utf-8",
errors="replace"))
        except OSError:
            self._stop.set()
    def _readline(self, echo=True):
        buf = b""
        while not self._stop.is_set():
            try:
                ch = os.read(self.master, 1)
            except OSError:
                return ""
            if ch in (b"\r", b"\n"):
                if buf:
                    self._w("\r\n")
                    return buf.decode(errors="replace")
                continue
            buf += ch
            if echo:
                self._w(ch.decode(errors="replace"))
        return ""
    def _boot(self):
        sc, start = self.scenario, time.monotonic()
        boot = list(NORMAL_BOOT)
        if sc.fault == "slow":
            boot = [(t * 10, line) for t, line in boot]
        for at, line in boot:
            delay = at / sc.speed - (time.monotonic() - start)
            if delay > 0:
                time.sleep(delay)
            if self._stop.is_set():
                return False
            if sc.fault == "garbage":                       # what a
wrong baud rate looks like
                line = "".join(chr(0x80 + (ord(c) * 7) % 0x7F) for c
in line)
            self._w(line + "\r\n")
            if sc.fault == "panic" and "mmcblk0" in line:
                self._w("[    2.004120] Kernel panic - not syncing:
VFS: Unable to mount root fs\r\n")
                return False
            if sc.fault == "hang" and "systemd" in line:
                return False                                 #
silence: nothing more is printed
        return sc.fault != "garbage"
    def _run(self):
        if not self._boot():
            return
        while not self._stop.is_set():
            self._w("sim-bmc login: ")
            user = self._readline()
            self._w("Password: ")
            password = self._readline(echo=False)
            if user == "root" and password == self.scenario.password:
                break
            time.sleep(0.05)
            self._w("\r\nLogin incorrect\r\n")
        while not self._stop.is_set():
            self._w("root@sim-bmc:~# ")
            command = self._readline().strip()
            if not command:
                continue
            marker = '; echo "__RC__=$?"'
            want_rc = command.endswith(marker)
            base = command[: -len(marker)].strip() if want_rc else
command
            known = base in self.scenario.responses
            out = self.scenario.responses[base] if known else f"-sh:
{base.split()[0]}: not found"
            if want_rc:
                out += f"\n__RC__={0 if known else 127}"
            self._w(out.replace("\n", "\r\n") + "\r\n")
# file: src/uartsim/console.py
"""Pattern-driven console on top of pySerial, with a timestamped
capture file."""
import re
import time
import serial
class ConsoleTimeout(TimeoutError):
    pass
class ConsoleFailure(RuntimeError):
    pass
class SerialConsole:
    PROMPT = r"[#$] $"
    def __init__(self, port, baudrate=115200, capture_path=None,
fail_patterns=(), clock=time.monotonic):
        self.ser = serial.serial_for_url(port, baudrate=baudrate,
timeout=0.05)
        self.buffer, self.clock = "", clock
        self.started = clock()
        self.fail_patterns = [re.compile(p) for p in fail_patterns]
        self.capture = open(capture_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") if
capture_path else None
    def _read(self):
        data = self.ser.read(4096).decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
        if data:
            self.buffer += data
            if self.capture:
                t = self.clock() - self.started
                for line in data.replace("\r", "").split("\n"):
                    if line.strip():
                        self.capture.write(f"[{t:8.3f}] {line}\n")
                self.capture.flush()
        return data
    def expect(self, pattern, timeout):
        """Wait for regex; return (text_before, elapsed_s). Raise on
failure patterns or timeout."""
        regex, start = re.compile(pattern), self.clock()
        deadline = start + timeout
        while True:
            for bad in self.fail_patterns:
                m = bad.search(self.buffer)
                if m:
                    line = self.buffer[m.start():].split("\n")
[0].strip()
                    raise ConsoleFailure(f"failure pattern seen:
{line!r}")
            m = regex.search(self.buffer)
            if m:
                before, self.buffer = self.buffer[:m.start()],
self.buffer[m.end():]
                return before, self.clock() - start
            if self.clock() >= deadline:
                tail = self.buffer[-60:].replace("\r", "").strip()
                raise ConsoleTimeout(f"no {pattern!r} within {timeout}
s; last output: {tail!r}")
            self._read()
    def send(self, text):
        self.ser.write((text + "\r").encode())
    def login(self, user, password, timeout=30, wait_for_prompt=True):
        if wait_for_prompt:                               # False if a
boot check already consumed it
            self.expect(r"login: $", timeout)
        self.send(user)
        self.expect(r"Password: $", 5)
        self.send(password)
        self.expect(self.PROMPT, 5)
    def run(self, command, timeout=10):
        """Run a shell command; return (output, exit_code) using an
exit-code marker."""
        self.buffer = ""
        self.send(f'{command}; echo "__RC__=$?"')
        before, _ = self.expect(self.PROMPT, timeout)
        lines = before.replace("\r", "").split("\n")[1:-1]       #
drop the echo and the prompt prefix
        if not lines or not lines[-1].startswith("__RC__="):
            raise ConsoleFailure(f"no exit-code marker after {command!
r}")
        return "\n".join(lines[:-1]), int(lines[-1].split("=", 1)[1])
    def close(self):
        self.ser.close()
        if self.capture:
            self.capture.close()
# file: src/uartsim/bootcheck.py
"""Match a boot log against ordered milestones with per-step time
limits."""
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from .console import ConsoleFailure, ConsoleTimeout
MILESTONES = [
    ("bootloader", r"U-Boot \S+", 5.0),
    ("kernel start", r"Starting kernel", 5.0),
    ("init", r"systemd\[1\]", 10.0),
    ("bmc ready", r"BMC state Ready", 15.0),
    ("login prompt", r"login: $", 10.0),
]
FAIL_PATTERNS = [r"Kernel panic[^\r\n]*", r"Unable to mount root",
r"watchdog: .*LOCKUP"]
def looks_like_wrong_baud(text, threshold=0.3):
    """Garbage characters (non-ASCII or control) dominate when the
baud rate is wrong."""
    chars = [c for c in text if c not in "\r\n\t "]
    if len(chars) < 20:
        return False
    bad = sum(1 for c in chars if ord(c) > 126 or ord(c) < 32)
    return bad / len(chars) > threshold
@dataclass
class BootReport:
    verdict: str = "PASS"
    reached: list = field(default_factory=list)      # (milestone,
seconds since start)
    failure: str = ""
    def lines(self):
        out = [f"  {name:<13} {t:6.2f} s" for name, t in self.reached]
        if self.failure:
            out.append(f"  FAILURE: {self.failure}")
        return out
def check_boot(console, milestones=MILESTONES, scale=1.0):
    """scale multiplies every time limit (use < 1 for a fast
simulator)."""
    report, elapsed = BootReport(), 0.0
    for name, pattern, limit in milestones:
        try:
            _, took = console.expect(pattern, limit * scale)
        except ConsoleFailure as e:
            report.verdict, report.failure = "FAIL", f"{e} (after
{report.reached[-1][0] if report.reached else 'start'})"
            return report
        except ConsoleTimeout as e:
            report.verdict, report.failure = "FAIL", f"{name}: {e}"
            if looks_like_wrong_baud(console.buffer):
                report.failure += " -- output is mostly unreadable:
check baud rate and serial settings"
            return report
        elapsed += took
        report.reached.append((name, round(elapsed, 2)))
    return report
# file: src/uartsim/executor.py
"""Executor over a serial console, compatible with P8's executor
interface."""
import shlex
import time
from dataclasses import dataclass
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class CommandResult:              # same fields as P8's CommandResult
    command: str
    returncode: int
    stdout: str
    stderr: str
    duration_s: float
    @property
    def ok(self):
        return self.returncode == 0
class SerialExecutor:
    """Runs commands on a logged-in console. The console has no stderr
channel: output is merged."""
    def __init__(self, name, console):
        self.name, self.console = name, console
    def run(self, argv, timeout=10.0):
        command = shlex.join(argv)
        start = time.monotonic()
        try:
            out, code = self.console.run(command, timeout)
            err = ""
        except TimeoutError as e:
            out, code, err = "", -1, str(e)
        return CommandResult(command, code, out, err,
round(time.monotonic() - start, 3))
# file: src/uartsim/__main__.py
"""python -m uartsim [normal|panic|hang|garbage|slow ...]: boot each
scenario and report."""
import sys
from .bootcheck import FAIL_PATTERNS, check_boot
from .console import SerialConsole
from .device import Scenario, VirtualSerialDevice
from .executor import SerialExecutor
def run_scenario(fault):
    scenario = Scenario(fault=None if fault == "normal" else fault,
speed=1.0)
    with VirtualSerialDevice(scenario) as dev:
        con = SerialConsole(dev.port,
capture_path=f"uart_{fault}.log", fail_patterns=FAIL_PATTERNS)
        dev.power_on()                                   # console
first, then power: no lost output
        try:
            report = check_boot(con, scale=0.1)          # simulator
boots ~30x faster than a real BMC
            print(f"[{fault}] boot {report.verdict}")
            print("\n".join(report.lines()))
            if report.verdict == "PASS":
                con.login("root", "simulated", wait_for_prompt=False)
                ex = SerialExecutor("sim-bmc", con)
                for argv in (["cat", "/etc/os-release"], ["cat",
"/sys/class/hwmon/hwmon0/temp1_input"],
                             ["fwupdate", "--status"]):
                    r = ex.run(argv)
                    first = r.stdout.splitlines()[0] if r.stdout else
""
                    print(f"  $ {r.command} -> rc={r.returncode}
{first!r}")
            return report.verdict == "PASS"
        finally:
            con.close()
def main(argv=None):
    faults = (argv if argv is not None else sys.argv[1:]) or
["normal"]
    results = [run_scenario(f) for f in faults]
    return 0 if all(results) else 1
sys.exit(main())
```

**P9.9 Code walkthrough**

- **pty pair:** os.openpty() returns a master and a slave file descriptor. The simulator writes to the master; anything reading the slave (pySerial here) sees it exactly like data from a USB serial adapter. tty.setraw(slave) disables the kernel’s line editing and echo, so the simulator controls echo itself, like a real device.

- **Lost early output (a bug found while building):** the first version started the device thread as soon as it was created, and every scenario failed with “no ‘U-Boot’ within 0.5 s” although the capture showed the rest of the boot. pySerial discards pending input when it opens a port on Linux, and the first lines were written before the console opened. Real benches have the same problem: if the script attaches to the console after power-on, the bootloader output is lost. The fix models the right procedure: power_on() is separate and is called **after** the console is open.

- **Second bug found:** after the boot check passed, login() timed out waiting for login: because the boot checker had already consumed the prompt from the buffer. login(..., wait_for_prompt=False) handles that; consumed text is gone, which is why expect returns what was before the match.

- serial.serial_for_url(port) accepts both device paths and URLs such as socket://host:port (console servers) or rfc2217://host:port, so the same code works with remote consoles.

- expect checks failure patterns first, on every iteration, so a kernel panic fails immediately rather than after the milestone timeout.

- Timeout errors include the last 60 characters received; for a hang, that shows where the boot stopped.

- looks_like_wrong_baud counts non-printable and non-ASCII characters; more than 30% suggests a baud-rate or serial-settings mismatch, the most common cause of “garbage” on a new bench.

- check_boot(scale=0.1) scales every limit because the simulator boots in about 0.35 s instead of tens of seconds; on hardware use scale=1.0 and limits from the product’s boot-time requirement.

- run() appends ; echo "__RC__=$?" and parses the marker: the console has no exit-status channel and no separate stderr, so SerialExecutor reports merged output and an empty stderr.

**P9.10 Sample run**

The capture file of the normal boot (first lines), with seconds since the console was opened:

```code
$ head -6 uart_normal.log

They have a resolution of about 50 ms: ser.read(4096) with timeout=0.05 returns after 50 ms when fewer than 4096 bytes arrive, so lines printed between 0.00 and 0.05 s are all stamped at about 0.05 s. For millisecond boot-time measurements, use a shorter read timeout or `ser.in_waiting.`

**P9.11 Tests**

```code
# file: tests/test_uartsim.py

    """Factory: start a virtual device with a fault, attach a console,
power on."""
    opened = []

        dev = VirtualSerialDevice(Scenario(fault=fault)).__enter__()
        con = SerialConsole(dev.port, capture_path=capture,
fail_patterns=FAIL_PATTERNS)
        dev.power_on()
        opened.append((dev, con))
        return con
    yield _boot
    for dev, con in opened:
        con.close()
        dev.__exit__(None, None, None)
def test_normal_boot_reaches_all_milestones_in_order(boot):
    report = check_boot(boot(), scale=0.1)
    assert report.verdict == "PASS"
    names = [n for n, _ in report.reached]
    assert names == ["bootloader", "kernel start", "init", "bmc
ready", "login prompt"]
    times = [t for _, t in report.reached]
    assert times == sorted(times)
@pytest.mark.parametrize("fault, expected", [
    ("panic", "Kernel panic"),
    ("hang", "bmc ready: no 'BMC state Ready'"),
    ("slow", "init: no"),
    ("garbage", "check baud rate"),
])
def test_faults_are_reported(boot, fault, expected):
    report = check_boot(boot(fault), scale=0.1)
    assert report.verdict == "FAIL" and expected in report.failure
def test_commands_and_exit_codes(boot):
    con = boot()
    assert check_boot(con, scale=0.1).verdict == "PASS"
    con.login("root", "simulated", wait_for_prompt=False)
    ex = SerialExecutor("sim", con)
    r = ex.run(["fw_printenv", "bootcount"])
    assert (r.returncode, r.stdout) == (0, "bootcount=7")
    assert ex.run(["reboot-now"]).returncode == 127
def test_wrong_password_then_right(boot):
    con = boot()
    check_boot(con, scale=0.1)
    con.send("root")
    con.expect(r"Password: $", 2)
    con.send("wrong")
    con.expect("Login incorrect", 2)
    con.login("root", "simulated")
    assert con.run("uname -r") == ("6.6.30-sim", 0)
def test_timeout_message_contains_last_output(boot):
    con = boot("hang")
    with pytest.raises(ConsoleTimeout, match="last
output: .*architecture arm"):
        con.expect("BMC state Ready", 0.6)
def test_capture_file_has_timestamps(boot, tmp_path):
    path = tmp_path / "uart.log"
    con = boot(capture=str(path))
    check_boot(con, scale=0.1)
    con.close()
    lines = path.read_text().splitlines()
    assert lines[0].endswith("U-Boot 2019.04-sim (Oct 10 2026)") and
lines[0].startswith("[")
def test_baud_heuristic():
    assert looks_like_wrong_baud("\x8f\xa4\xe1" * 20)
    assert not looks_like_wrong_baud("Starting kernel ...
[    0.000000] Booting Linux")
$ python -m pytest -q
..........
[100%]
10 passed in 6.46s
```

**P9.12 Error handling**

| Situation | Result |
| Kernel panic or other failure pattern | Immediate FAIL naming the last milestone reached |
| Hang | FAIL at the first missing milestone with the last output |
| Unreadable output | FAIL with a baud-rate hint |
| Command not found on the device | returncode 127, output contains the shell message |
| Missing exit-code marker (reboot, | ConsoleFailure, never a guessed exit code |

interleaved output)

| Command timeout | CommandResult with returncode -1 |

**P9.13 Logging and reporting** Every received line goes to uart_<scenario>.log with a timestamp: archive it with each run (Chapter 30). The boot report lists milestone times, which become metrics for boot-time trends across firmware builds (P10, P12).

**P9.14 How to run**

```code
$ cd p9
$ python3 -m pip install pyserial pytest
$ PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m uartsim normal panic
$ PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m pytest -q
```

Linux or macOS only (ptys); on Windows use WSL, or a pair of virtual COM ports (com0com) with the same console code. On real hardware, replace dev.port with /dev/serial/by- `id/... or socket://console-server:7004 and use scale=1.0.`

**P9.15 Extensions**

1. Add a U-Boot interaction: send a key when “Hit any key to stop autoboot” appears and run printenv at the U-Boot prompt.

2. Add a fault that prints a panic only on every third boot, and a campaign loop (Chapter 33) that counts boot failures.

3. Implement rfc2217:// support in the tests with serial.rfc2217 server from pySerial’s examples.

4. Make milestones configurable from TOML per platform.

5. Record milestone times into P5’s JSON format and plot boot time per firmware build.

6. Use pexpect.fdpexpect instead of the hand-written expect and compare.

**P9.16 Interview questions**

1. **Why open the console before powering on?** Otherwise early boot output is lost; many tools also flush input on open.

2. **How do you get a command’s exit code over a serial console?** Append an echo of $? with a unique marker and parse it.

3. **How do you detect a wrong baud rate automatically?** High ratio of non-printable or non-ASCII characters in received data.

4. **Why check failure patterns while waiting?** To fail fast with the real cause instead of waiting for a timeout.

5. **How would you test console automation without hardware?** A pty-based simulator with fault injection, as here.

**P9.17 Portfolio description** “P9 uartsim (learning project): pty-based virtual serial device with injectable boot faults, a pySerial console library with failure patterns and timestamped capture, a milestone-based boot checker with baud-rate diagnosis, and a serial command executor with exit codes; 10 tests across normal and fault scenarios.”

lessons.title: Firmware-Version and Device-Health Validation Framework
lessons.body:
**Portfolio note:** a learning project. Devices are simulated: an in-memory DUT with injected faults, the mock BMC from P7 and the virtual serial console from P9. No real hardware or firmware was tested.

**P10.1 Overview** fwval validates that a device runs the **right firmware** and is **healthy**, and stays that way across **repeated reboots**. It checks a firmware manifest (exact or minimum versions per component), evaluates telemetry against limits using the median of several samples, and runs a reboot campaign that, after every power cycle, checks boot time, firmware versions, telemetry and new events, stopping early on a firmware change. Validations depend only on small **capability interfaces**; adapters provide them from a simulator, from Redfish (P7) or from the serial console (P9), and can be mixed on one bench. Label: **Advanced**. Do it after Chapters 33 and 34. Builds on P7 (Redfish client), P8 (executor idea) and P9 (serial executor).

**P10.2 Learning objectives**

1. Design validations against capability interfaces and compose devices from adapters.

2. Compare version strings correctly, including pre-releases.

3. Make telemetry checks robust: retries for transient read errors, medians against spikes.

4. Build a reboot campaign with per-cycle checks, early stop and guaranteed cleanup.

5. Reuse earlier projects as libraries in a monorepo.

**P10.3 Real-world relevance** “Is the fleet on the qualified firmware?” and “does the board survive 1,000 reboots without a version change, missing drive or overheating?” are standard release gates for BMC, BIOS and storage firmware. Real campaigns find failover to a backup image, slow boots, drives that sometimes disappear, and sensors that read wrong after a warm reset, exactly the faults simulated here.

**P10.4 Requirements**

1. Capabilities: FirmwareInfo.firmware_versions(), Telemetry.readings(), Power.power_cycle() (returns seconds to ready) and ensure_on(), `EventLog.new_events().`

2. Manifest rules per component: expected (exact) or min; unknown components reported; missing components fail.

3. Version comparison numeric per part, pre-releases before releases (2.14.3-rc1 < `2.14.3 < 2.14.10).`

4. Telemetry: N samples, median per sensor, limits [low, high], transient read errors retried, persistent failures reported as error.

5. Campaign: N cycles; per cycle boot time limit, versions unchanged from baseline, telemetry within limits, no new events; stop on version change; device powered on at the end in all cases.

6. Simulated DUT with seeded faults: sensor glitches, slow boot, hot cycle, dropped drive, firmware downgrade.

7. CLI from TOML configuration; output table, campaign summary and P5-compatible JSON; exit 1 on any problem.

**P10.5 Design**

```code
validations (check_manifest, check_telemetry, reboot_campaign)
        │ depend only on
        ▼
capabilities: FirmwareInfo | Telemetry | Power | EventLog
        ▲ implemented by
adapters: SimulatedDut (all) | RedfishTelemetry, RedfishPower (P7
client) | ConsoleFirmwareInfo (P9 executor)
        ▲ composed by
cli.build_dut(config)   or   Bench(fw=ConsoleFirmwareInfo(...),
tel=RedfishTelemetry(...))
```

**P10.6 Folder structure**

```code
projects/
├── p7/src/apitest/        # reused: Redfish client and mock BMC
├── p9/src/uartsim/        # reused: virtual serial device, console,
executor
└── p10/
    ├── pyproject.toml     # pytest pythonpath includes ../p7/src
and ../p9/src
    ├── configs/           # sim_good.toml, sim_faulty.toml
    ├── bench_demo.py      # composition of real-protocol adapters
(against simulators)
    ├── src/fwval/
    │   ├── capabilities.py
    │   ├── retry.py
    │   ├── validations.py
    │   ├── cli.py
    │   └── adapters/{simulated,redfish,console}.py
    └── tests/test_fwval.py
```

**P10.7 Step-by-step build**

1. Write the capability protocols.

2. Write the simulated DUT with seeded fault injection.

3. Write check_manifest with a correct version key; test ordering edge cases first.

4. Write the retry decorator and check_telemetry with medians.

5. Write reboot_campaign with baseline, per-cycle checks, early stop and finally:

```code
ensure_on().
```

6. Write the CLI and two configurations (good and faulty).

7. Write Redfish and console adapters on top of P7 and P9, and the bench composition demo.

8. Write tests, including cleanup after a crash.

**P10.8 Complete code**

```code
# file: src/fwval/capabilities.py
"""What a validation needs from a device, independent of how the
device is reached."""
from typing import Protocol
class FirmwareInfo(Protocol):
    def firmware_versions(self) -> dict[str, str]: ...      #
component -> version
class Telemetry(Protocol):
    def readings(self) -> dict[str, float]: ...             # sensor -
> value
class Power(Protocol):
    def power_cycle(self) -> float: ...                     # returns
seconds until the device is ready
    def ensure_on(self) -> None: ...
class EventLog(Protocol):
    def new_events(self) -> list[str]: ...                  # events
since the last call
# file: src/fwval/retry.py
import functools
import logging
import time
log = logging.getLogger("fwval.retry")
class TransientError(Exception):
    """A read failed in a way that may succeed if repeated (timeouts,
busy device)."""
def retry(attempts=3, delay_s=0.5, sleep=time.sleep):
    def deco(func):
        @functools.wraps(func)
        def wrapper(*args, **kwargs):
            for n in range(1, attempts + 1):
                try:
                    return func(*args, **kwargs)
                except TransientError as e:
                    if n == attempts:
                        raise
                    log.warning("%s: %s (attempt %d/%d)",
func.__name__, e, n, attempts)
                    sleep(delay_s)
        return wrapper
    return deco
# file: src/fwval/validations.py
"""Validations: firmware manifest, telemetry thresholds, reboot
campaign. Each returns Findings."""
import logging
import statistics
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from .retry import TransientError, retry
log = logging.getLogger("fwval")
@dataclass
class Finding:
    check: str
    status: str          # passed / failed / error
    message: str = ""
def _vkey(version):
    """Sort key for versions like '2.14.3' or '2.14.3-rc1'. A pre-
release sorts before its release,
    as in Semantic Versioning: 2.14.3-rc1 < 2.14.3 < 2.14.10. Missing
parts count as 0."""
    main, _, pre = version.partition("-")
    numbers = tuple(int(p) if p.isdigit() else 0 for p in
main.split("."))
    numbers += (0,) * (4 - len(numbers))
    return numbers, 0 if pre else 1, pre
def check_manifest(fw, manifest):
    """manifest: component -> {"expected": "x.y.z"} or {"min":
"x.y.z"}."""
    actual, findings = fw.firmware_versions(), []
    for comp, rule in sorted(manifest.items()):
        have = actual.get(comp)
        name = f"firmware {comp}"
        if have is None:
            findings.append(Finding(name, "failed", "component not
reported"))
        elif "expected" in rule and have != rule["expected"]:
            findings.append(Finding(name, "failed", f"{have} !=
expected {rule['expected']}"))
        elif "min" in rule and _vkey(have) < _vkey(rule["min"]):
            findings.append(Finding(name, "failed", f"{have} < minimum
{rule['min']}"))
        else:
            findings.append(Finding(name, "passed", have))
    for comp in sorted(set(actual) - set(manifest)):
        findings.append(Finding(f"firmware {comp}", "passed",
f"{actual[comp]} (not in manifest)"))
    return findings
def check_telemetry(tel, limits, samples=3, sleep=lambda s: None,
interval_s=1.0):
    """limits: sensor -> [low, high]. Uses the median of several
samples to ignore single spikes."""
    read = retry(attempts=3, delay_s=0.1, sleep=sleep)(tel.readings)
    collected = {}
    for i in range(samples):
        try:
            for name, value in read().items():
                collected.setdefault(name, []).append(value)
        except TransientError as e:
            return [Finding("telemetry", "error", f"sensor reads keep
failing: {e}")]
        if i < samples - 1:
            sleep(interval_s)
    findings = []
    for name, (low, high) in sorted(limits.items()):
        if name not in collected:
            findings.append(Finding(f"sensor {name}", "failed",
"missing"))
            continue
        value = statistics.median(collected[name])
        ok = low <= value <= high
        findings.append(Finding(f"sensor {name}", "passed" if ok else
"failed",
                                f"median {value:g} (limits {low:g}..
{high:g})"))
    return findings
@dataclass
class CampaignResult:
    cycles: int
    failures: list = field(default_factory=list)     # (cycle,
[problems])
    boot_times: list = field(default_factory=list)
    def summary(self):
        if not self.boot_times:
            return f"{self.cycles} cycles, no boots measured"
        bt = sorted(self.boot_times)
        return (f"{self.cycles} cycles, {len(self.failures)} with
problems; boot median "
                f"{statistics.median(bt):.1f} s, max {bt[-1]:.1f} s")
def reboot_campaign(dut, cycles, boot_limit_s, manifest, limits,
stop_on=("version",)):
    """Power-cycle `cycles` times; after each, check boot time,
versions, telemetry and new events.
    Always leaves the device powered on (safe cleanup), even if an
exception escapes."""
    result = CampaignResult(cycles=0)
    baseline = dut.firmware_versions()
    try:
        for n in range(1, cycles + 1):
            result.cycles = n
            problems = []
            boot_s = dut.power_cycle()
            result.boot_times.append(boot_s)
            if boot_s > boot_limit_s:
                problems.append(f"slow boot {boot_s} s >
{boot_limit_s} s")
            now = dut.firmware_versions()
            if now != baseline:
                changed = {k: f"{baseline.get(k)} -> {v}" for k, v in
now.items() if baseline.get(k) != v}
                problems.append(f"version changed {changed}")
            bad = [f"{f.check}: {f.message}" for f in
check_telemetry(dut, limits, samples=1) if f.status != "passed"]
            problems += [f"telemetry {m}" for m in bad]
            problems += [f"event: {e}" for e in dut.new_events()]
            if problems:
                result.failures.append((n, problems))
                log.warning("cycle %d: %s", n, "; ".join(problems))
                if any(word in p for p in problems for word in
stop_on):
                    log.error("stopping campaign at cycle %d (%s)", n,
", ".join(stop_on))
                    break
    finally:
        dut.ensure_on()
    return result
# file: src/fwval/adapters/simulated.py
"""A simulated DUT implementing every capability, with seeded fault
injection. Simulation only."""
import random
class SimulatedDut:
    def __init__(self, seed=1, versions=None, faults=None):
        self.rng = random.Random(seed)
        self.versions = versions or {"bmc": "2.14.3", "bios": "1.9.0",
"cpld": "0.7", "psu0": "3.2.1"}
        self.faults = faults or {}          # e.g. {"sensor_glitch":
0.2, "slow_boot_cycle": 3, "drop_drive_cycle": 4}
        self.cycle, self.powered, self._events = 0, True, []
    # FirmwareInfo
    def firmware_versions(self):
        return dict(self.versions)
    # Telemetry
    def readings(self):
        from ..retry import TransientError
        if self.rng.random() < self.faults.get("sensor_glitch", 0.0):
            raise TransientError("sensor read timed out")
        values = {"CPU0_Temp": 45 + self.rng.uniform(-2, 2),
"Inlet_Temp": 24 + self.rng.uniform(-1, 1),
                  "FAN2_RPM": 3200 + self.rng.uniform(-100, 100),
"P12V": 12.0 + self.rng.uniform(-0.15, 0.15)}
        if self.cycle and self.cycle == self.faults.get("hot_cycle"):
            values["CPU0_Temp"] = 97.0
        return {k: round(v, 2) for k, v in values.items()}
    # Power
    def power_cycle(self):
        self.powered = False
        self.cycle += 1
        boot_s = 41.0 + self.rng.gauss(0, 0.8)
        if self.cycle == self.faults.get("slow_boot_cycle"):
            boot_s = 95.0
        if self.cycle == self.faults.get("drop_drive_cycle"):
            self._events.append("Drive 3 not present after boot")
        if self.cycle == self.faults.get("downgrade_cycle"):
            self.versions["bmc"] = "2.13.0"             # e.g. a
failover to the backup image
            self._events.append("BMC booted from secondary image")
        self.powered = True
        return round(boot_s, 1)
    def ensure_on(self):
        self.powered = True
    # EventLog
    def new_events(self):
        events, self._events = self._events, []
        return events

"""Telemetry and power through Redfish, using P7's client
(apitest)."""
import time
from apitest import RedfishClient, RedfishError
from ..retry import TransientError
class RedfishTelemetry:
    def __init__(self, client: RedfishClient):
        self.client = client
    def readings(self):
        try:
            temps = self.client.temperatures()
        except RedfishError as e:
            if e.status in (502, 503, 504):
                raise TransientError(str(e)) from e
            raise
        return {f"{name}_Temp": t["ReadingCelsius"] for name, t in
temps.items()}
class RedfishPower:
    def __init__(self, client: RedfishClient, ready_timeout_s=300,
poll_s=1.0):
        self.client, self.ready_timeout_s, self.poll_s = client,
ready_timeout_s, poll_s
    def power_cycle(self):
        start = time.monotonic()
        self.client.reset("ForceOff")
        self.client.reset("On")
        while self.client.system()["PowerState"] != "On":
            if time.monotonic() - start > self.ready_timeout_s:
                raise TimeoutError("host did not power on")
            time.sleep(self.poll_s)
        return round(time.monotonic() - start, 1)
    def ensure_on(self):
        if self.client.system()["PowerState"] != "On":
            self.client.reset("On")
# file: src/fwval/adapters/console.py
"""Firmware version from the BMC console (os-release), using P9's
SerialExecutor."""
import re
from uartsim.executor import SerialExecutor
class ConsoleFirmwareInfo:
    def __init__(self, executor: SerialExecutor):
        self.ex = executor
    def firmware_versions(self):
        r = self.ex.run(["cat", "/etc/os-release"])
        if r.returncode != 0:
            raise RuntimeError(f"cannot read os-release:
rc={r.returncode}")
        m = re.search(r'^VERSION_ID="?([^"\n]+)"?$', r.stdout, re.M)
        return {"bmc": m.group(1)} if m else {}

"""python -m fwval.cli CONFIG.toml [--json OUT]"""
import argparse
import json
import logging
import sys
import tomllib
from .adapters.simulated import SimulatedDut
from .validations import check_manifest, check_telemetry,
reboot_campaign
def build_dut(cfg):
    kind = cfg["device"]["kind"]
    if kind == "simulated":
        return SimulatedDut(seed=cfg["device"].get("seed", 1),
faults=cfg["device"].get("faults", {}))
    raise SystemExit(f"device kind {kind!r} needs the bench wiring
shown in P10.10")
def main(argv=None):
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="fwval")
    p.add_argument("config")
    p.add_argument("--json")
    args = p.parse_args(argv)
    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.WARNING, format="%(levelname)s %
(name)s: %(message)s")
    with open(args.config, "rb") as f:
        cfg = tomllib.load(f)
    dut = build_dut(cfg)
    findings = check_manifest(dut, cfg["manifest"]) +
check_telemetry(dut, cfg["limits"])
    camp = cfg.get("campaign", {})
    result = reboot_campaign(dut, camp.get("cycles", 0),
camp.get("boot_limit_s", 120), cfg["manifest"], cfg["limits"])
    for f in findings:
        print(f"{f.status.upper():<7} {f.check:<22} {f.message}")
    print("campaign:", result.summary())
    for cycle, problems in result.failures:
        print(f"  cycle {cycle}: " + "; ".join(problems))
    records = [{"test": f.check, "device": cfg["name"], "status":
f.status, "message": f.message} for f in findings]
    records.append({"test": "reboot_campaign", "device": cfg["name"],
                    "status": "failed" if result.failures else
"passed", "message": result.summary()})
    if args.json:
        with open(args.json, "w") as fh:
            json.dump({"results": records}, fh, indent=2)
    return 1 if any(r["status"] != "passed" for r in records) else 0
if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

"""Compose a 'bench' from real-protocol adapters: Redfish telemetry
(P7 mock) + console firmware info (P9).
Both endpoints are simulators started here; on a lab bench they would
be a real BMC and a real console.
"""
from dataclasses import dataclass
from apitest import RedfishClient
from apitest.mock_bmc import start
from uartsim.bootcheck import FAIL_PATTERNS, check_boot
from uartsim.console import SerialConsole
from uartsim.device import Scenario, VirtualSerialDevice
from uartsim.executor import SerialExecutor
from fwval.adapters.console import ConsoleFirmwareInfo
from fwval.adapters.redfish import RedfishTelemetry
from fwval.validations import check_manifest, check_telemetry
@dataclass
class Bench:
    """A DUT assembled from capabilities supplied by different
adapters."""
    fw: ConsoleFirmwareInfo
    tel: RedfishTelemetry
    def firmware_versions(self):
        return self.fw.firmware_versions()
    def readings(self):
        return self.tel.readings()
server, state, url = start()
with VirtualSerialDevice(Scenario()) as dev, RedfishClient(url,
"admin", "simulated") as client:
    console = SerialConsole(dev.port, fail_patterns=FAIL_PATTERNS)
    dev.power_on()
    print("boot:", check_boot(console, scale=0.1).verdict)
    console.login("root", "simulated", wait_for_prompt=False)
    bench = Bench(ConsoleFirmwareInfo(SerialExecutor("sim-bmc",
console)), RedfishTelemetry(client))
    findings = check_manifest(bench, {"bmc": {"min": "2.14.0"}})
    findings += check_telemetry(bench, {"CPU0_Temp": [10, 85],
"Inlet_Temp": [10, 35]}, samples=2)
    state.temps["CPU0"] = 91.0                     # inject an
overheating CPU into the mock BMC
    findings += check_telemetry(bench, {"CPU0_Temp": [10, 85]},
samples=1)
    for f in findings:
        print(f"{f.status.upper():<7} {f.check:<18} {f.message}")
    console.close()
server.shutdown()
```

**P10.9 Code walkthrough**

- **Version comparison:** as strings, "1.10.0" < "1.9.0" is True, because comparison goes character by character. _vkey splits off a pre-release suffix, converts the numeric parts to integers, pads to four parts so 2.14 == 2.14.0, and puts pre-releases before the release. The first version of this function sorted 2.14.3-rc1 **after** 2.14.3, which would accept a release candidate where the release is required; the test test_version_ordering was corrected to follow Semantic Versioning, and the code with it. For Python packages use packaging.version.Version (PEP 440); for firmware, follow the vendor’s documented scheme.

- **Robust telemetry:** retry wraps readings() so that a single TransientError (sensor read timeout, Redfish 503) is retried; persistent failures become an error finding, which P5 reports as an infrastructure problem rather than a hot CPU. The median of several samples ignores a single spike, which a test demonstrates with readings 45, 99, 46.

- **Campaign:** the baseline versions are read once before cycling; every cycle compares against them. A version change stops the campaign by default (stop_on=("version",)) because results after an unexpected image switch no longer describe the firmware under test. finally: dut.ensure_on() runs even when an exception escapes, so the bench is never left powered off; `test_campaign_always_powers_on_even_on_crash proves it.`

- **Adapters:** RedfishTelemetry turns 502/503/504 into TransientError so the same retry logic applies; ConsoleFirmwareInfo reads VERSION_ID from /etc/os-release over the serial console; Bench composes them. The validations never import `requests or serial.`

- **Monorepo reuse:** P10 imports apitest (P7) and uartsim (P9) through PYTHONPATH (and pythonpath in pyproject.toml for pytest). In a real repository, make them installable packages and depend on them (Chapter 23).

**P10.10 Sample run** A healthy simulated DUT: firmware matches, sensors in range, 20 clean reboots. The sensor-glitch fault caused read timeouts that were retried (warnings) but no failures:

reboot_campaign
LIMITS = {"CPU0_Temp": [10, 85], "P12V": [11.4, 12.6]}
@pytest.mark.parametrize("a, b", [("1.9.0", "1.10.0"), ("2.14.3",

strings compare character by character

check_manifest(dut, {

1.10.0"),

reported")}

[100%]

**P10.12 Error handling**

| Situation | Result |
| Transient sensor read error | Retried (WARNING logged); succeeds or becomes an error finding |
| Component missing from device | failed finding |
| Version below minimum or not expected | failed with both versions |
| Slow boot, out-of-range sensor, new event | Cycle recorded with problems; campaign continues |
| Firmware version changes during campaign | Cycle recorded, campaign stops |
| Exception during campaign (PDU | Propagates after ensure_on() cleanup |

unreachable)

**P10.13 Logging and reporting** WARNING lines record every retry and every problem cycle as it happens (useful in a live Jenkins console); the final table and campaign summary are the report; --json produces P5 input. A real campaign should also save console captures and event logs per failed cycle (P9, Chapter 33).

**P10.14 How to run**

```code
$ cd projects/p10
$ export PYTHONPATH=src:../p7/src:../p9/src          # Windows:
$env:PYTHONPATH="src;..\p7\src;..\p9\src"
$ python3 -m fwval.cli configs/sim_good.toml
$ python3 -m fwval.cli configs/sim_faulty.toml --json faulty.json &&
testreport faulty.json
$ python3 bench_demo.py
$ python3 -m pytest -q
```

**P10.15 Extensions**

1. Add a PduPower adapter (Chapter 31 exercise) and an AC-cycle campaign mode.

2. Add a firmware-update step before the campaign with checksum verification and post-update version check (Chapter 33).

3. Save per-cycle evidence (console capture, events, readings) to a folder per failed cycle.

4. Add the rule-of-three statement to the campaign summary (Chapter 33).

5. Read the manifest from the release’s bill of materials file and compare all components.

6. Run campaigns on several simulated DUTs in parallel (this is P11).

**P10.16 Interview questions**

1. **How do you compare firmware versions?** Parse into numeric parts with a defined rule for suffixes; never compare strings; follow the vendor’s scheme or SemVer.

2. **How do you avoid false failures from noisy sensors?** Several samples, median, retry transient read errors, separate read errors from limit violations.

3. **Why stop a reboot campaign on a firmware change?** Later cycles test a different image; continuing produces misleading results.

4. **How do you guarantee the bench is left in a safe state?** Cleanup in finally (or fixture teardown), tested by simulating a crash.

5. **Why capability interfaces instead of one device class?** Different benches provide capabilities through different paths; validations stay unchanged.

**P10.17 Portfolio description** “P10 fwval (learning project): firmware and health validation framework with capability interfaces and interchangeable adapters (simulator, Redfish, serial console), SemVer-correct manifest checks, median-based telemetry limits with retries, and a reboot campaign with per-cycle checks, early stop on image change and guaranteed cleanup; 11 tests plus fault-injected simulated campaigns.”
