lessons.title: Headers, JSON bodies and query parameters
lessons.body:
- **json=obj** serialises obj to JSON and sets Content-Type: application/json. Use it for Redfish bodies.

- **data=...** sends the value as-is: a dict becomes form-encoded (a=1&b=2), which a Redfish service rejects as malformed JSON. Use data= only when you deliberately want raw bytes — for example to send malformed JSON in a negative test.

- **params={"$top": 10, "$skip": 20}** builds and encodes the query string.

- **headers={...}** on a request is merged with (and overrides) session headers.

```code
r = s.get(base + "/redfish/v1/Systems/system/LogServices/EventLog/Entries",
          params={"$top": 10}, timeout=TIMEOUT)
print(r.url)   # ...Entries?%24top=10   ('$' is percent-encoded; servers
decode it)
```

source.section: 5.4 Headers, JSON bodies and query parameters

lessons.title: Basic authentication and session-based authentication
lessons.body:
```code
# Basic: credentials on every request
r = s.get(url, auth=(username, password), timeout=TIMEOUT)
# Session: credentials once, token afterwards
r = s.post(base + "/redfish/v1/SessionService/Sessions",
           json={"UserName": username, "Password": password}, timeout=TIMEOUT)
if r.status_code not in (200, 201):
    raise RuntimeError(f"login failed: HTTP {r.status_code}")
s.headers["X-Auth-Token"] = r.headers["X-Auth-Token"]
session_uri = r.headers.get("Location") or r.json()["@odata.id"]
try:
    ...  # do work
finally:
    s.delete(base + session_uri, timeout=TIMEOUT)   # always log out
```

Credentials must come from the environment or a secret store, never from source code (Chapter 21).

lessons.title: TLS verification and certificate handling
lessons.body:
verify controls certificate checking:

| Value | Meaning | When |
| True (default) | Verify against the system/ | Public CAs or CAs installed |
| certifi CA bundle | system-wide |
| Verify against this bundle | Lab BMCs with internal CA | "/path/lab-ca.pem" or pinned cert |
| False | No verification (insecure) | Isolated lab only, with an explicit warning |

```code
s.verify = "/etc/lab/lab-ca.pem"            # applies to every request in the
session
```

You can also set REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE=/path/lab-ca.pem in the environment. With verify=False, urllib3 emits InsecureRequestWarning on every request. Do not silence the warning globally in shared code — it is doing its job.

To obtain a BMC’s current certificate for pinning (over a network you trust):

```code
$ openssl s_client -connect bmc.example.test:443 -servername bmc.example.test
</dev/null \
    | openssl x509 -outform PEM > bmc01.pem
```

Pinning a self-signed certificate only works if its Subject Alternative Name matches the host name you connect to. Many default BMC certificates use a fixed name; in that case install a proper lab-CA certificate instead.

lessons.title: Connection and read timeouts
lessons.body:
Always pass timeout. A single number sets both connect and read; a tuple (connect, read) sets them separately. There is no global default in requests — a forgotten timeout means “wait forever”.

```code
r = s.get(url, timeout=(3.05, 30))   # 3.05: slightly over a multiple of 3 s,
which is
                                     # the classic TCP SYN retransmission
interval
```

Exceptions:

| Exception | Parent | Meaning |
| requests.exceptions.ConnectTimeout | ConnectionError, | TCP/TLS not estab‐ |
| Timeout | lished in time Connected, response requests.exceptions.ReadTimeout Timeout too slow |
| requests.exceptions.SSLError | ConnectionError | Certificate or handshake failure |
| requests.exceptions.ConnectionError | RequestException | Refused, reset, DNS failure, … Raised by requests.exceptions.HTTPError RequestException |

```code
raise_for_status()
```

| requests.exceptions.JSONDecodeError | ValueError | r.json() on a non- JSON body |

Because SSLError and ConnectTimeout are subclasses of ConnectionError, catch the specific ones first if you want different messages (Project 1 does).

lessons.title: Error handling and response validation
Safe retry strategies
lessons.body:
```code
urllib3.util.retry.Retry plus requests.adapters.HTTPAdapter:
  from requests.adapters import HTTPAdapter
  from urllib3.util.retry import Retry
  retry = Retry(
      total=3,                                   # overall cap
      connect=3, read=3, status=3,               # per-category caps
      backoff_factor=0.5,                        # sleeps grow exponentially
  between attempts
      status_forcelist=(502, 503, 504),          # retry these statuses
      allowed_methods=frozenset({"GET", "HEAD", "OPTIONS"}),  # never POST/PATCH
      respect_retry_after_header=True,
      raise_on_status=False,                     # return the last response
  instead of raising
  )
  s.mount("https://", HTTPAdapter(max_retries=retry, pool_maxsize=4))
```

Behaviour worth knowing:

- **Connection errors** (refused, connect timeout) are retried for all methods, because the request never reached the server.

- **Read errors** and **status retries** apply only to allowed_methods.

- With backoff_factor=b, urllib3 sleeps roughly b × 2^(n−1) seconds before later retries (capped by Retry.DEFAULT_BACKOFF_MAX); exact timing details have varied slightly between urllib3 versions.

- In urllib3 1.x the parameter was called method_whitelist; it was renamed to allowed_methods and the old name removed in 2.0. Old blog posts still show it.

lessons.title: Reusable API client design
lessons.body:
Copy-pasted requests calls across tests lead to inconsistent timeouts, leaked sessions and unreadable failures. Put HTTP handling in one class:

| Responsibility | Where |
| Base URL, credentials, verify, timeouts | A config object (dataclass) loaded from env |
| Session creation, retries, pooling | Client constructor |
| Login/logout and token header | Client methods + context manager |
| Responsibility | Where |
| Status checking and error parsing | One central request() method |
| Typed exceptions | RedfishHTTPError, RedfishAuthError, |

```code
RedfishConnectionError
```

| Logging (redacted) | Inside request() |
| Domain helpers | service_root(), iter_members(), |

```code
wait_for_task()
```

Tests then read like specifications:

```code
def test_manager_reports_firmware_version(rf):
    for uri in rf.member_uris("/redfish/v1/Managers"):
        assert rf.get_json(uri).get("FirmwareVersion")
```

The full client is developed in Chapter 8.

lessons.title: Common mistakes
lessons.body:
- No timeout= argument.

- data=dict instead of json=dict.

- Assuming requests raises on 4xx/5xx.

- Creating a new requests.get() connection for every call instead of a `Session.`

- Global verify=False plus urllib3.disable_warnings().

- Retrying POST on read timeouts.

- Logging r.request.headers with Authorization or X-Auth-Token in it.

lessons.title: Exercises
lessons.body:
1. Write a function that logs in, yields a session, and always logs out, us‐ `ing contextlib.contextmanager.`

2. Configure a session that retries GET on 503 up to 5 times but never retries POST.

3. Modify the tour to send malformed JSON in a PATCH and print the MessageId.

**Solutions.**

1.

```code
from contextlib import contextmanager
import requests
@contextmanager
def redfish_session(base: str, user: str, password: str, verify=True):
    s = requests.Session()
    s.verify = verify
    r = s.post(f"{base}/redfish/v1/SessionService/Sessions",
               json={"UserName": user, "Password": password}, timeout=(5, 30))
    r.raise_for_status()
    s.headers["X-Auth-Token"] = r.headers["X-Auth-Token"]
    uri = r.headers.get("Location") or r.json()["@odata.id"]
    try:
        yield s
    finally:
        try:
            s.delete(base + uri, timeout=(5, 30))
        finally:
            s.close()
```

1. Retry(total=5, status=5, status_forcelist=(503,), `allowed_methods=frozenset({"GET"})) mounted with HTTPAdapter.`

2. s.patch(url, data='{"AssetTag": ', headers={"Content-Type": "application/ `json"}, timeout=TIMEOUT) then r.json()["error"]["@Message.ExtendedInfo"] [0]["MessageId"]; the mock answers Base.1.13.0.MalformedJSON.`

lessons.title: Summary
lessons.body:
- requests + Session + explicit timeout is the foundation.

- Use json= for JSON bodies, params= for query strings.

- requests does not raise on HTTP errors; check status yourself and parse the Redfish error body.

- Retry only idempotent operations, with backoff, via urllib3.Retry.

- Wrap everything in a reusable client class.

lessons.title: Reusable API clients
lessons.body:
Chapter 5 introduced the principle. The concrete structure used across this book:

```code
RedfishConfig  (dataclass, from env)        <- what to connect to
      │
RedfishClient                                <- how to talk
  ├─ request(method, path, expected=...)     <- single choke point: timeout,
  │                                             logging, error translation
  ├─ get / get_json / patch / post / delete
  ├─ login / logout / __enter__ / __exit__
  └─ iter_members / get_with_etag / wait_for_task
      │
pytest fixtures (rf, system_restored, ...)   <- lifecycle per test
      │
tests                                        <- intent only
```

The single request() choke point is the key design decision. Every cross-cutting behaviour — timeouts, logging, retries, error parsing — lives there once.

lessons.title: Test data management
lessons.body:
Keep test data out of test logic:

**Static data** (valid/invalid payloads, boundary values) in parametrize • lists or small JSON/YAML files next to the tests.

- **Environment data** (hosts, users, resource IDs) in configuration, not tests.

- **Generated data** (unique names) created per test — e.g. f"autotest- {uuid4().hex[:8]}" — so parallel runs do not collide.

- **Discovered data** (member IDs) read from the service at run time instead of hard coded: rf.member_uris("/redfish/v1/Systems")[0] works on OpenBMC (Systems/system) and on other vendors (Systems/1, Systems/ `System.Embedded.1).`

Mark data that is implementation-specific. If a boundary such as “AssetTag max 32 characters” comes from your product documentation rather than the DMTF schema, say so in the test.

lessons.title: Response schema validation
lessons.body:
A **JSON Schema** describes the expected structure of JSON: required properties, types, enumerations, patterns. Validating responses catches missing or mistyped properties early. The jsonschema library implements the standard.

```code
from jsonschema import Draft7Validator
schema = {
    "type": "object",
    "required": ["Id", "PowerState"],
    "properties": {
        "Id": {"type": "string"},
        "PowerState": {"enum": ["On", "Off", "PoweringOn", "PoweringOff", "Pau
sed"]},
    },
}
validator = Draft7Validator(schema)
errors = list(validator.iter_errors({"Id": 5, "PowerState": "Sideways"}))
for e in errors:
    print(list(e.path), e.message)
# ['Id'] 5 is not of type 'string'
# ['PowerState'] 'Sideways' is not one of ['On', 'Off', 'PoweringOn',
'PoweringOff', 'Paused']
```

Use iter_errors() rather than validate() so a failure reports all problems at once (Project 1’s validate_resource() does this).

**Official DMTF schemas vs local subsets.** DMTF publishes JSON Schemas for every Redfish resource in the schema bundle **DSP8010**. They use cross-file $ref references and versioned definitions, so validating against them requires a reference resolver. For conformance, use DMTF’s **Redfish-Service-Validator** tool, which does this properly. For functional tests, small hand-written schemas covering exactly the properties your tests rely on are simpler and give clearer failures. Project 1 uses that approach and says so in its code.

lessons.title: Authentication failure tests
lessons.body:
Cover at least:

| Case | Expected [Spec]/[Impl] |
| No credentials on protected resource | 401 |
| Wrong password | 401 on session create |
| Unknown user | 401 (must not reveal whether the user exists) |
| Token after logout | 401 |
| Garbage token | 401 |
| Expired session (after SessionTimeout) | 401 — slow test; run in extended suite |
| Insufficient privilege (ReadOnly PATCH) | 403 |
| Service root without credentials | 200 (spec requires unauthenticated access) |
| Account lockout after N failures | Implementation policy — test only on dedicated accounts, then unlock |

**Warning.** Lockout tests can lock out the shared automation account and break every other job. Use a dedicated throwaway account created and deleted by the test.

lessons.title: Invalid input and malformed JSON tests
lessons.body:
Project 1’s negative tests show the pattern: one invalid input per case, assert the status and the message ID, and verify no side effect.

```code
redfish_suite/tests/test_negative.py
 def test_unknown_resource_is_404_with_extended_info(rf):
     with pytest.raises(RedfishHTTPError) as excinfo:
         rf.get_json("/redfish/v1/Systems/does-not-exist")
     err = excinfo.value
     assert err.status == 404
     assert err.has_message("ResourceMissingAtURI")
 @pytest.mark.parametrize(
     "payload, message",
     [
         ({"NoSuchProperty": 1}, "PropertyUnknown"),
         ({"PowerState": "Off"}, "PropertyNotWritable"),
         ({"AssetTag": 12345}, "PropertyValueTypeError"),
         ({"LocationIndicatorActive": "yes"}, "PropertyValueTypeError"),
     ],
     ids=["unknown-prop", "read-only", "int-for-string", "string-for-bool"],
 )
 def test_invalid_patch_payloads_are_rejected(system_restored, payload,
 message):
     with pytest.raises(RedfishHTTPError) as excinfo:
         system_restored.patch(SYSTEM, payload)
     assert excinfo.value.status == 400
     assert excinfo.value.has_message(message)
 def test_malformed_json_body_is_400(rf):
     with pytest.raises(RedfishHTTPError) as excinfo:
         rf.request("PATCH", SYSTEM, data='{"AssetTag": "unterminated',
                    headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"})
     assert excinfo.value.status == 400
     assert excinfo.value.has_message("MalformedJSON")
```

Things to note:

- ids=[...] gives readable names in reports `(test_invalid_patch_payloads_are_rejected[read-only]).`

- has_message("PropertyUnknown") matches only the last component of the MessageId, because the registry version (Base.1.13.0) differs between firmware builds.

- Malformed JSON is sent with data= (raw string) plus an explicit Content-Type.

- The system_restored fixture guarantees the system’s properties are put back even if the service wrongly accepts an invalid value.

lessons.title: Boundary and negative testing
lessons.body:
Boundary tests for a string property with a maximum length (here, the mock’s documented limit of 32):

```code
redfish_suite/tests/test_patch_and_actions.py
 @pytest.mark.parametrize("value", ["", "A", "X" * 32])  # boundary values
 def test_patch_asset_tag_boundaries_accepted(system_restored, value):
     rf = system_restored
     rf.patch(SYSTEM, {"AssetTag": value})
     assert rf.get_json(SYSTEM)["AssetTag"] == value
 def test_patch_asset_tag_too_long_rejected(system_restored):
     # The 32-character limit is a property of this mock. On a real BMC,
     # find the limit in its schema/documentation before writing this test.
     with pytest.raises(RedfishHTTPError) as excinfo:
         system_restored.patch(SYSTEM, {"AssetTag": "X" * 33})
     assert excinfo.value.status == 400
```

On a real BMC, find the limit in the schema (maxLength) or the vendor’s documentation. If neither states it, a test that discovers the limit is an investigation, not a pass/fail test.

lessons.title: Rate limiting and transient failures
lessons.body:
BMCs are small computers. Under load they answer **503 Service Un‐**

**available** (sometimes with Retry-After) or, rarely for BMCs, **429 Too Many Requests**. During start-up, the web server may refuse connections or return 503 for a while.

Guidelines:

- Treat 502/503/504 as transient for idempotent requests: retry with backoff, honour Retry-After, cap attempts.

- Do not hammer: tests that poll should sleep between polls (1–5 s typical).

- Treat persistent transient errors as real failures and report them — a BMC that returns 503 for minutes has a problem.

- Separate “BMC not ready yet” (wait for readiness before the suite starts) from “BMC failed during the test” (fail with evidence).

Project 1 tests both sides:

```code
redfish_suite/tests/test_negative.py
 def test_transient_503_is_retried_for_get(rf, mock_server):
     mock_server.state.fail_next.extend([503, 503])  # two failures, then
 success
     system = rf.get_json(SYSTEM)  # retries=2 in mock_config
     assert system["Id"] == "system"
 def test_persistent_503_eventually_surfaces(rf, mock_server):
     mock_server.state.fail_next.extend([503] * 5)
     with pytest.raises(RedfishHTTPError) as excinfo:
         rf.get_json(SYSTEM)
     assert excinfo.value.status == 503
```

lessons.title: Resource creation and cleanup
lessons.body:
Any test that creates something (session, user account, event subscription, log entry) must delete it, even if the test fails. Patterns, from best to worst:

1. **Fixture with yield** — create before yield, delete after. pytest runs the teardown even if the test fails.

2. **try/finally** inside the test.

3. **Context managers** (with RedfishClient(cfg) as rf: logs out on exit).

4. **Sweep jobs** — a cleanup step that deletes anything named autotest-*. A safety net, not a substitute.

```code
import uuid
import pytest
@pytest.fixture
def temp_user(rf):
    name = f"autotest{uuid.uuid4().hex[:6]}"
    resp = rf.post("/redfish/v1/AccountService/Accounts",
                   {"UserName": name, "Password": "Generated-Pw-1!", "RoleId":
  "ReadOnly"},
                    expected=(201,))
     uri = resp.headers["Location"]
     yield name, uri
     rf.delete(uri, expected=(200, 202, 204, 404))   # 404 = test already
 deleted it
```

(The mock service does not implement AccountService; this fixture is for a real test BMC. Password rules are implementation-specific.)

lessons.title: Polling asynchronous operations
API mocking and unit testing
lessons.body:
Unit tests should run in milliseconds with no server. unittest.mock.patch.object replaces the session’s request method with a fake that returns prepared requests.Response objects or raises exceptions.

```code
examples/test_ch06_mocking.py
 """Chapter 6: unit-testing API code with unittest.mock (no server at all).
 Run:  pytest -v test_ch06_mocking.py
 """
 from __future__ import annotations
 import sys
 from pathlib import Path
 from unittest import mock
 import pytest
 import requests
 ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "projects" / "redfish_suite"
 sys.path[:0] = [str(ROOT / "src")]
 from redfish_suite import (RedfishClient, RedfishConfig,  # noqa: E402
                            RedfishConnectionError, RedfishHTTPError)
 def fake_response(status: int, body: dict | None = None, headers: dict | None
 = None):
     """Build a real requests.Response object without any network I/O."""
     import json
     r = requests.Response()
     r.status_code = status
     r._content = json.dumps(body).encode() if body is not None else b""
     r.headers.update(headers or {})
     r.url = "https://bmc.example.test/fake"
     return r
@pytest.fixture
def client() -> RedfishClient:
    cfg = RedfishConfig(base_url="https://bmc.example.test", username="u",
password="p",
                        retries=0)
    return RedfishClient(cfg)
def test_get_json_returns_body(client):
    with mock.patch.object(client.http, "request",
                           return_value=fake_response(200, {"Id": "system"}))
as req:
        assert client.get_json("/redfish/v1/Systems/system") == {"Id": "system
"}
    # Verify HOW the client called requests: method, full URL, explicit
timeout.
    args, kwargs = req.call_args
    assert args == ("GET", "https://bmc.example.test/redfish/v1/Systems/
system")
    assert kwargs["timeout"] == (5.0, 30.0)
def test_error_body_is_parsed_into_exception(client):
    body = {"error": {"code": "Base.1.13.0.GeneralError", "message": "x",
                      "@Message.ExtendedInfo": [{"MessageId": "Base.
1.13.0.PropertyUnknown"}]}}
    with mock.patch.object(client.http, "request",
return_value=fake_response(400, body)):
        with pytest.raises(RedfishHTTPError) as exc:
            client.patch("/redfish/v1/Systems/system", {"Bogus": 1})
    assert exc.value.status == 400 and
exc.value.has_message("PropertyUnknown")
def test_non_json_error_body_still_raises_cleanly(client):
    r = fake_response(502)
    r._content = b"<html>Bad Gateway</html>"
    with mock.patch.object(client.http, "request", return_value=r):
        with pytest.raises(RedfishHTTPError) as exc:
            client.get_json("/redfish/v1/")
    assert exc.value.status == 502 and exc.value.extended_info == []
@pytest.mark.parametrize("exc_type, text", [
    (requests.exceptions.ConnectTimeout, "connect timeout"),
    (requests.exceptions.ReadTimeout, "read timeout"),
    (requests.exceptions.ConnectionError, "connection failed"),
    (requests.exceptions.SSLError, "TLS error"),
])
def test_transport_errors_are_translated(client, exc_type, text):
    with mock.patch.object(client.http, "request",
side_effect=exc_type("boom")):
        with pytest.raises(RedfishConnectionError, match=text):
            client.get_json("/redfish/v1/")
def test_login_stores_token_and_logout_deletes(client):
    responses = [
        fake_response(201, {"@odata.id": "/redfish/v1/SessionService/Sessions/
7"},
                      {"X-Auth-Token": "tok", "Location": "/redfish/v1/
SessionService/Sessions/7"}),
        fake_response(204),
    ]
    with mock.patch.object(client.http, "request", side_effect=responses) as
req:
        client.login()
        assert client.http.headers["X-Auth-Token"] == "tok"
        client.logout()
    assert req.call_args_list[1].args == (
        "DELETE", "https://bmc.example.test/redfish/v1/SessionService/
Sessions/7")
    assert "X-Auth-Token" not in client.http.headers
```

**Output [Run]:**

```code
============================= test session starts
==============================
collecting ... collected 8 items
test_ch06_mocking.py::test_get_json_returns_body PASSED
[ 12%]
test_ch06_mocking.py::test_error_body_is_parsed_into_exception PASSED
[ 25%]
test_ch06_mocking.py::test_non_json_error_body_still_raises_cleanly PASSED
[ 37%]
test_ch06_mocking.py::test_transport_errors_are_translated[ConnectTimeout-
connect timeout] PASSED [ 50%]
test_ch06_mocking.py::test_transport_errors_are_translated[ReadTimeout-read
timeout] PASSED [ 62%]
test_ch06_mocking.py::test_transport_errors_are_translated[ConnectionError-
connection failed] PASSED [ 75%]
test_ch06_mocking.py::test_transport_errors_are_translated[SSLError-TLS error]
PASSED [ 87%]
test_ch06_mocking.py::test_login_stores_token_and_logout_deletes PASSED
[100%]
============================== 8 passed in 0.09s
===============================
```

These tests check our code’s behaviour: the URL and timeout passed to requests, error parsing, exception translation and the login/logout sequence. They complement, not replace, tests against a simulator or a real service.

Libraries such as responses or requests-mock provide nicer APIs for the same idea; unittest.mock is used here because it is in the standard library.

lessons.title: Integration with pytest and structured logging
lessons.body:
**Structured logging** writes machine-readable records (one JSON object per line) instead of free text, so you can filter and correlate later. Project

```code
1 writes reports/redfish_suite.jsonl:
  {"ts": "2026-10-15T03:13:14.277+00:00", "level": "INFO", "logger":
  "redfish_suite.client", "msg": "http POST http://127.0.0.1:41243/redfish/v1/
  SessionService/Sessions -> 201", "method": "POST", "url": "http://
  127.0.0.1:41243/redfish/v1/SessionService/Sessions", "status": 201,
  "elapsed_ms": 3.5}
  {"ts": "2026-10-15T03:13:14.278+00:00", "level": "INFO", "logger":
  "redfish_suite.client", "msg": "session created", "session": "/redfish/v1/
  SessionService/Sessions/1"}
  {"ts": "2026-10-15T03:13:14.321+00:00", "level": "INFO", "logger":
  "redfish_suite.client", "msg": "http GET http://127.0.0.1:41243/redfish/v1/
  Systems/does-not-exist -> 404", "method": "GET", "url": "http://
  127.0.0.1:41243/redfish/v1/Systems/does-not-exist", "status": 404,
  "elapsed_ms": 42.5}
```

Each record carries method, URL, status and elapsed time. The formatter passes every line through a redaction function so passwords and tokens never reach the log — see logging_setup.py in Chapter 8. Combine this with pytest’s own log file (log_file in pytest.ini) and the HTML report (pytest-html) for complete evidence.

lessons.title: Exercises
lessons.body:
1. Write a test that verifies a rejected PATCH did not change the resource.

2. Extend wait_for_task to honour a Retry-After header on the task monitor.

3. Write a unit test proving the client never retries POST after a read timeout.

**Solutions.**

1.

```code
def test_rejected_patch_has_no_side_effect(system_restored):
    rf = system_restored
    before = rf.get_json("/redfish/v1/Systems/system")["AssetTag"]
    with pytest.raises(RedfishHTTPError):
        rf.patch("/redfish/v1/Systems/system", {"AssetTag": "X" * 33})
    assert rf.get_json("/redfish/v1/Systems/system")["AssetTag"] == before
```

1. Use resp = self.get(task_uri), read resp.headers.get("Retry-After"), and sleep min(float(value), remaining_time) when it is a number of seconds; fall back to poll_s otherwise (it may also be an HTTP date).

2. Patch client.http.request with

```code
side_effect=requests.exceptions.ReadTimeout, call client.post(...), expect
```

RedfishConnectionError, and assert req.call_count == 1. (The real retry logic lives in urllib3 below Session.request; to test it end-to-end use the mock server with delay_s and count state.request_log entries for POST.)

lessons.title: Summary
lessons.body:
- Centralise HTTP behaviour in one client; keep tests declarative.

- Validate structure with JSON Schema, reporting all errors.

- Negative tests assert specific errors and no side effects.

- Poll async tasks with deadlines; tolerate expected reboots explicitly.

- Clean up in fixtures; log structured, redacted records.

lessons.title: What Redfish is and why BMCs use it
lessons.body:
**Redfish** is a standard for managing servers, storage, networking and other infrastructure, published by the **DMTF** (Distributed Management Task Force). It defines a RESTful interface over HTTPS with JSON payloads, a data model described by schemas, and standard behaviours for authentication, events and tasks. The core document is the Redfish Specification (**DSP0266**); the resource schemas are published as the Redfish Schema bundle (**DSP8010**); the human-readable Redfish Resource and Schema Guide is **DSP2046**; standard message registries (such as the Base registry) are published as **DSP8011**.

Why it replaced IPMI as the primary management interface:

| Problem with IPMI | Redfish answer |
| Binary protocol, needs special tools | HTTPS + JSON: any language, curl, browsers |
| Weak, dated security (RMCP+ weak‐ | TLS, standard web authentication, role- |
| nesses, UDP) | based privileges |
| Limited, rigid data model; heavy use of | Rich, extensible schemas with versioning |
| OEM commands | and a defined OEM section |
| Hard to scale to modern hardware (stor‐ | Model covers storage, networking, com‐ |
| age, GPUs, fabrics) | posability, telemetry |
| Problem with IPMI | Redfish answer |
| Discovery by guessing commands | Hypermedia: follow links from one well-known URL |

The specification is updated several times a year (1.x series). A service reports the version it implements in the service root’s RedfishVersion property. Always check the version and the schema versions a service actually returns before relying on a newer feature.

lessons.title: Redfish architecture and HTTPS communication
lessons.body:
```code
 Client (your test)                     Redfish service (on the BMC)
 ───────────────────                    ────────────────────────────
 HTTPS request  ─────────────────────▶  web server (bmcweb on OpenBMC)
   GET /redfish/v1/Systems/system         │  authentication & privilege check
   X-Auth-Token: ...                      │  route URL -> resource handler
                                          │  handler gathers data (D-Bus on
OpenBMC)
 JSON response ◀─────────────────────     │  build JSON per schema
   200 OK, ETag, body                     ▼
```

Rules from DSP0266 you should know **[Spec]**:

- Redfish resources live under /redfish/v1/. GET /redfish returns {"v1":

```code
"/redfish/v1/"}.
```

- HTTPS (TLS) is required for operations carrying credentials; services commonly disable plain HTTP entirely.

- The service root (/redfish/v1/) must be readable without authentication so clients can discover the service. Most other resources require authentication.

- Clients must not assume URI structure beyond what the specification fixes; they should navigate via links. (The specification has, in recent versions, also defined standard URI patterns for many resources, which makes URIs predictable — but member IDs still differ between implementations.)

lessons.title: Service root and resource discovery
lessons.body:
The **service root** is the entry point. Example **[Sim]** from the book’s mock:

```code
{
  "@odata.id": "/redfish/v1/",
  "@odata.type": "#ServiceRoot.v1_15_0.ServiceRoot",
  "Id": "RootService",
  "Name": "Root Service",
  "RedfishVersion": "1.17.0",
  "UUID": "00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001",
  "Systems": {"@odata.id": "/redfish/v1/Systems"},
  "Managers": {"@odata.id": "/redfish/v1/Managers"},
  "Chassis": {"@odata.id": "/redfish/v1/Chassis"},
  "SessionService": {"@odata.id": "/redfish/v1/SessionService"},
  "TaskService": {"@odata.id": "/redfish/v1/TaskService"},
  "Links": {"Sessions": {"@odata.id": "/redfish/v1/SessionService/Sessions"}}
}
```

A real service root typically also links AccountService, EventService,

```code
UpdateService, CertificateService, Registries, JsonSchemas and contains
```

ProtocolFeaturesSupported (which query parameters and features are available), Vendor and Product.

**Discovery** means starting at the root and following @odata.id links. The program below walks the mock service breadth-first, skipping Actions (which are POST targets, not readable resources):

```code
 examples/ch07_discover.py
  """Chapter 7: walk a Redfish service by following links, never by guessing
  URLs.
  Uses the redfish_suite client from Chapter 8 against the mock service.
  """
  from __future__ import annotations
  import sys
  from collections import deque
  from pathlib import Path
  ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "projects" / "redfish_suite"
  sys.path[:0] = [str(ROOT), str(ROOT / "src")]
  from redfish_suite import RedfishClient, RedfishConfig, RedfishHTTPError  #
  noqa: E402
  from simulator.mock_redfish import MockRedfishServer  # noqa: E402
def links(obj, found=None):
    """Collect every '@odata.id' value nested anywhere in a payload."""
    found = [] if found is None else found
    if isinstance(obj, dict):
        for k, v in obj.items():
            if k == "@odata.id" and isinstance(v, str):
                found.append(v)
            elif k != "Actions":          # action targets are POST-only
                links(v, found)
    elif isinstance(obj, list):
        for item in obj:
            links(item, found)
    return found
with MockRedfishServer("walker", "walker-pass") as srv:
    cfg = RedfishConfig(base_url=srv.base_url, username="walker", password="wa
lker-pass")
    with RedfishClient(cfg) as rf:
        queue, seen = deque(["/redfish/v1/"]), set()
        while queue and len(seen) < 40:          # safety limit on large
services
            uri = queue.popleft().rstrip("/") or "/"
            if uri in seen:
                continue
            seen.add(uri)
            try:
                body = rf.get_json(uri)
            except RedfishHTTPError as exc:
                print(f"{uri:<62} HTTP {exc.status}")
                continue
            print(f"{uri:<62} {body.get('@odata.type', '-')}")
            queue.extend(u for u in links(body) if u.rstrip("/") not in seen)
```

**Output [Run]** (truncated):

```code
/redfish/v1
#ServiceRoot.v1_15_0.ServiceRoot
/redfish/v1/Systems
#ComputerSystemCollection.ComputerSystemCollection
/redfish/v1/Managers
#ManagerCollection.ManagerCollection
/redfish/v1/Chassis
#ChassisCollection.ChassisCollection
/redfish/v1/SessionService
#SessionService.v1_1_9.SessionService
/redfish/v1/TaskService
#TaskService.v1_2_0.TaskService
/redfish/v1/SessionService/Sessions
#SessionCollection.SessionCollection
/redfish/v1/Systems/system
#ComputerSystem.v1_20_0.ComputerSystem
/redfish/v1/Managers/bmc
#Manager.v1_17_0.Manager
/redfish/v1/Chassis/chassis
#Chassis.v1_23_0.Chassis
/redfish/v1/TaskService/Tasks
#TaskCollection.TaskCollection
/redfish/v1/SessionService/Sessions/1
#Session.v1_6_0.Session
/redfish/v1/Systems/system/LogServices
#LogServiceCollection.LogServiceCollection
/redfish/v1/Systems/system/LogServices/EventLog
#LogService.v1_4_0.LogService
/redfish/v1/Systems/system/LogServices/EventLog/Entries
```

The same script works on any Redfish service because it never guesses a URL. (On a large real service, limit depth and count, and expect some links to return 404 or 403 depending on privileges and optional features.)

source.section: 7.4 Systems, Managers, Chassis and other common resources

lessons.title: Collections, members and resource identifiers
lessons.body:
A **collection** lists references to **members**:

```code
{
  "@odata.id": "/redfish/v1/Systems",
  "@odata.type": "#ComputerSystemCollection.ComputerSystemCollection",
  "Name": "Computer System Collection",
  "Members": [{"@odata.id": "/redfish/v1/Systems/system"}],
  "Members@odata.count": 1
}
```

- Members contains links, not full resources (unless $expand is used and supported).

- Members@odata.count is the total number of members, which can exceed the number in the current page; then Members@odata.nextLink gives the next page.

- Each resource has an Id (unique within its collection) and an @odata.id (its URI). Treat @odata.id as opaque; do not parse it to build other URIs.

lessons.title: Properties, links and navigation
lessons.body:
Resources contain:

- Properties — "PowerState": "On", "Status": {"State": "Enabled", "Health": "OK"}. Status.State describes availability (Enabled, Disabled, `Absent, StandbyOffline, Starting, …); Status.Health the health (OK,`

Warning, Critical); some resources add HealthRollup for subordinate resources.

- **Navigation links** — objects with an @odata.id, such as "LogServices":

```code
{"@odata.id": "..."}.
```

- **The Links object** — relationships to resources elsewhere in the tree. For example a ComputerSystem’s Links.Chassis and Links.ManagedBy point to the chassis that contains it and the manager that manages it.

- **Actions** — operations invoked by POST:

```code
"Actions": {
  "#ComputerSystem.Reset": {
    "target": "/redfish/v1/Systems/system/Actions/ComputerSystem.Reset",
    "ResetType@Redfish.AllowableValues": ["On", "ForceOff",
"GracefulShutdown",
                                          "GracefulRestart", "ForceRestart"]
  }
}
```

Always read the target from the resource and validate against the advertised allowable values (or the @Redfish.ActionInfo resource when present) instead of hard-coding them.

- **OEM extensions** — vendor-specific data lives under an Oem object keyed by vendor (for example "Oem": {"OpenBmc": {...}}). Tests for standard behaviour should not depend on OEM content.

lessons.title: Redfish schemas and versioning
lessons.body:
Every resource declares its type and version in @odata.type:

```code
#ComputerSystem.v1_20_0.ComputerSystem
 \____________/ \_____/ \____________/
   namespace    version    type name
```

- Versions are vMAJOR_MINOR_ERRATA. Within a major version, newer minor versions only add properties (backward compatible); errata versions fix documentation and schema mistakes.

- A property’s absence usually means “not supported by this implementation”, not an error — unless your requirements or an interoperability **profile** make it mandatory.

- Schemas are available as JSON Schema and CSDL (OData XML). A service may host copies under /redfish/v1/JsonSchemas or point to the DMTF public repository.

- **Interoperability profiles** (JSON documents processed by DMTF’s Redfish-Interop-Validator) let an organisation state “these properties are mandatory for our products” — a great foundation for requirement-driven tests.

lessons.title: Authentication methods and sessions
lessons.body:
Redfish services support HTTP Basic authentication and Redfish session login **[Spec]**. Many also support other mechanisms (for example mutual TLS); check the service.

Session login:

```code
$ curl -s --cacert lab-ca.pem -D headers.txt -o /dev/null \
       -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
       -d '{"UserName":"automation","Password":"'"$BMC_PASSWORD"'"}' \
       https://bmc.example.test/redfish/v1/SessionService/Sessions
$ grep -i -E "x-auth-token|location" headers.txt
X-Auth-Token: <token>
Location: /redfish/v1/SessionService/Sessions/<session-id>
```

Then:

```code
$ curl -s --cacert lab-ca.pem -H "X-Auth-Token: $TOKEN" \
       https://bmc.example.test/redfish/v1/Systems/system
  $ curl -s --cacert lab-ca.pem -X DELETE -H "X-Auth-Token: $TOKEN" \
         https://bmc.example.test/redfish/v1/SessionService/Sessions/<session-
  id>
```

Authorisation uses **roles** and **privileges**. Standard roles are Administrator, Operator and ReadOnly; standard privileges include Login,

```code
ConfigureManager, ConfigureUsers, ConfigureComponents and ConfigureSelf
```

**[Spec]**. The privilege registry maps each resource and method to the privileges required. A typical rule: reading most resources needs Login; changing system settings needs ConfigureComponents; managing accounts `needs ConfigureUsers.`

lessons.title: Error responses and extended error information
lessons.body:
On error, a Redfish service returns a JSON body like this **[Spec]**:

```code
{
  "error": {
    "code": "Base.1.13.0.GeneralError",
    "message": "A general error has occurred. See ExtendedInfo for more
information.",
    "@Message.ExtendedInfo": [
      {
        "@odata.type": "#Message.v1_1_1.Message",
        "MessageId": "Base.1.13.0.PropertyUnknown",
        "Message": "The property NoSuchProperty is not in the list of valid
properties.",
        "MessageArgs": ["NoSuchProperty"],
        "MessageSeverity": "Warning",
        "Resolution": "Remove the unknown property from the request body and
resubmit."
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

- MessageId = <RegistryPrefix>.<Major>.<Minor>.<Errata>.<MessageKey>. Match tests on the registry prefix and message key (Base … PropertyUnknown), not the version.

- MessageArgs holds the variable parts (property names, values).

- Older message schema versions use Severity; newer ones use MessageSeverity. Parse both.

- Successful responses can also carry @Message.ExtendedInfo (for example to report that a setting will apply after reboot).

Common Base registry message keys: PropertyUnknown,

```code
PropertyValueTypeError, PropertyValueFormatError, PropertyValueNotInList,
PropertyNotWritable, PropertyMissing, MalformedJSON, ResourceNotFound,
ResourceMissingAtURI, ActionNotSupported, ActionParameterMissing,
ActionParameterUnknown, InsufficientPrivilege, NoValidSession,
ResourceAtUriUnauthorized, ServiceTemporarilyUnavailable, PreconditionFailed,
```

Success. The exact set depends on the registry version; the authoritative list is DSP8011.

lessons.title: Event subscriptions and task resources
lessons.body:
**Events.** The EventService delivers notifications. Two delivery styles:

1. **Push subscriptions**: create a subscription with a Destination URL; the service POSTs event payloads to it.

```code
POST /redfish/v1/EventService/Subscriptions
{
  "Destination": "https://listener.lab.example.test:8443/events",
  "Protocol": "Redfish",
  "EventFormatType": "Event",
  "RegistryPrefixes": ["ResourceEvent"],
  "Context": "autotest-1234"
}
```

1. **Server-Sent Events (SSE)**: the client opens a long-lived HTTP GET to the ServerSentEventUri and reads a text stream.

For testing, Actions/#EventService.SubmitTestEvent (when implemented) asks the service to emit a test event. An event test checks: subscription created (201 + Location), event received with the right Context and MessageId, and subscription deleted at the end. Your listener must be reachable from the BMC — often the hardest part in a lab network.

**Tasks.** Long operations (firmware update, some resets, log collection) return 202 Accepted with Location pointing to a task or task monitor. Polling the task monitor typically returns 202 while running and the final result when done; the task resource under /redfish/v1/TaskService/Tasks/ `<id> shows TaskState, TaskStatus, PercentComplete and Messages. Project 1’s` mock returns a task for the Reset action so you can practise polling.

lessons.title: Relationships between Redfish, BMC firmware and server management
lessons.body:
On **OpenBMC**, the Redfish service is **bmcweb**, a C++ web server. Most Redfish properties are computed on request by reading **D-Bus** objects published by other daemons:

| Redfish | D-Bus (examples, OpenBMC | Daemon [Impl]) |

```code
Systems/system          xyz.openbmc_project.State.Host / .Chassis phosphor-state-
PowerState                                                     manager
Managers/bmc            xyz.openbmc_project.Software.Version   phosphor-bmc-code-
FirmwareVersion                                                mgmt
```

| Sensor readings | xyz.openbmc_project.Sensor.Value | dbus-sensors, |

```code
phosphor-hwmon,
        pldmd
```

| Event log entries | xyz.openbmc_project.Logging.Entry | phosphor-logging |

This matters for debugging: if a Redfish value is wrong, check D-Bus on `the BMC (busctl tree, busctl introspect, busctl get-property). If D-Bus is` right, the bug is in bmcweb; if D-Bus is wrong, look at the producing daemon or the hardware below it.

```code
# On an OpenBMC test system (examples; service names vary by platform/release)
# busctl tree xyz.openbmc_project.State.Host
# busctl get-property xyz.openbmc_project.State.Host \
     /xyz/openbmc_project/state/host0 xyz.openbmc_project.State.Host
CurrentHostState
s "xyz.openbmc_project.State.Host.HostState.Running"
```

(The output line above shows the format D-Bus property output takes; it was not captured from a specific system.)

The **Redfish Host Interface** (DSP0270) lets the host OS reach the BMC’s Redfish service over an internal channel (commonly a USB virtual NIC), without the external management network.

lessons.title: Lab: explore a Redfish service
lessons.body:
Start the mock in one terminal and explore with curl in another:

```code
$ cd projects/redfish_suite
$ python -m simulator.mock_redfish --port 8000
# second terminal:
$ curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8000/redfish/v1/ | python -m json.tool
$ curl -s -u mock_user:mock_pass_123 http://127.0.0.1:8000/redfish/v1/Systems/
system \
     | python -m json.tool
$ curl -s -u mock_user:mock_pass_123 -X PATCH -H "Content-Type: application/
json" \
     -d '{"PowerState":"Off"}' http://127.0.0.1:8000/redfish/v1/Systems/system
```

Tasks: (1) find the allowable reset types; (2) trigger GracefulRestart and poll the returned task; (3) produce a PropertyNotWritable error and read `its MessageId.`

**Solution sketch.** (1) Read

```code
Actions."#ComputerSystem.Reset"."ResetType@Redfish.AllowableValues". (2) curl
-i -u ... -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d
'{"ResetType":"GracefulRestart"}' http://127.0.0.1:8000/redfish/v1/Systems/
system/Actions/ComputerSystem.Reset → 202 with Location: /redfish/v1/
```

TaskService/Tasks/1; GET it twice and see TaskState change from Running to Completed. (3) The PATCH above returns 400 with Base. `1.13.0.PropertyNotWritable.`

lessons.title: Common mistakes
lessons.body:
- Hard-coding Systems/1 or Systems/system instead of discovering members.

- Treating a missing optional property as a failure.

- Matching full MessageIds including the registry version.

- Ignoring Status.State (an Absent component’s Health is meaningless).

- Not checking RedfishVersion and schema versions before testing a new feature.

- Polling tasks without a deadline; not tolerating a BMC reboot during updates.

lessons.title: Exercises
lessons.body:
1. What is the difference between Members@odata.count and len(Members)?

2. A test expects Chassis/<id>/Thermal and gets 404 on a new firmware. Why might that be correct behaviour?

3. Why must the service root be readable without authentication?

**Solutions.**

1. The count is the total number of members in the collection; Members holds only the current page. They differ when the collection is paginated.

2. Thermal is deprecated in newer schemas in favour of ThermalSubsystem and Sensors; the firmware may have moved to the newer model. Check the chassis resource for the links it actually provides.

3. So clients can discover the service — its version, capabilities and where the session service is — before they have credentials.

lessons.title: Summary
lessons.body:
- Redfish = DMTF standard: HTTPS + JSON + schemas + hypermedia navigation.

- Start at /redfish/v1/, follow @odata.id links, page with nextLink.

- @odata.type carries schema and version; absent optional properties are normal.

- Errors carry registry-based MessageIds in @Message.ExtendedInfo.

- Long operations are tasks; events can be pushed or streamed.

- On OpenBMC, Redfish is a view over D-Bus provided by bmcweb.

lessons.title: Project directory structure
lessons.body:
```code
redfish_suite/
├── README.md                 # setup and usage (Chapter 22)
├── requirements.txt          # dependencies
├── pytest.ini                # markers, paths, log file settings
├── .env.example              # template for live-BMC settings (never
commit .env)
├── .gitignore
├── schemas/                  # small JSON Schemas for the properties we test
│   ├── service_root.json
│   └── computer_system.json
├── simulator/                # offline mock Redfish service
│   ├── __init__.py
│   └── mock_redfish.py
├── src/redfish_suite/        # the reusable library
│   ├── __init__.py
│   ├── config.py             # RedfishConfig (env vars, validation)
 │   ├── errors.py             # exception hierarchy + error-body parsing
 │   ├── logging_setup.py      # JSON-lines logging with redaction
 │   ├── client.py             # RedfishClient
 │   └── validators.py         # JSON Schema helpers
 └── tests/
     ├── conftest.py           # fixtures, --live option, markers
     ├── test_service_root.py  # discovery and schema tests
     ├── test_sessions.py      # authentication and sessions
     ├── test_patch_and_actions.py
     ├── test_negative.py
     ├── test_live_bmc.py      # optional, real BMC only
     └── unit/test_units.py    # no network
```

Why this layout:

- **src/ layout** keeps library code separate from tests and simulators; tests import the library the same way users will.

- **simulator/** is test infrastructure, not part of the library.

- **schemas/** is data; keeping it out of code makes changes reviewable.

- pytest.ini sets pythonpath = src . so no package installation is required to run the tests (for distribution you would add a `pyproject.toml).`

```code
redfish_suite/requirements.txt

```

pytest-html was chosen over Allure because it produces a single self-contained HTML file with no extra server or command-line tool, which is easy to archive in Jenkins. Allure gives richer history and trend views but needs the Allure CLI to generate reports; it is a good upgrade for large teams.

lessons.title: Configuration using environment variables
lessons.body:
```code
redfish_suite/src/redfish_suite/config.py
 """Configuration loaded from environment variables.
 Credentials are never hard-coded. In CI they come from the CI secret store
 (for example Jenkins credentials bound to environment variables).
 """
 from __future__ import annotations
 import os
 from dataclasses import dataclass, field
 class ConfigError(ValueError):
     """Raised when required configuration is missing or invalid."""
 def _parse_verify(raw: str) -> bool | str:
     """RF_VERIFY may be 'true', 'false', or a path to a CA bundle file."""
     value = raw.strip()
     if value.lower() in {"1", "true", "yes"}:
         return True
     if value.lower() in {"0", "false", "no"}:
         return False
     if not os.path.isfile(value):
         raise ConfigError(f"RF_VERIFY points to a missing CA bundle: {value}")
     return value
 @dataclass(frozen=True)
 class RedfishConfig:
     base_url: str
     username: str
     # repr=False keeps the password out of logs and pytest failure output.
     password: str = field(repr=False)
     verify: bool | str = True
     connect_timeout: float = 5.0
     read_timeout: float = 30.0
     retries: int = 3
     backoff_factor: float = 0.5
     def __post_init__(self) -> None:
         if not self.base_url.startswith(("http://", "https://")):
             raise ConfigError("base_url must start with http:// or https://")
         if self.connect_timeout <= 0 or self.read_timeout <= 0:
             raise ConfigError("timeouts must be positive")
         if self.retries < 0:
             raise ConfigError("retries must be >= 0")
     @property
    def timeout(self) -> tuple[float, float]:
        """(connect, read) tuple in the form requests expects."""
        return (self.connect_timeout, self.read_timeout)
    @classmethod
    def from_env(cls, prefix: str = "RF_") -> "RedfishConfig":
        """Build a config from RF_BASE_URL, RF_USERNAME, RF_PASSWORD, ...."""
        def need(name: str) -> str:
            value = os.environ.get(prefix + name)
            if not value:
                raise ConfigError(f"environment variable {prefix}
{name} is not set")
            return value
        try:
            return cls(
                base_url=need("BASE_URL").rstrip("/"),
                username=need("USERNAME"),
                password=need("PASSWORD"),
                verify=_parse_verify(os.environ.get(prefix + "VERIFY", "true")
),
                connect_timeout=float(os.environ.get(prefix + "CONNECT_TIMEOUT
", "5")),
                read_timeout=float(os.environ.get(prefix + "READ_TIMEOUT", "30
")),
                retries=int(os.environ.get(prefix + "RETRIES", "3")),
            )
        except ValueError as exc:  # float()/int() conversion problems
            if isinstance(exc, ConfigError):
                raise
            raise ConfigError(f"invalid numeric setting: {exc}") from exc
```

Design points:

- A **frozen dataclass**: configuration cannot be changed accidentally mid-run.

- password has field(repr=False), so printing the config — or a pytest failure showing it — never reveals the password.

- verify accepts true, false or a CA bundle path; a missing bundle path is an immediate, clear error.

- __post_init__ validates values so mistakes fail fast at start-up, not deep in a test.

- timeout returns the (connect, read) tuple requests expects.

The template for live runs:

```code
red‐
fish_suite/.env.example
 # Copy to .env (never commit .env) and load with:  set -a; . ./.env; set +a
 # Only needed for --live runs against an AUTHORISED test BMC.
 RF_BASE_URL=https://bmc.lab.example.test
 RF_USERNAME=automation_user
 RF_PASSWORD=change-me
 # true | false | /path/to/lab-ca.pem   (prefer a CA bundle over false)
 RF_VERIFY=/etc/ssl/certs/lab-ca.pem
 RF_CONNECT_TIMEOUT=5
 RF_READ_TIMEOUT=30
 RF_RETRIES=3
```

lessons.title: Errors and extended information
lessons.body:
```code
redfish_suite/src/redfish_suite/errors.py
 """Exception hierarchy for the Redfish client.
 Every failure raised by the client is a subclass of RedfishError so that
 tests can catch "anything from the client" without catching unrelated bugs
 (for example a KeyError in the test itself).
 """
 from __future__ import annotations
 from dataclasses import dataclass, field
 from typing import Any
 class RedfishError(Exception):
     """Base class for all errors raised by redfish_suite."""
 class RedfishConnectionError(RedfishError):
     """The TCP/TLS connection could not be made, or the request timed out."""
 @dataclass
 class ExtendedInfo:
     """One entry of the Redfish '@Message.ExtendedInfo' array."""
     message_id: str
     message: str = ""
     severity: str = ""
     resolution: str = ""
     @classmethod
     def from_dict(cls, raw: dict[str, Any]) -> "ExtendedInfo":
        return cls(
            message_id=str(raw.get("MessageId", "")),
            message=str(raw.get("Message", "")),
            # Newer schemas use MessageSeverity; older ones use Severity.
            severity=str(raw.get("MessageSeverity", raw.get("Severity", ""))),
            resolution=str(raw.get("Resolution", "")),
        )
@dataclass
class RedfishHTTPError(RedfishError):
    """The service answered, but with a status code the caller did not
expect."""
    method: str
    url: str
    status: int
    code: str = ""
    message: str = ""
    extended_info: list[ExtendedInfo] = field(default_factory=list)
    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        super().__init__(str(self))
    def __str__(self) -> str:
        ids = ", ".join(e.message_id for e in self.extended_info) or "none"
        return (
            f"{self.method} {self.url} -> HTTP {self.status} "
            f"(code={self.code or 'n/a'}, message_ids=[{ids}])"
        )
    def has_message(self, suffix: str) -> bool:
        """True if any MessageId ends with suffix, e.g. 'PropertyUnknown'.
        MessageIds look like 'Base.1.13.0.PropertyUnknown'. The registry
        version in the middle differs between firmware builds, so tests
        should match on the final component only.
        """
        return any(e.message_id.split(".")[-1] == suffix for e in self.extende
d_info)
class RedfishAuthError(RedfishHTTPError):
    """HTTP 401 - the credentials or token were rejected."""
def parse_error_body(body: Any) -> tuple[str, str, list[ExtendedInfo]]:
    """Extract (code, message, extended_info) from a Redfish error payload.
    The Redfish specification defines an error response of the form
    {"error": {"code": ..., "message": ..., "@Message.ExtendedInfo": [...]}}.
    Real services sometimes return an empty body or HTML on errors, so every
    lookup here is defensive.
    """
     if not isinstance(body, dict):
         return "", "", []
     err = body.get("error")
     if not isinstance(err, dict):
         # Some services put @Message.ExtendedInfo at the top level of a
         # successful-but-annotated response; handle that too.
         infos = body.get("@Message.ExtendedInfo", [])
         return "", "", [ExtendedInfo.from_dict(i) for i in infos if
 isinstance(i, dict)]
     infos = err.get("@Message.ExtendedInfo", [])
     return (
         str(err.get("code", "")),
         str(err.get("message", "")),
         [ExtendedInfo.from_dict(i) for i in infos if isinstance(i, dict)],
     )
```

- All library exceptions derive from RedfishError, so callers can catch “anything from the client” without masking unrelated bugs.

- RedfishHTTPError keeps method, URL, status, code, message and the parsed ExtendedInfo list; its __str__ is informative in pytest output.

- has_message("PropertyUnknown") compares only the message key, making tests portable across registry versions.

- parse_error_body is defensive: real services sometimes send empty or HTML error bodies (for example from a reverse proxy).

lessons.title: Structured logging with redaction
lessons.body:
```code
redfish_suite/src/redfish_suite/logging_setup.py
 """Structured (JSON-lines) logging with secret redaction."""
 from __future__ import annotations
 import json
 import logging
 import re
 from datetime import datetime, timezone
 # Keys whose values must never appear in logs.
 SENSITIVE_KEYS = ("password", "x-auth-token", "authorization", "token", "secre
 t")
 _KV_PATTERN = re.compile(
     r'(?i)("?(?:' + "|".join(re.escape(k) for k in SENSITIVE_KEYS) + r')"?
 \s*[:=]\s*)'
     r'("[^"]*"|\'[^\']*\'|[^\s,}]+)'
 )
def redact(text: str) -> str:
    """Replace values that follow sensitive keys with '***'."""
    return _KV_PATTERN.sub(lambda m: m.group(1) + '"***"', text)
class RedactingFilter(logging.Filter):
    def filter(self, record: logging.LogRecord) -> bool:
        record.msg = redact(record.getMessage())
        record.args = None
        return True
class JsonFormatter(logging.Formatter):
    """One JSON object per line: easy to grep, parse and correlate."""
    def format(self, record: logging.LogRecord) -> str:
        entry = {
            "ts": datetime.fromtimestamp(record.created, tz=timezone.utc).isof
ormat(
                timespec="milliseconds"
            ),
            "level": record.levelname,
            "logger": record.name,
            "msg": record.getMessage(),
        }
        # Extra fields passed with logger.info(..., extra={"fields": {...}})
        fields = getattr(record, "fields", None)
        if isinstance(fields, dict):
            entry.update({k: v for k, v in fields.items() if k not in entry})
        if record.exc_info:
            entry["exc"] = self.formatException(record.exc_info)
        return redact(json.dumps(entry, default=str))
def configure_logging(log_file: str | None = None, level: int = logging.INFO)
-> None:
    """Attach a JSON handler to the 'redfish_suite' logger (idempotent)."""
    logger = logging.getLogger("redfish_suite")
    logger.setLevel(level)
    if any(getattr(h, "_rf_json", False) for h in logger.handlers):
        return
    handler: logging.Handler = (
        logging.FileHandler(log_file, encoding="utf-8") if log_file else
logging.StreamHandler()
    )
    handler.setFormatter(JsonFormatter())
    handler.addFilter(RedactingFilter())
     handler._rf_json = True  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
     logger.addHandler(handler)
```

- JsonFormatter writes one JSON object per line with a UTC timestamp, level, logger and message, plus any structured fields passed via `extra=.`

- redact() replaces values that follow sensitive keys (password, x-auth-token, authorization, token, secret) with "***", both in the message and in the final JSON line. The unit tests prove it.

- configure_logging is idempotent so repeated calls (for example from multiple fixtures) do not duplicate handlers.

lessons.title: The reusable Redfish client
lessons.body:
```code
redfish_suite/src/redfish_suite/client.py
 """A small, reusable Redfish client built on requests.
 Design goals:
 * Explicit (connect, read) timeouts on every request.
 * Automatic retries only where they are safe (idempotent methods,
   connection failures, 502/503/504).
 * Session-based authentication with guaranteed logout (context manager).
 * Non-success responses become typed exceptions carrying Redfish
   extended error information.
 """
 from __future__ import annotations
 import logging
 import time
 from collections.abc import Iterator
 from typing import Any
 from urllib.parse import urljoin
 import requests
 from requests.adapters import HTTPAdapter
 from urllib3.util.retry import Retry
 from .config import RedfishConfig
 from .errors import (
     RedfishAuthError,
     RedfishConnectionError,
     RedfishError,
     RedfishHTTPError,
     parse_error_body,
 )
log = logging.getLogger("redfish_suite.client")
SERVICE_ROOT = "/redfish/v1/"
SESSIONS = "/redfish/v1/SessionService/Sessions"
def _build_session(config: RedfishConfig) -> requests.Session:
    retry = Retry(
        total=config.retries,
        connect=config.retries,
        read=config.retries,
        status=config.retries,
        backoff_factor=config.backoff_factor,
        status_forcelist=(502, 503, 504),
        # Only idempotent methods are retried after the request was sent.
        # POST and PATCH are NOT here: retrying them can apply a change twice.
        allowed_methods=frozenset({"GET", "HEAD", "OPTIONS"}),
        respect_retry_after_header=True,
        raise_on_status=False,  # let our own code turn statuses into errors
    )
    session = requests.Session()
    adapter = HTTPAdapter(max_retries=retry, pool_connections=4,
pool_maxsize=4)
    session.mount("http://", adapter)
    session.mount("https://", adapter)
    session.verify = config.verify
    session.headers.update(
        {"Accept": "application/json", "OData-Version": "4.0"}
    )
    return session
class RedfishClient:
    """Usage:
    with RedfishClient(cfg) as rf:          # logs in
        root = rf.get_json("/redfish/v1/")
    # logged out here, even if the block raised
    """
    def __init__(self, config: RedfishConfig, session: requests.Session |
None = None):
        self.config = config
        self.http = session or _build_session(config)
        self._session_uri: str | None = None
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ utils
    def url(self, path: str) -> str:
        """Turn '/redfish/v1/Systems' or a full URL into a full URL."""
        if path.startswith(("http://", "https://")):
            return path
        return urljoin(self.config.base_url + "/", path.lstrip("/"))
    @property
    def logged_in(self) -> bool:
        return "X-Auth-Token" in self.http.headers
    # --------------------------------------------------------------- core I/O
    def request(
        self,
        method: str,
        path: str,
        *,
        json: Any = None,
        data: str | bytes | None = None,
        headers: dict[str, str] | None = None,
        expected: tuple[int, ...] = (200,),
        auth: Any = None,
    ) -> requests.Response:
        url = self.url(path)
        started = time.monotonic()
        try:
            resp = self.http.request(
                method,
                url,
                json=json,
                data=data,
                headers=headers,
                timeout=self.config.timeout,
                auth=auth,
            )
        except requests.exceptions.SSLError as exc:
            raise RedfishConnectionError(f"TLS error for {method} {url}:
{exc}") from exc
        except requests.exceptions.ConnectTimeout as exc:
            raise RedfishConnectionError(f"connect timeout for {method}
{url}") from exc
        except requests.exceptions.ReadTimeout as exc:
            raise RedfishConnectionError(f"read timeout for {method} {url}") f
rom exc
        except requests.exceptions.ConnectionError as exc:
            raise RedfishConnectionError(f"connection failed for {method}
{url}: {exc}") from exc
        elapsed_ms = round((time.monotonic() - started) * 1000, 1)
        log.info(
            "http %s %s -> %s",
            method,
            url,
            resp.status_code,
            extra={"fields": {"method": method, "url": url,
                              "status": resp.status_code, "elapsed_ms":
elapsed_ms}},
        )
        if resp.status_code not in expected:
            self._raise_for(method, url, resp)
        return resp
    @staticmethod
    def _raise_for(method: str, url: str, resp: requests.Response) -> None:
        try:
            body = resp.json()
        except ValueError:  # empty body or non-JSON (e.g. an HTML proxy page)
            body = None
        code, message, infos = parse_error_body(body)
        cls = RedfishAuthError if resp.status_code == 401 else
RedfishHTTPError
        raise cls(method=method, url=url, status=resp.status_code,
                  code=code, message=message, extended_info=infos)
    # ------------------------------------------------------- convenience
verbs
    def get(self, path: str, expected: tuple[int, ...] = (200,)) ->
requests.Response:
        return self.request("GET", path, expected=expected)
    def get_json(self, path: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
        resp = self.get(path)
        try:
            body = resp.json()
        except ValueError as exc:
            raise RedfishError(f"GET {path} returned non-JSON body") from exc
        if not isinstance(body, dict):
            raise RedfishError(f"GET {path} returned JSON that is not an
object")
        return body
    def patch(
        self,
        path: str,
        payload: dict[str, Any],
        etag: str | None = None,
        expected: tuple[int, ...] = (200, 204),
    ) -> requests.Response:
        headers = {"If-Match": etag} if etag else None
        return self.request("PATCH", path, json=payload, headers=headers,
expected=expected)
    def post(
        self, path: str, payload: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
        expected: tuple[int, ...] = (200, 201, 202, 204),
    ) -> requests.Response:
        return self.request("POST", path, json=payload if payload is not None
else {},
                            expected=expected)
    def delete(self, path: str, expected: tuple[int, ...] = (200, 202, 204)) -
> requests.Response:
        return self.request("DELETE", path, expected=expected)
    # ----------------------------------------------------------------
sessions
    def login(self) -> None:
        """Create a Redfish session and store the X-Auth-Token header."""
        resp = self.request(
            "POST",
            SESSIONS,
            json={"UserName": self.config.username, "Password": self.config.pa
ssword},
            expected=(201, 200),
        )
        token = resp.headers.get("X-Auth-Token")
        if not token:
            raise RedfishError("session created but no X-Auth-Token header
returned")
        self.http.headers["X-Auth-Token"] = token
        # Location is the spec-defined place for the session URI; fall back
        # to @odata.id in the body for services that omit the header.
        location = resp.headers.get("Location")
        if not location:
            try:
                location = resp.json().get("@odata.id")
            except ValueError:
                location = None
        self._session_uri = location
        log.info("session created", extra={"fields": {"session": location}})
    def logout(self) -> None:
        """Delete our session. Safe to call twice; never masks the original
error."""
        if not self._session_uri:
            self.http.headers.pop("X-Auth-Token", None)
            return
        uri, self._session_uri = self._session_uri, None
        try:
            self.delete(uri)
            log.info("session deleted", extra={"fields": {"session": uri}})
        except RedfishError as exc:
            # The session will expire on its own; log loudly but do not raise
            # from cleanup, which would hide the real test failure.
            log.warning("logout failed: %s", exc)
        finally:
            self.http.headers.pop("X-Auth-Token", None)
    def __enter__(self) -> "RedfishClient":
        self.login()
        return self
    def __exit__(self, *exc_info: object) -> None:
        self.logout()
        self.http.close()
    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- helpers
    def service_root(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return self.get_json(SERVICE_ROOT)
    def iter_members(self, collection_path: str, max_pages: int = 100) ->
Iterator[dict[str, Any]]:
        """Yield member references of a collection, following nextLink
pages."""
        path: str | None = collection_path
        pages = 0
        while path:
            pages += 1
            if pages > max_pages:
                raise RedfishError(f"{collection_path}: more than {max_pages}
pages; loop?")
            body = self.get_json(path)
            yield from body.get("Members", [])
            path = body.get("Members@odata.nextLink")
    def member_uris(self, collection_path: str) -> list[str]:
        return [m["@odata.id"] for m in self.iter_members(collection_path)]
    def get_with_etag(self, path: str) -> tuple[dict[str, Any], str | None]:
        resp = self.get(path)
        body = resp.json()
        etag = resp.headers.get("ETag") or body.get("@odata.etag")
        return body, etag
    def wait_for_task(self, task_uri: str, timeout_s: float = 60.0,
                      poll_s: float = 1.0) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Poll a Redfish Task until it leaves a running state or times
out."""
        deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout_s
        running = {"New", "Starting", "Running", "Pending", "Stopping", "Cance
lling"}
        while True:
            task = self.get_json(task_uri)
            state = task.get("TaskState", "")
            if state not in running:
                return task
            if time.monotonic() >= deadline:
                raise RedfishError(
                    f"task {task_uri} still {state} after {timeout_s}s"
                )
            time.sleep(poll_s)
```

Walk-through:

- **_build_session** mounts an HTTPAdapter with a Retry policy that retries connection failures for any method, but read failures and 502/503/504 only for GET/HEAD/OPTIONS. raise_on_status=False returns the final response so our own code builds the error with full Redfish details.

- **url()** accepts either a path or an absolute URL (task Location headers may be either).

- **request()** is the single choke point. It always passes the configured timeout, translates requests exceptions into RedfishConnectionError with a precise message (TLS, connect timeout, read timeout, other connection failure), logs a structured record with elapsed time, and raises a typed error for any status not in expected.

- **login()** reads the token from X-Auth-Token and the session URI from Location, falling back to @odata.id in the body.

- **logout()** never raises: a failed logout is logged as a warning, because raising from cleanup would hide the real test failure. The session will expire on its own.

- **Context manager** — with RedfishClient(cfg) as rf: guarantees logout and connection-pool closure.

- **iter_members()** follows Members@odata.nextLink with a page limit; **get_with_etag()** returns the ETag from the header or @odata.etag; **wait_for_task()** polls with a monotonic deadline.

lessons.title: Schema-aware validation
lessons.body:
```code
redfish_suite/src/redfish_suite/validators.py
 """Response validation helpers.
 The JSON schemas in ../../schemas are deliberately small, hand-written
 subsets that check the properties *these tests* depend on. They are not the
 official DMTF schemas (published in the DSP8010 schema bundle). Validating
 against the official schemas is possible but requires resolving many
 cross-file $ref links; tools such as the DMTF Redfish-Service-Validator
 already do that job well.
 """
 from __future__ import annotations
 import json
 from functools import lru_cache
 from pathlib import Path
 from typing import Any
 from jsonschema import Draft7Validator
 SCHEMA_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / "schemas"
 class ValidationFailed(AssertionError):
     """Raised with every schema problem listed, not only the first one."""
 @lru_cache(maxsize=None)
 def load_schema(name: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
     path = SCHEMA_DIR / f"{name}.json"
     with path.open(encoding="utf-8") as fh:
         schema = json.load(fh)
     Draft7Validator.check_schema(schema)  # catch broken schemas early
     return schema
 def validate_resource(payload: dict[str, Any], schema_name: str) -> None:
     validator = Draft7Validator(load_schema(schema_name))
     errors = sorted(validator.iter_errors(payload), key=lambda e: list(e.path)
 )
     if errors:
         lines = [
             f"  at /{'/'.join(map(str, e.path))}: {e.message}" for e in errors
         ]
         raise ValidationFailed(f"{schema_name} validation failed:\n" + "\n".jo
 in(lines))
 def odata_type_is(payload: dict[str, Any], resource: str) -> bool:
     """'#ComputerSystem.v1_20_0.ComputerSystem' -> resource
 'ComputerSystem'."""
     odata_type = str(payload.get("@odata.type", ""))
     return odata_type.lstrip("#").split(".")[0] == resource
```
