lessons.title: The mock Redfish service
lessons.body:
The simulator implements just enough behaviour for the tests: unauthenticated service root, sessions (create/delete, Basic auth too), Systems/Managers/Chassis, paginated log entries, PATCH with type and writability checks and ETags, the Reset action returning a task, 404/405 errors, and fault injection (fail_next statuses and delay_s). It runs in a background thread on 127.0.0.1 with an OS-chosen port.

```code
redfish_suite/simulator/mock_redfish.py
"""A small in-process mock Redfish service for offline testing.
IMPORTANT: this is a teaching simulator, not a conformant Redfish service.
* It speaks plain HTTP on 127.0.0.1 (real BMCs use HTTPS).
* It implements only the resources the test suite needs.
* Resource paths follow common OpenBMC conventions (Systems/system,
  Managers/bmc, Chassis/chassis); other BMCs use different member IDs.
* Error MessageIds follow the DMTF Base message registry naming style; the
  registry version in them is illustrative.
Run standalone:  python -m simulator.mock_redfish --port 8000
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import argparse
import base64
import copy
import itertools
import json
import secrets
import threading
import time
from http import HTTPStatus
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer
from typing import Any
from urllib.parse import parse_qs, urlsplit
REG = "Base.1.13.0"  # illustrative registry version
def error_body(message_id: str, message: str, resolution: str = "") -> dict[st
r, Any]:
    return {
        "error": {
            "code": f"{REG}.GeneralError",
            "message": "A general error has occurred. See ExtendedInfo for
more information.",
            "@Message.ExtendedInfo": [
                {
                    "@odata.type": "#Message.v1_1_1.Message",
                    "MessageId": f"{REG}.{message_id}",
                    "Message": message,
                    "MessageSeverity": "Warning",
                    "Resolution": resolution,
                }
            ],
        }
    }
class MockState:
    """All mutable state lives here so tests can inspect and reset it."""
    def __init__(self, username: str, password: str, page_size: int = 10):
        self.username = username
        self.password = password
        self.page_size = page_size
        self.lock = threading.Lock()
        self.sessions: dict[str, str] = {}  # session id -> token
        self.session_ids = itertools.count(1)
        self.task_ids = itertools.count(1)
        self.tasks: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
        self.fail_next: list[int] = []  # statuses to inject on the next GETs
        self.delay_s: float = 0.0  # artificial response delay
        self.request_log: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
        self.system: dict[str, Any] = {
            "@odata.id": "/redfish/v1/Systems/system",
            "@odata.type": "#ComputerSystem.v1_20_0.ComputerSystem",
            "Id": "system",
            "Name": "System",
            "SystemType": "Physical",
            "Manufacturer": "ExampleVendor",
            "Model": "SIM-1000",
            "SerialNumber": "SIM0000001",
            "AssetTag": "",
            "PowerState": "On",
            "LocationIndicatorActive": False,
            "Status": {"State": "Enabled", "Health": "OK"},
            "ProcessorSummary": {"Count": 2},
            "MemorySummary": {"TotalSystemMemoryGiB": 64},
            "Actions": {
                "#ComputerSystem.Reset": {
                    "target": "/redfish/v1/Systems/system/Actions/
ComputerSystem.Reset",
                    "ResetType@Redfish.AllowableValues": [
                        "On", "ForceOff", "GracefulShutdown",
                        "GracefulRestart", "ForceRestart",
                    ],
                }
            },
            "LogServices": {"@odata.id": "/redfish/v1/Systems/system/
LogServices"},
        }
        self.etag_counter = 1
        self.log_entries = [
            {
                "@odata.id": f"/redfish/v1/Systems/system/LogServices/
EventLog/Entries/{i}",
                "Id": str(i),
                "Message": f"Simulated event {i}",
                "Severity": "OK",
            }
            for i in range(1, 26)
        ]
    def etag(self) -> str:
        return f'W/"{self.etag_counter}"'
def _static(state: MockState) -> dict[str, dict[str, Any]]:
    return {
        "/redfish": {"v1": "/redfish/v1/"},
        "/redfish/v1": {
            "@odata.id": "/redfish/v1/",
            "@odata.type": "#ServiceRoot.v1_15_0.ServiceRoot",
            "Id": "RootService",
            "Name": "Root Service",
            "RedfishVersion": "1.17.0",
            "UUID": "00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001",
            "Systems": {"@odata.id": "/redfish/v1/Systems"},
            "Managers": {"@odata.id": "/redfish/v1/Managers"},
            "Chassis": {"@odata.id": "/redfish/v1/Chassis"},
            "SessionService": {"@odata.id": "/redfish/v1/SessionService"},
            "TaskService": {"@odata.id": "/redfish/v1/TaskService"},
            "Links": {"Sessions": {"@odata.id": "/redfish/v1/SessionService/
Sessions"}},
        },
        "/redfish/v1/Systems": {
            "@odata.id": "/redfish/v1/Systems",
            "@odata.type": "#ComputerSystemCollection.ComputerSystemCollection
",
            "Name": "Computer System Collection",
            "Members": [{"@odata.id": "/redfish/v1/Systems/system"}],
            "Members@odata.count": 1,
        },
        "/redfish/v1/Managers": {
            "@odata.id": "/redfish/v1/Managers",
            "@odata.type": "#ManagerCollection.ManagerCollection",
            "Name": "Manager Collection",
            "Members": [{"@odata.id": "/redfish/v1/Managers/bmc"}],
            "Members@odata.count": 1,
        },
        "/redfish/v1/Managers/bmc": {
            "@odata.id": "/redfish/v1/Managers/bmc",
            "@odata.type": "#Manager.v1_17_0.Manager",
            "Id": "bmc",
            "Name": "OpenBmc Manager",
            "ManagerType": "BMC",
            "FirmwareVersion": "sim-2.15.0-dev",
            "Status": {"State": "Enabled", "Health": "OK"},
        },
        "/redfish/v1/Chassis": {
            "@odata.id": "/redfish/v1/Chassis",
            "@odata.type": "#ChassisCollection.ChassisCollection",
            "Name": "Chassis Collection",
            "Members": [{"@odata.id": "/redfish/v1/Chassis/chassis"}],
            "Members@odata.count": 1,
        },
        "/redfish/v1/Chassis/chassis": {
            "@odata.id": "/redfish/v1/Chassis/chassis",
            "@odata.type": "#Chassis.v1_23_0.Chassis",
            "Id": "chassis",
            "Name": "Chassis",
            "ChassisType": "RackMount",
            "Status": {"State": "Enabled", "Health": "OK"},
        },
        "/redfish/v1/SessionService": {
            "@odata.id": "/redfish/v1/SessionService",
            "@odata.type": "#SessionService.v1_1_9.SessionService",
            "Id": "SessionService",
            "Name": "Session Service",
            "SessionTimeout": 1800,
            "Sessions": {"@odata.id": "/redfish/v1/SessionService/Sessions"},
        },
        "/redfish/v1/TaskService": {
            "@odata.id": "/redfish/v1/TaskService",
            "@odata.type": "#TaskService.v1_2_0.TaskService",
            "Id": "TaskService",
            "Name": "Task Service",
            "Tasks": {"@odata.id": "/redfish/v1/TaskService/Tasks"},
        },
        "/redfish/v1/Systems/system/LogServices/EventLog": {
            "@odata.id": "/redfish/v1/Systems/system/LogServices/EventLog",
            "@odata.type": "#LogService.v1_4_0.LogService",
            "Id": "EventLog",
            "Name": "System Event Log",
            "Entries": {"@odata.id": "/redfish/v1/Systems/system/LogServices/
EventLog/Entries"},
        },
        "/redfish/v1/Systems/system/LogServices": {
            "@odata.id": "/redfish/v1/Systems/system/LogServices",
            "@odata.type": "#LogServiceCollection.LogServiceCollection",
            "Members": [{"@odata.id": "/redfish/v1/Systems/system/LogServices/
EventLog"}],
            "Members@odata.count": 1,
        },
    }
def make_handler(state: MockState) -> type[BaseHTTPRequestHandler]:
    static = _static(state)
    class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
        server_version = "MockRedfish/1.0"
        protocol_version = "HTTP/1.1"
        # -------------------------------------------------------- plumbing
        def log_message(self, fmt: str, *args: Any) -> None:  # keep test
output quiet
            pass
        def _send(self, status: int, body: Any = None,
                  headers: dict[str, str] | None = None) -> None:
            raw = b"" if body is None else json.dumps(body).encode()
            self.send_response(status)
            if body is not None:
                self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
            self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(raw)))
            self.send_header("OData-Version", "4.0")
            for k, v in (headers or {}).items():
                self.send_header(k, v)
            self.end_headers()
            if raw:
                self.wfile.write(raw)
        def _err(self, status: int, message_id: str, message: str,
                 headers: dict[str, str] | None = None) -> None:
            self._send(status, error_body(message_id, message), headers)
        def _read_json(self) -> tuple[bool, Any]:
            length = int(self.headers.get("Content-Length") or 0)
            raw = self.rfile.read(length) if length else b""
            try:
                return True, json.loads(raw or b"{}")
            except json.JSONDecodeError:
                return False, None
        def _path(self) -> tuple[str, dict[str, list[str]]]:
            parts = urlsplit(self.path)
            path = parts.path.rstrip("/") or "/"
            return path, parse_qs(parts.query)
        def _authorized(self) -> bool:
            token = self.headers.get("X-Auth-Token")
            if token and token in state.sessions.values():
                return True
            auth = self.headers.get("Authorization", "")
            if auth.startswith("Basic "):
                try:
                    user, _, pw = base64.b64decode(auth[6:]).decode().partitio
n(":")
                except ValueError:
                    return False
                return user == state.username and pw == state.password
            return False
        def _require_auth(self) -> bool:
            if self._authorized():
                return True
            self._err(401, "NoValidSession",
                      "There is no valid session established with the
implementation.",
                      {"WWW-Authenticate": 'Basic realm="mock"'})
            return False
        def _pre(self, method: str) -> tuple[str, dict[str, list[str]]] |
None:
            path, query = self._path()
            with state.lock:
                state.request_log.append((method, path))
                injected = state.fail_next.pop(0) if (method == "GET" and
state.fail_next) else None
            if state.delay_s:
                time.sleep(state.delay_s)
            if injected is not None:
                self._err(injected, "ServiceTemporarilyUnavailable",
                          "Injected fault from mock.", {"Retry-After": "0"})
                return None
            return path, query
        # ------------------------------------------------------------ verbs
        def do_GET(self) -> None:
            pre = self._pre("GET")
            if pre is None:
                return
            path, query = pre
            if path in ("/redfish", "/redfish/v1"):
                self._send(200, static[path])  # service root needs no auth
                return
            if not self._require_auth():
                return
            if path == "/redfish/v1/Systems/system":
                with state.lock:
                    self._send(200, state.system, {"ETag": state.etag()})
                return
            if path == "/redfish/v1/SessionService/Sessions":
                members = [{"@odata.id": f"{path}/{sid}"} for sid in
state.sessions]
                self._send(200, {
                    "@odata.id": path,
                    "@odata.type": "#SessionCollection.SessionCollection",
                    "Members": members, "Members@odata.count": len(members)})
                return
            if path.startswith("/redfish/v1/SessionService/Sessions/"):
                sid = path.rsplit("/", 1)[1]
                if sid in state.sessions:
                    self._send(200, {"@odata.id": path, "Id": sid,
                                     "@odata.type": "#Session.v1_6_0.Session",
                                     "UserName": state.username})
                else:
                    self._err(404, "ResourceMissingAtURI", f"The resource at
{path} was not found.")
                return
            if path == "/redfish/v1/Systems/system/LogServices/EventLog/
Entries":
                skip = int(query.get("$skip", ["0"])[0])
                page = state.log_entries[skip: skip + state.page_size]
                body: dict[str, Any] = {
                    "@odata.id": path,
                    "@odata.type": "#LogEntryCollection.LogEntryCollection",
                    "Members": [{"@odata.id": e["@odata.id"]} for e in page],
                    "Members@odata.count": len(state.log_entries),
                }
                if skip + state.page_size < len(state.log_entries):
                    body["Members@odata.nextLink"] = f"{path}?$skip={skip +
state.page_size}"
                self._send(200, body)
                return
            if path == "/redfish/v1/TaskService/Tasks":
                with state.lock:
                    members = [{"@odata.id": t["@odata.id"]} for t in
state.tasks.values()]
                self._send(200, {"@odata.id": path,
                                 "@odata.type": "#TaskCollection.TaskCollectio
n",
                                 "Members": members, "Members@odata.count": le
n(members)})
                return
            if path.startswith("/redfish/v1/Systems/system/LogServices/
EventLog/Entries/"):
                eid = path.rsplit("/", 1)[1]
                for entry in state.log_entries:
                    if entry["Id"] == eid:
                        self._send(200, {**entry, "@odata.type": "#LogEntry.v1
_15_0.LogEntry"})
                        return
                self._err(404, "ResourceMissingAtURI", f"The resource at
{path} was not found.")
                return
            if path.startswith("/redfish/v1/TaskService/Tasks/"):
                tid = path.rsplit("/", 1)[1]
                with state.lock:
                    task = state.tasks.get(tid)
                    if task is None:
                        self._err(404, "ResourceMissingAtURI", f"The resource
at {path} was not found.")
                        return
                    task["_polls"] += 1
                    if task["_polls"] >= task["_done_after"]:
                        task["TaskState"] = "Completed"
                        task["PercentComplete"] = 100
                    public = {k: v for k, v in task.items() if not
k.startswith("_")}
                self._send(200, public)
                return
            if path in static:
                self._send(200, static[path])
                return
            self._err(404, "ResourceMissingAtURI", f"The resource at {path}
was not found.")
        def do_POST(self) -> None:
            pre = self._pre("POST")
            if pre is None:
                return
            path, _ = pre
            ok, body = self._read_json()
            if path == "/redfish/v1/SessionService/Sessions":
                if not ok:
                    self._err(400, "MalformedJSON", "The request body
submitted was malformed JSON.")
                    return
                for prop in ("UserName", "Password"):
                    if prop not in body:
                        self._err(400, "PropertyMissing",
                                  f"The property {prop} is a required
property.")
                        return
                if body["UserName"] != state.username or body["Password"] !=
state.password:
                    self._err(401, "ResourceAtUriUnauthorized",
"While accessing the resource, an authentication error occurred.")
                    return
                with state.lock:
                    sid = str(next(state.session_ids))
                    token = secrets.token_hex(16)
                    state.sessions[sid] = token
                uri = f"{path}/{sid}"
                self._send(201, {"@odata.id": uri, "Id": sid,
                                 "@odata.type": "#Session.v1_6_0.Session",
                                 "UserName": state.username},
                           {"X-Auth-Token": token, "Location": uri})
                return
            if not self._require_auth():
                return
            if not ok:
                self._err(400, "MalformedJSON", "The request body submitted
was malformed JSON.")
                return
            if path == "/redfish/v1/Systems/system/Actions/
ComputerSystem.Reset":
                allowed = state.system["Actions"]["#ComputerSystem.Reset"][
                    "ResetType@Redfish.AllowableValues"]
                rtype = body.get("ResetType")
                if rtype is None:
                    self._err(400, "ActionParameterMissing",
                              "The action requires the parameter ResetType.")
                    return
                if rtype not in allowed:
                    self._err(400, "ActionParameterValueNotInList",
                              f"The value {rtype} for ResetType is not in the
list of acceptable values.")
                    return
                with state.lock:
                    tid = str(next(state.task_ids))
                    turi = f"/redfish/v1/TaskService/Tasks/{tid}"
                    state.tasks[tid] = {
                        "@odata.id": turi, "@odata.type": "#Task.v1_7_0.Task",
                        "Id": tid, "Name": f"Reset {rtype}",
                        "TaskState": "Running", "TaskStatus": "OK",
                        "PercentComplete": 0, "_polls": 0, "_done_after": 2,
                    }
                    state.system["PowerState"] = "Off" if rtype == "ForceOff"
else "On"
                    state.etag_counter += 1
                self._send(202, {"@odata.id": turi, "TaskState": "Running"},
                           {"Location": turi})
                return
            if path in static or path == "/redfish/v1/Systems/system":
                self._err(405, "ActionNotSupported", "The action POST is not
supported.",
                          {"Allow": "GET, HEAD, PATCH" if path == "/redfish/
v1/Systems/system" else "GET, HEAD"})
                return
            self._err(404, "ResourceMissingAtURI", f"The resource at {path}
was not found.")
        def do_PATCH(self) -> None:
            pre = self._pre("PATCH")
            if pre is None:
                return
            path, _ = pre
            if not self._require_auth():
                return
            if path != "/redfish/v1/Systems/system":
                if path in static:
                    self._err(405, "OperationNotAllowed", "PATCH is not
allowed on this resource.",
                              {"Allow": "GET, HEAD"})
                else:
                    self._err(404, "ResourceMissingAtURI", f"The resource at
{path} was not found.")
                return
            ok, body = self._read_json()
            if not ok:
                self._err(400, "MalformedJSON", "The request body submitted
was malformed JSON.")
                return
            if not isinstance(body, dict) or not body:
                self._err(400, "PropertyMissing", "The request body must
contain at least one property.")
                return
            if_match = self.headers.get("If-Match")
            with state.lock:
                if if_match and if_match != state.etag():
                    self._err(412, "PreconditionFailed",
                              "The ETag supplied did not match the ETag
required to change this resource.")
                    return
                writable = {"AssetTag": str, "LocationIndicatorActive": bool}
                for prop, value in body.items():
                    if prop not in state.system:
                        self._err(400, "PropertyUnknown",
                                  f"The property {prop} is not in the list of
valid properties.")
                        return
                    if prop not in writable:
                        self._err(400, "PropertyNotWritable",
                                  f"The property {prop} is a read only
property and cannot be assigned a value.")
                        return
                    if type(value) is not writable[prop]:
                        self._err(400, "PropertyValueTypeError",
                                  f"The value {value!r} for the property
{prop} is of a different type than the property can accept.")
                        return
                    if prop == "AssetTag" and len(value) > 32:  # mock-
specific limit
                        self._err(400, "PropertyValueFormatError",
                                  f"The value for the property {prop} is of a
different format than the property can accept.")
                        return
                state.system.update(body)
                state.etag_counter += 1
                snapshot = copy.deepcopy(state.system)
                etag = state.etag()
            self._send(200, snapshot, {"ETag": etag})
        def do_DELETE(self) -> None:
            pre = self._pre("DELETE")
            if pre is None:
                return
            path, _ = pre
            if not self._require_auth():
                return
            if path.startswith("/redfish/v1/SessionService/Sessions/"):
                sid = path.rsplit("/", 1)[1]
                with state.lock:
                    existed = state.sessions.pop(sid, None)
                if existed is None:
                    self._err(404, "ResourceMissingAtURI", f"The resource at
{path} was not found.")
                else:
                    self._send(204)
                return
            self._err(405, "OperationNotAllowed", "DELETE is not allowed on
this resource.",
                      {"Allow": "GET, HEAD"})
        def do_PUT(self) -> None:
            pre = self._pre("PUT")
            if pre is None:
                return
            self._err(405, "OperationNotAllowed", "PUT is not supported by
this mock.",
                      {"Allow": "GET, HEAD, PATCH"})
    return Handler
class _QuietServer(ThreadingHTTPServer):
    daemon_threads = True
    def handle_error(self, request: Any, client_address: Any) -> None:
        # A client that times out and disconnects makes our late write fail
        # with BrokenPipe/ConnectionReset. That is expected in timeout tests.
        import sys
        if isinstance(sys.exc_info()[1], ConnectionError):
            return
        super().handle_error(request, client_address)
class MockRedfishServer:
    """Start/stop helper. Use as a context manager or call start()/stop()."""
    def __init__(self, username: str = "mock_user", password: str = "mock_pass
_123",
                 host: str = "127.0.0.1", port: int = 0):
        self.state = MockState(username, password)
        self.httpd = _QuietServer((host, port), make_handler(self.state))
        self._thread = threading.Thread(target=self.httpd.serve_forever,
daemon=True)
    @property
    def base_url(self) -> str:
        host, port = self.httpd.server_address[:2]
        return f"http://{host}:{port}"
    def start(self) -> "MockRedfishServer":
        self._thread.start()
        return self
    def stop(self) -> None:
        self.httpd.shutdown()
        self.httpd.server_close()
        self._thread.join(timeout=5)
    def __enter__(self) -> "MockRedfishServer":
        return self.start()
    def __exit__(self, *exc: object) -> None:
        self.stop()
if __name__ == "__main__":
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Run the mock Redfish service")
    ap.add_argument("--port", type=int, default=8000)
    ap.add_argument("--user", default="mock_user")
    ap.add_argument("--password", default="mock_pass_123")
    args = ap.parse_args()
    srv = MockRedfishServer(args.user, args.password, port=args.port)
    print(f"Mock Redfish listening on {srv.base_url}  (Ctrl+C to stop)")
     try:
         srv.httpd.serve_forever()
     except KeyboardInterrupt:
         pass
     finally:
         srv.httpd.server_close()
```

**Warning.** The mock is not a conformant Redfish service and must never be used to claim conformance. It uses HTTP, not HTTPS, to keep the examples dependency-free.

lessons.title: pytest configuration and fixtures
lessons.body:
```code
redfish_suite/pytest.ini
 [pytest]
 pythonpath = src .
 testpaths = tests
 addopts = -ra --strict-markers
 markers =
     mock: runs against the in-process mock Redfish service (no hardware)
     live: requires a real, authorised test BMC (set RF_BASE_URL etc.)
     destructive: changes BMC state; never run against shared or production
 systems
     unit: pure unit tests with no network at all
 log_cli = false
 log_file = reports/pytest.log
 log_file_level = INFO
 log_file_format = %(asctime)s.%(msecs)03d %(levelname)s %(name)s %(message)s
 log_file_date_format = %Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S
redfish_suite/tests/conftest.py
 """Shared fixtures.
 Two target modes:
 * default  -> an in-process MockRedfishServer (no hardware needed)
 * --live   -> a real test BMC described by RF_* environment variables
 """
 from __future__ import annotations
 import os
 from collections.abc import Iterator
 import pytest
 from simulator.mock_redfish import MockRedfishServer
 from redfish_suite import RedfishClient, RedfishConfig
from redfish_suite.logging_setup import configure_logging
MOCK_USER = "mock_user"
MOCK_PASS = "mock_pass_123"  # test-only credential for the local simulator
def pytest_addoption(parser: pytest.Parser) -> None:
    parser.addoption("--live", action="store_true",
                     help="run live tests against the BMC in RF_BASE_URL")
    parser.addoption("--allow-destructive", action="store_true",
                     help="permit tests marked 'destructive' on a live BMC")
def pytest_configure(config: pytest.Config) -> None:
    os.makedirs("reports", exist_ok=True)
    configure_logging("reports/redfish_suite.jsonl")
def pytest_collection_modifyitems(config: pytest.Config, items: list[pytest.It
em]) -> None:
    live = config.getoption("--live")
    destructive_ok = config.getoption("--allow-destructive")
    skip_live = pytest.mark.skip(reason="live BMC tests need --live and RF_*
variables")
    skip_destr = pytest.mark.skip(reason="destructive test: pass --allow-
destructive")
    for item in items:
        if "live" in item.keywords and not live:
            item.add_marker(skip_live)
        if live and "destructive" in item.keywords and not destructive_ok:
            item.add_marker(skip_destr)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------- mock mode
@pytest.fixture(scope="session")
def mock_server() -> Iterator[MockRedfishServer]:
    with MockRedfishServer(MOCK_USER, MOCK_PASS) as srv:
        yield srv
@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
def _reset_fault_injection(request: pytest.FixtureRequest) -> Iterator[None]:
    """Make sure one test's injected faults never leak into the next test."""
    yield
    if "mock_server" in request.fixturenames:
        srv: MockRedfishServer = request.getfixturevalue("mock_server")
        srv.state.fail_next.clear()
        srv.state.delay_s = 0.0
@pytest.fixture
def mock_config(mock_server: MockRedfishServer) -> RedfishConfig:
    return RedfishConfig(
        base_url=mock_server.base_url,
        username=MOCK_USER,
        password=MOCK_PASS,
        verify=True,  # irrelevant for http:// but keeps the secure default
        connect_timeout=2,
        read_timeout=5,
        retries=2,
        backoff_factor=0,  # no sleeping in unit-speed tests
    )
@pytest.fixture
def rf(mock_config: RedfishConfig) -> Iterator[RedfishClient]:
    """A logged-in client against the mock. Logs out automatically."""
    with RedfishClient(mock_config) as client:
        yield client
@pytest.fixture
def system_restored(rf: RedfishClient, mock_server: MockRedfishServer) ->
Iterator[RedfishClient]:
    """Snapshot writable ComputerSystem properties and restore them
afterwards."""
    before, _ = rf.get_with_etag("/redfish/v1/Systems/system")
    saved = {k: before[k] for k in ("AssetTag", "LocationIndicatorActive")}
    yield rf
    rf.patch("/redfish/v1/Systems/system", saved)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------- live mode
@pytest.fixture(scope="session")
def live_config() -> RedfishConfig:
    return RedfishConfig.from_env()
@pytest.fixture
def live_rf(live_config: RedfishConfig) -> Iterator[RedfishClient]:
    with RedfishClient(live_config) as client:
        yield client
```

How the fixtures work together:

- mock_server (session scope) starts one mock for the whole run.

- _reset_fault_injection (autouse) clears injected faults after every test, so one test’s faults never leak into the next.

- rf gives each test a fresh logged-in client and logs out afterwards.

- system_restored snapshots writable properties and restores them in teardown — test isolation for state-changing tests.

- --live enables tests marked live; --allow-destructive additionally enables tests marked destructive. Without the flags those tests are skipped with a reason, which shows clearly in reports.

 from redfish_suite.validators import odata_type_is, validate_resource
 pytestmark = pytest.mark.mock

lessons.title: Common mistakes when building frameworks
lessons.body:
- Spreading requests calls through tests instead of one client.

- Fixtures that log in but never log out.

- Catching Exception in the client and returning None.

- Tests that depend on the mock’s exact limits and then “fail” on real hardware.

- Hiding skipped live tests — always print skip reasons (-ra).

lessons.title: Summary
lessons.body:
- A clean framework separates config, transport, domain helpers, test lifecycle and test intent.

- The client’s single request method enforces timeouts, logging, retries and error translation everywhere.

- Fixtures provide sessions, isolation and restoration; markers gate live and destructive tests.

- Mock-first development gives fast feedback; live tests are opt-in and honestly labelled.

lessons.title: What IPMI is
BMC, IPMI messages and management functions
lessons.body:
An IPMI **request** contains:

| Field | Size | Meaning |
| NetFn (Network Function) | 6 bits | Functional group of the command. Requests use even values; the response NetFn is request + 1 |
| LUN (Logical Unit Number) | 2 bits | Sub-address within the controller; usually 0 |
| Cmd | 1 byte | Command within the NetFn |
| Data | 0..n bytes | Request parameters |

A **response** contains the same NetFn+1/LUN/Cmd and data whose **first byte is the completion code**.

Common network functions **[Spec]**:

| NetFn (request) | Name | Example commands |
| 0x00 | Chassis | Get Chassis Status (0x01), Chassis Control (0x02), Get System Restart Cause (0x07), Set/Get System Boot Options (0x08/0x09) |
| 0x04 | Sensor/Event | Get Sensor Reading (0x2D), Get/Set Sensor Thresholds (0x27/0x26), Platform Event (0x02) |
| NetFn (request) | Name | Example commands |
| 0x06 | Application | Get Device ID (0x01), Cold Reset (0x02), Warm Reset (0x03), Get Self Test Results (0x04), Watchdog (0x22/0x24/0x25), Get Device GUID (0x08), Master Write-Read (0x52), user/ channel/session commands |
| 0x0A | Storage | FRU: Get Inventory Area Info (0x10), Read FRU Data (0x11); SDR: Get SDR Repository Info (0x20), Reserve SDR (0x22), Get SDR (0x23); SEL: Get SEL Info (0x40), Reserve SEL (0x42), Get SEL Entry (0x43), Clear SEL (0x47) |
| 0x0C | Transport | Get/Set LAN Configuration Parameters (0x02/0x01), SOL configuration |
| 0x2C | Group extension | Defined by other bodies (e.g. PICMG, DCMI) |
| 0x2E | OEM/Group | Vendor-specific, identified by an IANA enterprise number in the data |
| 0x30–0x3F | OEM | Vendor-specific |

source.section: 9.2 BMC, IPMI messages and management functions

lessons.title: Completion codes
lessons.body:
| Code | Meaning | Typical cause in tests |
| 0x00 | Command completed nor‐ | — mally |
| 0xC0 | Node busy | BMC overloaded; retry later |
| 0xC1 | Invalid command | Command not supported (common for optional/OEM commands) |
| 0xC2 | Command invalid for given | Wrong LUN LUN |
| 0xC3 | Timeout while processing | Internal timeout |
| command | (e.g. sensor bus) |
| 0xC7 | Request data length invalid | Too many/few data bytes |
| Code | Meaning | Typical cause in tests |
| 0xC9 | Parameter out of range | Value outside allowed range |
| 0xCB | Requested sensor, data, or | Bad sensor number / FRU |
| record not present | ID / record ID |
| 0xCC | Invalid data field in request | Field value invalid |
| 0xCE | Command response could | Generic failure not be provided |
| 0xD4 | Insufficient privilege level | Session privilege too low |
| 0xD5 | Command not supported in | e.g. during firmware up‐ |
| present state | date |
| 0xFF | Unspecified error | Generic failure |

Codes 0x01–0x7E are OEM-defined and 0x80–0xBE are command-specific (meaning depends on the command). Project 3’s fwval/protocols/ipmi.py contains this table and a describe_cc() helper.

lessons.title: In-band and out-of-band management
lessons.body:
- **In-band**: management traffic goes through the host’s own operating system and CPU. The host OS talks to the BMC over a system interface (KCS, BT, SSIF). Example: ipmitool -I open sensor list run on the server’s OS uses /dev/ipmi0. It only works while the host is running. **Out-of-band**: management traffic reaches the BMC without the host • OS — over the BMC’s network port (dedicated or shared via NC-SI). Example: ipmitool -I lanplus -H <bmc> .... It works with the host powered off, as long as the BMC has standby power.

```code
        out-of-band (LAN, RMCP+ UDP 623)
Admin PC ────────────────────────────────────────┐
                                                 ▼
┌──────────── Host ─────────────┐        ┌──── BMC ────┐
│ OS: ipmitool -I open           │  KCS/  │  ipmid      │
│      │                         │  BT/   │  (OpenBMC:  │
│  /dev/ipmi0 (ipmi_si driver)───┼─SSIF──▶│  phosphor-  │
└────────────────────────────────┘ in-band│  host-ipmid)│
                                          └─────────────┘
```

lessons.title: IPMI system interfaces
lessons.body:
| Interface | Physical path | Notes |
| KCS (Keyboard Controller | LPC/eSPI I/O ports | Most common; byte-at-a- |
| Style) | time handshake through status/data registers |
| SMIC (Server Management | I/O ports | Legacy, rarely seen |

Interface Chip)

| BT (Block Transfer) | I/O ports + buffer | Transfers whole messages; faster than KCS |
| SSIF (SMBus System Inter‐ | SMBus/I²C | Used on platforms without |
| face) | LPC (common on Arm servers) |

On Linux hosts, the ipmi_si driver handles KCS/SMIC/BT, ipmi_ssif handles SSIF and ipmi_devintf creates /dev/ipmi0. On an OpenBMC BMC, a kernel driver exposes the BMC side of the KCS/BT interface and a bridge daemon (kcsbridged, btbridged) passes messages to ipmid over D- Bus **[Impl]**.

lessons.title: KCS fundamentals
LAN-based management concepts
lessons.body:
IPMI over LAN encapsulates IPMI messages in **RMCP** (Remote Management Control Protocol, from the DMTF ASF specification) over **UDP port 623**.

- **IPMI v1.5 LAN** sessions use challenge–response authentication with MD2/MD5 or a straight password, and **no encryption**. Insecure; should be disabled.

- **IPMI v2.0 RMCP+** adds a stronger session protocol (RAKP) with negotiated authentication, integrity and confidentiality (encryption) algorithms selected by a **cipher suite**. ipmitool -I lanplus uses RMCP+.

Chapter 11 covers RMCP+ in depth. Key configuration objects:

- **Channels** — numbered communication paths (the LAN channel is often 1, but check with ipmitool channel info).

- **Users** — up to a platform-specific number of user slots per BMC, each with per-channel privilege limits.

- **LAN configuration parameters** — IP source, address, netmask, gateway, VLAN, enabled cipher suites (ipmitool lan print 1).

**Serial over LAN (SOL)** is an RMCP+ payload type that carries the host’s serial console over the network (ipmitool -I lanplus ... sol `activate).`

lessons.title: Worked example: Get Device ID
lessons.body:
Request: NetFn 0x06 (App), Cmd 0x01, no data. Response data (after the completion code) **[Spec]**:

| Byte | Field | Notes |
| 1 | Device ID | 0x00 = unspecified |
| 2 | Device Revision | bit 7: provides Device SDRs; bits 3:0: revision |
| 3 | Firmware Revision 1 | bit 7: 1 = device firmware/ SDR update or self-init in progress; bits 6:0: major version (binary) |
| 4 | Firmware Revision 2 | minor version, BCD |
| 5 | IPMI Version | BCD, bits 7:4 = minor digit, bits 3:0 = major digit; 0x02 = 2.0 |
| 6 | Additional Device Support | bitmask (sensor device, SDR repository, SEL, FRU, IPMB, chassis, …) |
| 7–9 | Manufacturer ID | IANA enterprise number, 20 bits, least significant byte first |
| 10–11 | Product ID | least significant byte first |
| 12–15 | Auxiliary Firmware Revision | optional, vendor-defined |

Decoding with Project 3’s parser:

```code
  from fwval.protocols.ipmi import parse_device_id
  data = bytes([0x20, 0x81, 0x02, 0x15, 0x02, 0xBF, 0x57, 0x01, 0x00, 0x34,
  0x12])
  dev = parse_device_id(data)
  print(dev)
# DeviceId(device_id=32, device_revision=1, provides_sdrs=True,
device_available=True,
#          firmware_major=2, firmware_minor=15, ipmi_version='2.0',
#          manufacturer_id=343, product_id=4660)
```

The bytes above are an illustrative example, not captured from a device. The decoding logic is covered by unit tests in Project 3.

lessons.title: Raw commands with ipmitool
lessons.body:
ipmitool raw <netfn> <cmd> [data...] sends any command and prints the response data bytes (without the completion code) when the completion code is 0x00. On a non-zero code it prints an error that includes rsp=0x.. and exits non-zero.

```code
$ ipmitool -I lanplus -H bmc.example.test -U automation -E -C 17 raw 0x06 0x01
```

lessons.title: Sensors and SDRs
lessons.body:
Each sensor is described by a **Sensor Data Record (SDR)**. A Full Sensor Record (type 0x01) holds the sensor number, type, units, thresholds and the **conversion formula** from the raw reading byte to a real value:

```code
y = L[(M × x + B × 10^K1) × 10^K2] units
```

where x is the raw reading, M, B, K1, K2 come from the SDR and L is a linearisation function (often linear). That is why **Get Sensor Reading** (NetFn 0x04, Cmd 0x2D) alone is not enough: it returns a raw byte plus status bits; ipmitool sensor and ipmitool sdr read the SDRs to convert and label it.

Threshold sensors have up to six thresholds: lower/upper non-critical (lnc/unc), critical (lcr/ucr) and non-recoverable (lnr/unr). **Discrete** sensors (power supply presence, OS boot status) report states as bits.

lessons.title: FRU inventory
lessons.body: **FRU** data describes replaceable parts: chassis, board and product areas with manufacturer, product name, serial and part numbers. The format is defined by the Platform Management FRU Information Storage Definition specification. FRU 0 is usually the main board/BMC. Access via Storage commands Get FRU Inventory Area Info (0x10) and Read FRU Data (0x11), or simply ipmitool fru print 0.

lessons.title: Chassis operations
lessons.body:
Chassis Control (NetFn 0x00, Cmd 0x02) data byte **[Spec]**:

**Value Action ipmitool** 0x00 Power down (hard off) chassis power off 0x01 Power up chassis power on 0x02 Power cycle chassis power cycle 0x03 Hard reset chassis power reset 0x04 Pulse diagnostic interrupt chassis power diag 0x05 Initiate soft shutdown via ACPI chassis power soft

Get Chassis Status (Cmd 0x01) returns the current power state byte (bit 0 = power on, bit 1 = overload, bit 3 = power fault, bits 6:5 = power-restore policy), the last power event and miscellaneous chassis state.

lessons.title: System Event Log
lessons.body: The **SEL** stores events (threshold crossings, power events, firmware progress) with a timestamp, generator ID, sensor type and number, and event data. Tests often check that an action produced the expected SEL entry. ipmitool sel elist prints entries with sensor names resolved through SDRs. **sel clear is destructive** — only on test systems, and save the log first.

lessons.title: IPMI versus Redfish
lessons.body:
| Aspect | IPMI | Redfish |
| Standard body | Intel/HP/NEC/Dell pro‐ | DMTF moters |
| Aspect | IPMI | Redfish |
| Encoding | Binary NetFn/Cmd/data | JSON over HTTPS |
| Transport (remote) | RMCP+ over UDP 623 | HTTPS over TCP 443 |
| In-band | KCS/BT/SSIF | Redfish Host Interface (USB NIC) |
| Security | RMCP+ RAKP (known weak‐ | TLS, sessions, roles, mod‐ |
| nesses) | ern auth |
| Discovery | Fixed commands; SDR re‐ | Hypermedia from |
| pository | /redfish/v1/ |
| Extensibility | OEM NetFns / commands | Oem sections, new schemas |
| Data model breadth | Sensors, FRU, SEL, chassis, | Everything plus storage, |
| users, LAN | networking, telemetry, composition |
| Evolution | Effectively frozen | Actively developed |
| Tooling | ipmitool, freeipmi, pyghmi | curl, any HTTP library, DMTF tools |

On OpenBMC both are front ends over the same D-Bus state, so the same sensor or power state should agree across both — a useful cross-check (Project 3 does this).

lessons.title: IPMI version and implementation considerations
lessons.body:
- Many commands are **optional**. A missing command returns 0xC1; that is not a bug unless your requirements need it.

- Vendors add **OEM commands** and OEM completion codes; their meaning is in vendor documentation, not the IPMI spec.

- Default user slot numbering, the LAN channel number and enabled cipher suites differ by platform.

- Sensor numbers and names come from platform configuration; never hard-code them across platforms.

- OpenBMC implements IPMI in phosphor-host-ipmid (ipmid) for in-band and phosphor-net-ipmid (netipmid) for RMCP+, with command handlers provided by libraries (including OEM libraries) **[Impl]**.

lessons.title: Common mistakes
lessons.body:
- Treating 0xC1 on an optional command as a firmware bug.

- Hard-coding sensor numbers, FRU IDs or LAN channel numbers.

- Converting raw sensor bytes without the SDR factors.

- Clearing the SEL before saving it.

- Running in-band commands from the host when the host IPMI driver is not loaded.

lessons.title: Exercises
lessons.body:
1. Decode IPMI version byte 0x51 and 0x02.

2. A response to NetFn 0x0A Cmd 0x11 has completion code 0xCB. What does it mean?

3. Why does ipmitool -I open fail on a powered-off host while -I lanplus works?

**Solutions.**

1. 0x51: major digit = low nibble 1, minor digit = high nibble 5 → IPMI 1.5. 0x02 → 2.0.

2. Read FRU Data: the requested FRU device (ID) is not present.

3. -I open uses the in-band system interface through the host OS; with the host off there is no OS. -I lanplus reaches the BMC over its own network port on standby power.

lessons.title: Summary
lessons.body:
- IPMI messages are NetFn/LUN/Cmd/data; responses start with a completion code.

- In-band uses KCS/BT/SSIF from the host OS; out-of-band uses RMCP+ over UDP 623.

- SDRs describe sensors, SEL records events, FRU stores inventory.

- Many commands are optional or OEM; never assume universal support.

- Redfish is the modern successor; both expose the same underlying state on OpenBMC.

lessons.title: Using standard IPMI utilities where available
lessons.body:
| Tool | What it is | Notes |
| ipmitool | The classic CLI | Interfaces: open (in-band / dev/ipmi0), lan (1.5), lanplus (2.0 RMCP+), others |
| FreeIPMI (ipmi-sensors, | GNU suite of tools | Different output formats; |
| ipmi-sel, ipmipower, bmc- | good for cross-checking |

```code
info…)
```

| pyghmi | Pure-Python IPMI LAN lib‐ | Avoids subprocess; check |
| rary | maintenance status and feature coverage for your needs |

**Command-line tools wrap different transports and implementa‐ tions.** The same ipmitool sensor list may go through the Linux kernel driver (-I open) or be built into RMCP+ packets by ipmitool itself (-I lanplus). Output formats vary between tool versions, and a command that works on one platform may return 0xC1 or different fields on another. Every parser you write must be checked against the actual tool version and platform, and must fail loudly on output it does not understand.

Installing:

```code
$ sudo apt install ipmitool         # Debian/Ubuntu
$ sudo dnf install ipmitool         # Fedora/RHEL
# macOS: brew install ipmitool ; Windows: use WSL or a Linux jump host
```

lessons.title: Executing commands and interpreting output
lessons.body:
A practice harness is provided: examples/fake_tools/ipmitool is a **fake ip‐ mitool** that prints synthetic output in the shape of the real tool, so you can practise without a BMC. Its source is in the appendix project index; the important part is that it behaves like a real CLI: it writes to stdout/ stderr and returns exit codes.

The wrapper and parsers:

```code
examples/ch10_ipmi_cli.py
 """Chapter 10: driving an IPMI command-line tool safely from Python.
 By default this uses examples/fake_tools/ipmitool (synthetic output) so it
 runs anywhere. Point IPMITOOL at a real ipmitool binary and set real
 connection details to use it against an AUTHORISED test BMC.
 """
 from __future__ import annotations
 import os
 import subprocess
 import sys
 from dataclasses import dataclass
 from pathlib import Path
 FAKE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "fake_tools" / "ipmitool"
 IPMITOOL = os.environ.get("IPMITOOL", f"{sys.executable} {FAKE}")
 class IpmiToolError(RuntimeError):
     def __init__(self, msg: str, returncode: int | None, stderr: str):
         super().__init__(msg)
         self.returncode, self.stderr = returncode, stderr
 @dataclass
 class IpmiTool:
     host: str
     user: str
     password: str
 # passed via the environment, never on the command line
     interface: str = "lanplus"
     cipher_suite: int = 17
    timeout_s: float = 15.0
    def run(self, *cmd: str) -> str:
        argv = IPMITOOL.split() + ["-I", self.interface, "-H", self.host,
                                   "-U", self.user, "-E", "-C", str(self.ciphe
r_suite), *cmd]
        env = {**os.environ, "IPMI_PASSWORD": self.password}
        try:
            proc = subprocess.run(argv, capture_output=True, text=True,
                                  timeout=self.timeout_s, env=env,
check=False)
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired as exc:
            raise IpmiToolError(f"'{' '.join(cmd)}' timed out after {self.time
out_s}s",
                                None, "") from exc
        if proc.returncode != 0:
            raise IpmiToolError(f"'{' '.join(cmd)}' failed: {proc.stderr.strip
()}",
                                proc.returncode, proc.stderr)
        return proc.stdout
def parse_colon_block(text: str) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Parse 'Key : Value' lines (mc info, fru print)."""
    out = {}
    for line in text.splitlines():
        key, sep, value = line.partition(":")
        if sep:
            out[key.strip()] = value.strip()
    return out
def parse_sensor_list(text: str) -> list[dict[str, str | float | None]]:
    """Parse 'ipmitool sensor' pipe-separated output (10 columns)."""
    cols = ["name", "value", "unit", "status", "lnr", "lcr", "lnc", "unc", "uc
r", "unr"]
    rows = []
    for line in text.splitlines():
        parts = [p.strip() for p in line.split("|")]
        if len(parts) != len(cols):
            continue  # skip anything we do not understand rather than guess
        row: dict[str, str | float | None] = dict(zip(cols, parts,
strict=True))
        for k in ("value", "lnr", "lcr", "lnc", "unc", "ucr", "unr"):
            v = row[k]
            try:
                row[k] = float(v) if v not in ("na", "") else None  # type:
ignore[arg-type]
            except ValueError:
                pass  # discrete sensors report hex strings like 0x0
        rows.append(row)
    return rows
def check_thresholds(sensors) -> list[str]:
    problems = []
    for s in sensors:
        v = s["value"]
        if s["unit"] == "discrete":
            continue
        if v is None:
            problems.append(f"{s['name']}: no reading (status {s['status']})")
            continue
        if s["ucr"] is not None and v >= s["ucr"]:
            problems.append(f"{s['name']}: {v} >= upper critical {s['ucr']}")
        if s["lcr"] is not None and v <= s["lcr"]:
            problems.append(f"{s['name']}: {v} <= lower critical {s['lcr']}")
    return problems
if __name__ == "__main__":
    bmc = IpmiTool(host="bmc.lab.example.test", user="automation", password="e
xample-only")
    info = parse_colon_block(bmc.run("mc", "info"))
    print("mc info   -> firmware", info["Firmware Revision"], "| IPMI", info["
IPMI Version"])
    fru = parse_colon_block(bmc.run("fru", "print", "0"))
    print("fru 0     -> board serial", fru["Board Serial"])
    sensors = parse_sensor_list(bmc.run("sensor", "list"))
    print(f"sensors   -> {len(sensors)} parsed; problems:",
check_thresholds(sensors))
    print("raw 06 01 ->", bmc.run("raw", "0x06", "0x01").split())
    for label, tool, args in [
        ("invalid raw cmd", bmc, ("raw", "0x06", "0xfe")),
        ("missing FRU id", bmc, ("fru", "print", "7")),
        ("wrong password", IpmiTool("bmc.lab.example.test", "automation", "wro
ng"), ("mc", "info")),
        ("unreachable BMC", IpmiTool("hang.example.test", "automation", "x",
timeout_s=1), ("mc", "info")),
    ]:
        try:
            tool.run(*args)
        except IpmiToolError as exc:
            print(f"{label:<16}-> rc={exc.returncode} {exc}")
```

lessons.title: Managing subprocess execution safely
lessons.body:
Rules applied in IpmiTool.run():

1. **Pass an argument list, never a shell string.** subprocess.run([...]) without shell=True means no shell parses the arguments, so a hostname containing ; or spaces cannot inject commands.

2. **Keep secrets out of argv.** Command-line arguments are visible to other users via ps and often end up in CI logs. ipmitool -E reads the password from the IPMI_PASSWORD environment variable; -f <file> reads it from a file with restricted permissions. Never use -P <password> in automation.

3. **Always set timeout=.** An unreachable BMC can make a tool wait for a long time while it retries UDP packets. subprocess.TimeoutExpired is raised and the child is killed.

4. **Capture stdout and stderr separately** (capture_output=True, text=True) — errors go to stderr and must be logged and parsed.

5. **check=False and inspect returncode yourself**, so you can build a useful exception containing stderr instead of a bare CalledProcessError.

6. **Log the command safely** — log the arguments without secrets (shlex.join() on the list once secrets are removed).

```code
import shlex
safe = [a for a in argv]                       # argv contains no password
when -E is used
log.info("running: %s", shlex.join(safe))
```

lessons.title: Timeouts, exit codes and error handling
lessons.body:
Classify failures into three groups, because they lead to different actions:

| Group | How it shows | Meaning | Test outcome |
| Transport/session | Non-zero exit, | Could not talk to | Error (infrastruc‐ |
| failure | stderr like “Unable | the BMC | ture) — not a |
| to establish IPMI | product verdict on |
| v2 / RMCP+ ses‐ | the command sion”, or timeout |
| Command rejected | Non-zero exit, | The BMC answered | Pass or fail depend‐ |
| stderr contains | with a completion | ing on what the test |
| rsp=0x.. | code | expects |
| Command suc‐ | Exit 0, data on | — | Validate the data |
| ceeded | stdout |

Project 3’s real adapter implements exactly this classification:

```code
fwval/fwval/adapters/real.py
 class IpmitoolIpmi:
     """Wraps the ipmitool CLI (must be installed on the test host).
     The password is passed through the IPMI_PASSWORD environment variable and
     ipmitool's -E option, so it never appears in the process list or logs.
     """
     def __init__(self, host: str, username: str, password: str, interface:
 str = "lanplus",
                  cipher_suite: int | None = 17, timeout_s: float = 20.0,
                  ipmitool: str = "ipmitool"):
         self.base = [ipmitool, "-I", interface, "-H", host, "-U", username, "-
 E"]
         if cipher_suite is not None:
             self.base += ["-C", str(cipher_suite)]
         self.env = {**os.environ, "IPMI_PASSWORD": password}
         self.timeout_s = timeout_s
     def raw(self, netfn: int, cmd: int, data: bytes = b"") ->
 ipmi.IpmiResponse:
         args = self.base + ["raw", f"0x{netfn:02x}", f"0x{cmd:02x}", *[f"0x{b:
 02x}" for b in data]]
         try:
             proc = subprocess.run(args, capture_output=True, text=True,
                                   timeout=self.timeout_s, env=self.env,
 check=False)
         except FileNotFoundError as exc:
             raise InterfaceError("ipmitool not found on PATH") from exc
         except subprocess.TimeoutExpired as exc:
             raise InterfaceTimeout(f"ipmitool raw {netfn:#x} {cmd:#x} timed
 out") from exc
         if proc.returncode == 0:
             return ipmi.IpmiResponse(0x00,
 ipmi.parse_ipmitool_raw(proc.stdout))
         match = _RSP.search(proc.stderr)
         if match:  # the BMC answered with a non-zero completion code
             return ipmi.IpmiResponse(int(match.group(1), 16), b"")
         # No completion code: session/transport/authentication problem.
         raise InterfaceError(f"ipmitool failed (exit {proc.returncode}):
 {proc.stderr.strip()}")
     def close(self) -> None:
         pass
```

And its behaviour is pinned by offline tests that replace subprocess.run:

```code
fwval/tests/test_real_adapters_offline.py
 def test_ipmitool_success_parsed(monkeypatch):
     seen = {}
     def fake_run(args, **kw):
         seen["args"], seen["env"] = args, kw["env"]
         return FakeCompleted(0, " 20 81 02 15 02 bf a0 a0 00 01 00\n")
     monkeypatch.setattr(subprocess, "run", fake_run)
     resp = IpmitoolIpmi("bmc.example.test", "u", "pw").raw(0x06, 0x01)
     assert resp.ok and resp.data[0] == 0x20
     assert "pw" not in seen["args"]            # password not on command line
     assert seen["env"]["IPMI_PASSWORD"] == "pw"
     assert seen["args"][-3:] == ["raw", "0x06", "0x01"]
 def test_ipmitool_completion_code_extracted(monkeypatch):
     err =
 ("Unable to send RAW command (channel=0x0 netfn=0x6 lun=0x0 cmd=0xfe
 rsp=0xc1): "
            "Invalid command\n")
     monkeypatch.setattr(subprocess, "run", lambda a, **k: FakeCompleted(1,
 "", err))
     resp = IpmitoolIpmi("h", "u", "p").raw(0x06, 0xFE)
     assert resp.completion_code == 0xC1
 def test_ipmitool_session_failure_raises(monkeypatch):
     err = "Error: Unable to establish IPMI v2 / RMCP+ session\n"
     monkeypatch.setattr(subprocess, "run", lambda a, **k: FakeCompleted(1,
 "", err))
     with pytest.raises(InterfaceError, match="RMCP"):
         IpmitoolIpmi("h", "u", "p").raw(0x06, 0x01)
```

**Note.** The exact wording of ipmitool error messages varies between versions. The parser above relies only on the rsp=0x.. token, which appears in raw-command failures in the ipmitool versions the author is aware of; verify on yours.

lessons.title: Parsing command output
lessons.body:
Three output shapes cover most needs:

1. **Key : value blocks** (mc info, fru print, lan print) — split each line on the first colon. Keys can repeat in fru print for multiple FRUs; parse per FRU section if you request all.

2. **Pipe-separated tables** (sensor list has 10 columns; sdr list has 3; sel list has 6). Split on |, strip, check the column count, skip lines you do not understand rather than guessing.

3. **Hex byte lists** (raw) — split on whitespace and convert with int(x, 16); may span lines.

When possible, prefer **raw commands plus your own decoder** for the fields that matter most (as with Get Device ID and Get Chassis Status in Project 3). Raw bytes are defined by the IPMI specification; tool output formatting is not.

lessons.title: Sensor, FRU, chassis and device-information tests
lessons.body:
Representative tests (written against the abstract IPMI port from Project 3, so they run against the simulator and, unchanged, against a real BMC via ipmitool):

```code
fwval/tests/test_smoke.py
 def test_ipmi_get_device_id(ipmi):
     resp = ipmi.raw(ipmi_proto.NETFN_APP, ipmi_proto.APP_GET_DEVICE_ID)
     resp.raise_for_cc("Get Device ID")
     dev = ipmi_proto.parse_device_id(resp.data)
     assert dev.ipmi_version == "2.0"
     assert dev.device_available
fwval/tests/test_power_cycle.py
def ipmi_power_on(ipmi) -> bool:
    resp = ipmi.raw(ipmi_proto.NETFN_CHASSIS, ipmi_proto.CHASSIS_GET_STATUS)
    resp.raise_for_cc("Get Chassis Status")
    return ipmi_proto.parse_chassis_status(resp.data).power_on
def test_redfish_off_is_seen_by_ipmi_and_ssh(powered_on, redfish, ipmi, ssh):
    redfish.reset("ForceOff")
    wait_for(lambda: not ipmi_power_on(ipmi), 60, what="IPMI to report power
off")
    assert "PowerState.Off" in ssh.run("obmcutil state").stdout
```

Sensor checks with the CLI wrapper:

```code
import pytest
from ch10_ipmi_cli import IpmiTool, parse_sensor_list, check_thresholds
REQUIRED = {"CPU0 Temp", "Inlet Temp", "FAN0"}        # from the platform spec
@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
def ipmitool() -> IpmiTool:
    import os
    return IpmiTool(host=os.environ["BMC_HOST"], user=os.environ["IPMI_USER"],
                    password=os.environ["IPMI_PASSWORD"])
@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
def sensors(ipmitool: IpmiTool):
    return parse_sensor_list(ipmitool.run("sensor", "list"))
def test_required_sensors_present(sensors):
    names = {s["name"] for s in sensors}
    assert REQUIRED <= names, f"missing: {REQUIRED - names}"
def test_no_threshold_violations(sensors):
    assert check_thresholds([s for s in sensors if s["name"] in REQUIRED]) ==
[]
```

Against the fake tool, the full sensor list includes FAN3 with no reading, which check_thresholds reports — demonstrating that the check catches “na” values. Whether “no reading” is a failure depends on the platform (an unpopulated fan header legitimately reads na), which is why the test restricts itself to required sensors.

FRU tests typically assert presence and format of serial/part numbers; device tests assert IPMI version, firmware version consistency with Redfish, and that the device is available (not in update mode).

lessons.title: Regression test design
lessons.body:
- **Pin the tool version** on CI agents (ipmitool -V logged at start). Output format changes break parsers.

- **Separate infrastructure errors from product failures**: a session failure should mark the run as error, not as N failed commands.

- **Data-driven command coverage**: a table of (netfn, cmd, data, expected_cc) rows parametrised into one test; extend it as features are added.

- **Cross-interface consistency**: power state via IPMI vs Redfish; firmware version via Get Device ID vs Redfish Manager vs /etc/os-release.

- **Golden data with tolerance**: FRU strings compared exactly; sensor values within plausible ranges, never exact.

- **Run order independence**: power tests restore power state in a fixture.

- **Rate limiting**: insert small delays in loops; BMC IPMI stacks have limited session slots.

lessons.title: Capturing command output and diagnostic logs
lessons.body:
For every IPMI call, record: timestamp, argv (without secrets), exit code, duration, stdout and stderr. On failure, also capture sel elist, sdr elist (sensor state), mc info, and — via SSH — the BMC journal for ipmid/ netipmid. Project 2’s diagnostic tool (Chapter 23) shows the artifact-store pattern for this.

For protocol-level debugging, ipmitool -v (repeat for more verbosity) prints session and packet details, and a packet capture of UDP port 623 can be decoded by Wireshark’s IPMI/RMCP dissectors. Capture only on networks you are authorised to monitor; captures can contain sensitive session material.

lessons.title: Common mistakes
lessons.body:
- Passing the password with -P, visible in ps and CI logs.

- shell=True with string formatting of host names.

- No timeout on subprocess.run.

- Treating a session failure as a command failure.

- Parsers that silently accept unexpected output.

- Assuming sensor names, numbers or counts are the same on every platform.

lessons.title: Exercises
lessons.body:
1. Extend parse_sensor_list to return discrete-sensor states as integers.

2. Write a test that runs chassis power status and maps the text to a boolean, failing loudly on unexpected text.

3. Add retry-on-session-failure (max 2) to IpmiTool.run() without retrying commands that returned a completion code.

**Solutions.**

1. For rows with unit == "discrete", convert value and status with int(v, 16) when they start with 0x. 2.

```code
def power_is_on(text: str) -> bool:
    text = text.strip()
    if text == "Chassis Power is on":
        return True
    if text == "Chassis Power is off":
        return False
    raise AssertionError(f"unexpected chassis power output: {text!r}")
```

1. In run(), loop for attempt in range(3); on IpmiToolError whose stderr lacks rsp= (transport/session error) or on timeout, log and retry after a short sleep; if stderr contains rsp= re-raise immediately. Remember that retrying a state- changing command after a timeout has the same ambiguity as HTTP POST — check state first.

lessons.title: Summary
lessons.body:
- Wrap IPMI tools with argument lists, environment-passed secrets, timeouts and separate stdout/stderr.

- Classify outcomes as transport failure, completion-code rejection or success.

- Parse defensively; prefer raw bytes for important fields.

- Make tests platform-aware and cross-check against Redfish.

lessons.title: RMCP and RMCP+ fundamentals
lessons.body:
**RMCP** (Remote Management Control Protocol) is a simple UDP-based protocol defined by DMTF’s ASF specification. An RMCP packet has a 4-byte header (version, reserved, sequence number, class of message). The class says what follows — for example an ASF message (used by RMCP ping/pong presence detection) or an IPMI message.

IPMI over LAN puts an **IPMI session header** and the IPMI message inside RMCP:

```code
UDP/623 ─▶ RMCP header (class = IPMI)
            └─▶ IPMI session header
                 IPMI v1.5:  auth type, session seq, session ID, [auth code],
length
                 IPMI v2.0:  auth type = RMCP+ (0x06), payload type (+
encrypted/
                             authenticated flags), session ID, session seq,
length
                 └─▶ payload: IPMI message (or SOL data, or session set-up
messages)
                 └─▶ [integrity trailer: padding, next header, AuthCode]
```

**RMCP+** (IPMI v2.0) extends this with payload types (IPMI messages, SOL, session set-up messages, OEM payloads) and per-packet encryption and integrity.

lessons.title: Session establishment concepts
lessons.body:
An RMCP+ session is set up with this sequence **[Spec]**:

```code
Client (ipmitool -I lanplus)                         BMC
  │ Get Channel Authentication Capabilities ─────────▶ │  what auth/RMCP+
supported?
  │ ◀──────────────────────────────── capabilities ─── │
  │ RMCP+ Open Session Request ──────────────────────▶ │  proposes auth/
integrity/
  │   (requested max privilege, algorithm proposals)   │  confidentiality
algorithms
  │ ◀────────────────────── Open Session Response ──── │  accepts or rejects
  │ RAKP Message 1 (client random, user name, role) ─▶ │
  │ ◀───────── RAKP Message 2 (BMC random, GUID, HMAC) │
  │ RAKP Message 3 (HMAC proving client knows key) ──▶ │
  │ ◀────────────────── RAKP Message 4 (integrity) ─── │  session keys derived
  │ Set Session Privilege Level ─────────────────────▶ │
  │ ... authenticated/encrypted IPMI commands ...      │
  │ Close Session ───────────────────────────────────▶ │
```

**RAKP** (Remote Authenticated Key-Exchange Protocol) authenticates both sides with a key derived from the user’s password and produces session keys for integrity and encryption. A generic diagnostic consequence: if a session fails, which step fails tells you why — an Open Session rejection points to unsupported algorithms (cipher suite) or privilege; a RAKP failure points to the user name, password or role.

lessons.title: Authentication, integrity and confidentiality
lessons.body:
RMCP+ negotiates three independent algorithms:

| Function | Purpose | Algorithms in IPMI v2.0 (examples) |
| Authentication (RAKP) | Prove identities during set- | none, HMAC-SHA1, HMAC- |
| up | MD5, HMAC-SHA256 |
| Function | Purpose | Algorithms in IPMI v2.0 (examples) |
| Integrity | Detect tampering per pack‐ | none, HMAC-SHA1-96, |
| et | HMAC-MD5-128, MD5-128, HMAC-SHA256-128 |
| Confidentiality | Encrypt payloads | none, AES-CBC-128, xRC4-128, xRC4-40 |

lessons.title: Cipher suites and compatibility
lessons.body:
A **cipher suite ID** names a combination of the three. Commonly referenced IDs **[Spec]**:

| ID | Authentica‐ | Integrity | Confidential‐ | Assessment |
| tion | ity |
| 0 | none | none | none | Must be dis‐ abled — no authentication at all |
| 1 | HMAC-SHA1 | none | none | No integrity or encryption |
| 2 | HMAC-SHA1 | HMAC-SHA1-96 | none | No encryption |
| 3 | HMAC-SHA1 | HMAC-SHA1-96 | AES-CBC-128 | Widely supported legacy choice |
| 17 | HMAC-SHA256 | HMAC- | AES-CBC-128 | Preferred |
| SHA256-128 | where supported |

Compatibility notes:

- The client chooses with ipmitool -C <id>. Newer ipmitool releases default to 17; older ones defaulted to 3. If a BMC does not offer the requested suite, the Open Session step fails with a generic “Unable to establish IPMI v2 / RMCP+ session”.

- The BMC advertises which suites it supports and the maximum privilege allowed per suite in its LAN configuration (ipmitool lan print <channel> shows “RMCP+ Cipher Suites” and “Cipher Suite Priv Max”).

- OpenBMC’s netipmid supports a configured subset (commonly including 17 and 3) **[Impl]**; check your build’s configuration.

lessons.title: Privilege levels
lessons.body:
| Level | Value | Typical allowed opera‐ tions |
| Callback | 1 | Very limited (legacy callback) |
| User | 2 | Read-only: sensors, FRU, SEL read, Get Device ID |
| Operator | 3 | Most configuration-free control: chassis power control, SEL clear on some platforms |
| Administrator | 4 | Everything: users, LAN settings, firmware |
| OEM | 5 | Vendor-defined |

Effective privilege = min(user’s channel privilege limit, session’s requested level, cipher suite’s privilege maximum). ipmitool requests a level with -L (default Administrator for lanplus in many versions); requesting more than allowed makes the session fail or produces 0xD4 on privileged commands.

Least privilege in automation: monitoring jobs use a **User**-level account; power-control jobs use **Operator**; only provisioning jobs use **Adminis‐ trator**.

lessons.title: Network reachability and session failures
lessons.body:
Because RMCP+ uses UDP, a firewall that drops UDP 623 produces silence: ipmitool retries and finally reports a session failure after its timeout. There is no “connection refused” signal to help you.

Troubleshooting sequence:

1. **Is the BMC reachable at all?** HTTPS port: nc -vz -w 3 bmc 443. If that fails, fix basic networking first.

2. **Is IPMI over LAN enabled?** Many hardened BMCs disable it. Check

```code
via Redfish Managers/<id>/NetworkProtocol → IPMI.ProtocolEnabled, or
```

BMC configuration.

3. **Is UDP 623 reachable?** A UDP port scan is unreliable; better, run ipmitool -I lanplus ... -v mc info and look at where it stops, or capture with tcpdump -nn udp port 623 on your side to see whether replies arrive.

4. **Cipher suite**: try -C 17, then -C 3.

5. **Credentials and privilege**: confirm user is enabled for the LAN channel and has IPMI access (some BMCs separate web and IPMI access per user); try -L USER.

6. **Session slots**: BMCs support a limited number of concurrent RMCP+ sessions; crashed scripts that never closed sessions can exhaust them until timeouts free them.

7. BMC side logs: journalctl -u phosphor-ipmi-net@<interface> (unit names vary) on OpenBMC.

| Message (typical) | Likely cause |
| “Unable to establish IPMI v2 / RMCP+ ses‐ | Algorithm/cipher mismatch, IPMI disabled, |
| sion” quickly | wrong user/password |
| Same message after a long delay | No replies at all: UDP blocked, wrong IP, IPMI service down |
| “Insufficient privilege level” / CC 0xD4 | User or cipher suite privilege limit |
| “Invalid user name” or RAKP-related errors | Unknown user, or user not enabled for |
| (wording varies) | LAN |
| Works with -C 3 but not -C 17 | BMC lacks suite 17 |

lessons.title: Secure testing practices
lessons.body:
- Use **dedicated automation accounts** with the least privilege needed; never share the factory admin account.

- Pass passwords via -E/environment or protected files, injected by the CI secret store; rotate them.

- Prefer **Redfish** for anything Redfish can do; enable IPMI over LAN only where a requirement needs it.

- Keep management networks isolated (separate VLAN, ACLs). IPMI traffic should never be exposed to the Internet.

- Close sessions; do not run unbounded parallel IPMI jobs against one BMC.

- Treat packet captures and SEL/FRU dumps as sensitive data.
