Unit tests cover every outcome: success, refused when not allowed, failed task, hanging task (bounded), device not returning, wrong version after update.

On real hardware, collect for a failed update: the task’s messages, BMC journal (software manager service), console across the reboot, image name/version/SHA-256, the MANIFEST/version metadata, and the Redfish firmware inventory before and after.

lessons.title: Rollback and recovery concepts
lessons.body:
- **Dual image / A-B**: many BMCs keep two images; a failed update can boot the other. Rollback tests verify switching back works.

- **Recovery path**: a “golden” image, recovery mode in the bootloader, or external programming (JTAG/flash programmer). These are platform-specific lab procedures with physical access; automate only what your platform documents and your lab owns.

- A failed update test must leave the board **identified as needing recovery** (health check fails next time; notify the lab) rather than silently reused.

lessons.title: Preserving logs and metadata
lessons.body: Store with the build: UpdateReport JSON, console log, journal, inventory snapshots, image metadata, timings. Keep release-qualification evidence beyond normal build rotation.

lessons.title: Handling unavailable hardware
lessons.body: If the device is unreachable before the update: do not start (precheck fails with LAB_UNAVAILABLE). If it does not return after the update: DeviceUnavailableError from wait_until_ready, classified LAB_UNAVAILABLE, plus a recovery hint in the report. `[EXECUTED] unit test test_device_not_returning_after_update.`

lessons.title: Authorised lab-only integration (separate, deliberate step) [LAB-ONLY]
lessons.body:
RedfishAdapter deliberately does **not** implement flashing. To add it in your private lab repository:

1. Read your platform’s update documentation. For OpenBMC, start with the code-update architecture document in the openbmc/docs repository: it describes image tarballs with a MANIFEST, version IDs, activation, and that Redfish uploads return a task to monitor, with reboot behaviour depending on ApplyTime.

2. Agree a recovery procedure with the lab owner **before** the first automated flash.

3. Implement start_firmware_update() using your BMC’s UpdateService (check which of HttpPushUri / MultipartHttpPushUri it advertises and the required apply-time settings) and update_status() polling the returned task.

4. Verify the image checksum first; refuse unsigned/unknown images.

5. Set allow_firmware_update: true only in the config of a device reserved for update tests.

6. Run under lock() with a dedicated credential that has the needed privilege.

7. First runs: attended, with the console captured.

lessons.title: Exercises
lessons.body:
**24.1** Add a “boot time budget” check: fail if waited_s after update exceeds 300 s. **Solution:** in the test, after orch.run, read ready step waited_s from report.steps and `assert waited <= 300, f"BMC took {waited}s to return".`

**24.2** The update task stays at 75 % for 40 minutes. What does the orchestrator do and what evidence exists? **Solution:** at update_timeout_s it raises FirmwareUpdateError("... still Running after ...s") (category FIRMWARE_REGRESSION); every status poll is in the report; the console tail is recorded in finally.

lessons.title: The adapter design
lessons.body:
```code
  tests ──► DeviceAdapter (interface)
              ├── SimulatedDevice.run_command / console_log          [EXECUTED]
              └── RedfishAdapter.run_command ──► SSHRunner (paramiko) [LAB-ONLY]
                                    UARTConsole (pyserial)            [LAB-ONLY]
Tests call device.run_command("systemctl is-system-running", timeout_s) and never import
```

paramiko or pyserial. In simulation the same test runs against canned outputs:

```code
@pytest.mark.regression
def test_bmc_os_reports_running(device, evidence_dir, etif_config):
    result = device.run_command("systemctl is-system-running",
etif_config.command_timeout_s)
    (evidence_dir / "systemctl.txt").write_text(result.stdout + result.stderr)
    assert result.exit_code == 0 and result.stdout.strip() == "running"
```

lessons.title: Running remote diagnostic commands

Useful read-only diagnostics on an OpenBMC system (availability varies by image):

lessons.title: SSH connection management
lessons.body:
From src/etif/adapters/ssh.py **[LAB-ONLY — not executed]**:

```code
self.client = paramiko.SSHClient()
self.client.load_system_host_keys()
if known_hosts:
    self.client.load_host_keys(known_hosts)
self.client.set_missing_host_key_policy(paramiko.RejectPolicy())
self.params = dict(hostname=host, port=port, username=user, password=password,
                   key_filename=key_file, timeout=connect_timeout_s,
                   banner_timeout=connect_timeout_s, auth_timeout=connect_timeout_s)
```

- RejectPolicy: unknown host keys are rejected. AutoAddPolicy would trust any impostor at that address. Add the BMC’s key to the agent’s known_hosts once, after verifying it on the console.

- Every connect phase has a timeout (TCP, banner, auth); exec_command(timeout=...) bounds the command.

- Prefer key-based auth from sshUserPrivateKey credentials; password auth only if the platform requires it.

**Note on reflashed BMCs:** a reflashed or factory-reset BMC may generate a **new host key**. The test framework must not “fix” this by disabling checks; the lab procedure updates known_hosts for that device after verification (a known-hosts file per device in the lab repository works well).

lessons.title: Serial console access concepts
lessons.body:
The UART console shows what network interfaces cannot: bootloader output, kernel panics, early boot failures, and a login when the network is down.

- Physical: USB-serial adapter on the lab agent (/dev/ttyUSB0, better /dev/serial/by-id/...) or a networked **console server**.

- Typical settings: 115200 baud, 8N1 (platform-specific).

- **One reader at a time.** A second program opening the port steals data.

- Manual access for humans: picocom -b 115200 /dev/ttyUSB0, minicom, screen. Automation must not run while a human is attached (lock it).

source.chapter: 25 UART, SSH and Remote Test Execution

lessons.title: Test execution through approved lab adapters
lessons.body: Only adapters that your lab approves, for devices you are authorised to use. The adapter interface keeps the rest of the framework identical across simulation and lab, and factory.create() is the single place where transports are chosen.

lessons.title: Capturing UART logs
lessons.body:
From src/etif/adapters/uart.py **[LAB-ONLY — not executed]**:

```code
def capture(self, seconds: float, out_file, stop_on: str | None = None) -> str:
    """Read console output for up to `seconds` (bounded), append it to out_file."""
    if self._ser is None:
        self.open()
    buf = bytearray()
    deadline = time.monotonic() + seconds
    while time.monotonic() < deadline:
        chunk = self._ser.read(4096)
        if chunk:
            buf += chunk
            if stop_on and stop_on.encode() in buf:
                break
    ...
```

Patterns:

- Start capture **before** the action that reboots the device (update, reset), stop on a marker such as login: or at a deadline.

- For long runs, a background capture process per device writing a rotating log, started and stopped by the pipeline, archived with the build.

- Timestamps on each line help correlate with test logs.

lessons.body:

lessons.title: Reconnection after reboot
lessons.body: After a reboot, existing SSH connections are dead. SSHRunner.run() marks itself disconnected on transport errors (self._connected = False), so the next call reconnects. The test must first wait for readiness (wait_until_ready), then reconnect; SSH often becomes available a little after Redfish or vice versa, so check the interface you are about to use.

lessons.body: Credentials come from Jenkins bindings (DUT_USER, DUT_PASSWORD, or an SSH key file variable); configuration files are rejected if they contain password/token/secret keys (Project 3 config.py); logs are masked.

lessons.title: Hardware resource locking
lessons.body: Lock the device, and treat the serial port as part of it (or lock it separately with extra:). Project 3 combines Jenkins lock() (cross-agent) with DeviceLock (per-machine flock, released by the kernel if the process dies). **[EXECUTED]** unit tests: a second holder times out with LockTimeoutError; a killed holder’s lock is released automatically.

lessons.title: Cleanup after failed tests
lessons.body:
- yield fixtures restore settings in finally.

- The session device fixture always writes console.log, closes connections and releases the lock (finally).

- A serial port left open blocks the next job: always close in finally.

- If cleanup itself fails, report it (it is an error) and let the next health check decide.

lessons.title: Handling an unreachable device
lessons.body:
**[EXECUTED]** simulator fault unreachable:

```code
E       etif.errors.DeviceUnavailableError: sim-bmc-01 not ready after 5s (last error:
never reachable)
  6  LAB_UNAVAILABLE        Device unreachable or reserved by another job. Owner: lab/
infra.
1 skipped, 6 errors in 5.12s
```

The session fixture fails once; pytest reuses the cached failure for every test that needs the device, so the run does not wait 5 s × 6. All six are errors (not failures) and classified as lab problems. In the pipeline, the pre-flight python -m etif.diagnostics catches this earlier (exit 10) and the device tests do not run.

lessons.title: Exercises
lessons.body:
**25.1** Design a test that verifies the BMC console shows login: within 300 s after a

```code
reset. Solution: @pytest.mark.hardware_only + lock; start UARTConsole.capture(seconds=300,
out_file=evidence_dir/'console.log', stop_on='login:') in a thread, trigger reboot_bmc(),

lessons.title: Practical comparisons
lessons.body:
- **Firmware regression vs test change:** rerun the same test commit on the previous firmware (and the previous test commit on the new firmware). The combination that flips the result identifies the cause.

- **Infra vs product:** infra failures cluster in time and across unrelated tests; product failures stick to specific functionality and reproduce.

- **Agent vs device:** if the agent disconnected, the device may be fine; if the device stopped answering, the agent’s other jobs are fine.

lessons.title: src/sensortools/cli.py
lessons.body:
```code
"""Command-line entry point: python -m sensortools.cli <file>"""
from __future__ import annotations
import argparse
import sys
from .parser import SensorParseError, parse_text
from .thresholds import Threshold, evaluate_all
DEFAULT_THRESHOLDS = {
    "CPU0_Temp": Threshold(upper_critical=95.0),
    "CPU1_Temp": Threshold(upper_critical=95.0),
    "P12V": Threshold(lower_critical=11.4, upper_critical=12.6),
}
def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Check sensor readings against thresholds")
    ap.add_argument("file", help="text file with 'name | value | unit | status' lines")
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
    try:
        with open(args.file, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            readings = parse_text(fh.read())
    except (OSError, SensorParseError) as exc:
        print(f"ERROR: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    results = evaluate_all(readings, DEFAULT_THRESHOLDS)
    for name, state in sorted(results.items()):
        print(f"{name:<12} {state}")
    return 1 if "critical" in results.values() else 0
if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())
```

```code
# p1-sensor-ci — Python Test Automation CI Pipeline
A small, synthetic Python package (`sensortools`) that parses BMC-style sensor
readings and checks them against thresholds, plus a pytest suite and a Jenkins
pipeline. It is Project 1 of the *Git, Jenkins & CI/CD Automation Handbook*.
All data in this repository is synthetic. No employer code or logs are used.
## Layout
```
p1-sensor-ci/
├── Jenkinsfile            # Declarative pipeline: checkout → venv → pytest → reports
├── README.md
├── pytest.ini             # test paths, markers, src path
├── requirements.txt       # pinned test dependencies
├── .gitignore
├── scripts/run_tests.sh   # local pipeline, same steps as Jenkins
├── src/sensortools/       # code under test
│   ├── parser.py
│   ├── thresholds.py
│   └── cli.py
└── tests/                 # pytest suite (15 tests, 3 marked smoke)
```
## Run locally
```bash
./scripts/run_tests.sh          # full suite
./scripts/run_tests.sh smoke    # only @pytest.mark.smoke tests
```
Reports are written to `reports/`: `junit.xml`, `report.html`, `pytest-console.log`.
## pytest exit codes used by the pipeline
| Code | Meaning                         | Jenkins result |
|------|---------------------------------|----------------|
| 0    | all selected tests passed       | SUCCESS        |
| 1    | some tests failed               | UNSTABLE       |
| 2    | interrupted (incl. collection errors) | FAILURE  |
| 3    | internal error                  | FAILURE        |
| 4    | usage error (bad option)        | FAILURE        |
| 5    | no tests collected              | FAILURE        |
| 6    | warnings over `--max-warnings`  | FAILURE        |
## Jenkins setup
1. Create a **Pipeline** job (or Multibranch Pipeline) pointing at this repository,
   with *Script Path* = `Jenkinsfile`.
2. Provide an agent with label `python3` (and `linux`) that has `python3`,
   `python3-venv` and `git` installed.
3. Required plugins: Pipeline, Git, JUnit, Workspace Cleanup, Timestamper.
4. Optional: HTML Publisher, if you want the HTML report as a sidebar link.
   Without it, `report.html` is still archived as a build artifact.
## Known limitations
- The Jenkinsfile was syntax-reviewed but not executed on a Jenkins server while
  writing the handbook. The pytest suite and `scripts/run_tests.sh` were run.
- Jenkins' Content Security Policy may block the styling of archived HTML reports
  when opened from the artifact page; use `--self-contained-html` (already set)
  and see the handbook, Chapter 15.
```

lessons.title: bmcsim/backend.py
lessons.body:
```code
"""In-memory model of a BMC. Not real OpenBMC: just enough behaviour to test a pipeline.
Fault injection: set BMC_SIM_FAULTS to a comma-separated list, e.g.
    BMC_SIM_FAULTS=sensor_na,slow_root
Supported faults:
    sensor_na      - one sensor returns no reading (Reading = null)
    fan_critical   - fan sensor reports a critical value
    slow_root      - service root answers after 3 s (to exercise timeouts)
    auth_fail      - every request returns 401
    wrong_version  - firmware version differs from the expected one
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import copy
import os
import threading
DEFAULT_STATE = {
    "manager_id": "bmc",
    "system_id": "system",
    "chassis_id": "chassis",
    "firmware_version": "2.16.0-sim",
    "power_state": "On",
    "sensors": {
        "CPU0_Temp": {"Reading": 45.0, "ReadingUnits": "Cel", "UpperCritical": 95.0},
        "Inlet_Temp": {"Reading": 24.5, "ReadingUnits": "Cel", "UpperCritical": 45.0},
        "P12V": {"Reading": 12.05, "ReadingUnits": "V", "LowerCritical": 11.4, "UpperCrit
ical": 12.6},
        "FAN0": {"Reading": 5200.0, "ReadingUnits": "RPM", "LowerCritical": 1000.0},
    },
}
class SimulatedBMC:
    def __init__(self, faults: str | None = None):
        self._lock = threading.Lock()
        self.state = copy.deepcopy(DEFAULT_STATE)
        raw = faults if faults is not None else os.environ.get("BMC_SIM_FAULTS", "")
        self.faults = {f.strip() for f in raw.split(",") if f.strip()}
        self.event_log: list[str] = ["BMC simulator started"]
        if "sensor_na" in self.faults:
            self.state["sensors"]["Inlet_Temp"]["Reading"] = None
        if "fan_critical" in self.faults:
            self.state["sensors"]["FAN0"]["Reading"] = 400.0
        if "wrong_version" in self.faults:
            self.state["firmware_version"] = "2.15.9-sim"
    def log(self, msg: str) -> None:
        with self._lock:
            self.event_log.append(msg)
    def set_power(self, action: str) -> bool:
        mapping = {"On": "On", "ForceOff": "Off", "GracefulShutdown": "Off",
                   "ForceRestart": "On", "GracefulRestart": "On"}
        if action not in mapping:
            return False
        with self._lock:
            self.state["power_state"] = mapping[action]
        self.log(f"Power action {action} -> {mapping[action]}")
        return True
```

"""Start the simulator inside the current process (used by tests and scripts in sim
mode)."""
from __future__ import annotations
import threading
from http.server import ThreadingHTTPServer
from .backend import SimulatedBMC
from .server import make_handler
class SimulatorHandle:
    def __init__(self, user: str, password: str, faults: str | None = None):
        self.bmc = SimulatedBMC(faults)
        self.server = ThreadingHTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), make_handler(self.bmc, user,
password))
        self.url = f"http://127.0.0.1:{self.server.server_address[1]}"
        self._thread = threading.Thread(target=self.server.serve_forever, daemon=True)
    def __enter__(self):
        self._thread.start()
        return self
    def __exit__(self, *exc):
        self.server.shutdown()
        self.server.server_close()
        self._thread.join(timeout=5)
```

```code
"""Load target configuration. Secrets come only from environment variables."""
from __future__ import annotations
import os
from pathlib import Path
import yaml
REQUIRED = ("mode", "expected_firmware", "manager_id", "system_id", "chassis_id")
class ConfigError(Exception):
    pass
def load_config(path: str | None = None) -> dict:
    path = path or os.environ.get("TARGET_CONFIG", "config/sim.yaml")
    p = Path(path)
    if not p.is_file():
        raise ConfigError(f"config file not found: {p}")
    cfg = yaml.safe_load(p.read_text()) or {}
    missing = [k for k in REQUIRED if k not in cfg]
    if missing:
        raise ConfigError(f"{p}: missing keys {missing}")
    if cfg["mode"] not in ("sim", "lab"):
        raise ConfigError(f"{p}: mode must be 'sim' or 'lab'")
    if cfg["mode"] == "lab" and "base_url" not in cfg:
        raise ConfigError(f"{p}: lab mode needs base_url")
    # Allow pipeline parameters to override the expected firmware.
    if os.environ.get("EXPECTED_FW"):
        cfg["expected_firmware"] = os.environ["EXPECTED_FW"]
    cfg.setdefault("request_timeout_s", 10)
    cfg.setdefault("allow_power_actions", False)
    cfg.setdefault("verify_tls", True)
    return cfg
def credentials(cfg: dict) -> tuple[str, str]:
    user = os.environ.get("BMC_USER")
    password = os.environ.get("BMC_PASSWORD")
    if cfg["mode"] == "sim":
        return user or "sim-user", password or "sim-only-password"
    if not user or not password:
        raise ConfigError("lab mode requires BMC_USER and BMC_PASSWORD environment
variables")
    return user, password
```

"""Give callers a ready RedfishClient, starting the simulator when mode == sim."""
from __future__ import annotations
import contextlib
from bmcsim.runner import SimulatorHandle
from .client import RedfishClient
from .config import credentials
@contextlib.contextmanager
def open_target(cfg: dict):
    """Yield (client, simulator_or_None)."""
    user, password = credentials(cfg)
    if cfg["mode"] == "sim":
        with SimulatorHandle(user, password) as sim:
            client = RedfishClient(sim.url, user, password, timeout=cfg["request_timeout_
s"])
            try:
                yield client, sim
            finally:
                client.close()
    else:  # LAB ADAPTER: requires an authorised, reachable BMC
        client = RedfishClient(cfg["base_url"], user, password,
                               timeout=cfg["request_timeout_s"], verify_tls=cfg["verify_t
ls"])
        try:
            yield client, None
        finally:
            client.close()

```code
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Pre-test BMC health check. Run BEFORE the suite so an unhealthy lab is reported as
an environment problem instead of producing dozens of misleading test failures.
Exit codes: 0 healthy | 10 unreachable | 11 auth failure | 12 unhealthy | 13 config error
Writes artifacts/health.json in every case.
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import json
import os
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path
sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]))
from bmcclient.client import BMCAuthError, BMCConnectionError  # noqa: E402
from bmcclient.config import ConfigError, load_config           # noqa: E402
from bmcclient.target import open_target                        # noqa: E402
ART = Path(os.environ.get("ARTIFACT_DIR", "artifacts"))
def check(cfg: dict) -> tuple[int, dict]:
    result = {"mode": cfg["mode"], "checks": {}}
    with open_target(cfg) as (bmc, _sim):
        t0 = time.monotonic()
        root = bmc.get("/redfish/v1")
        result["checks"]["service_root"] = {"ok": True, "latency_s": round(time.monotonic
() - t0, 3),
                                            "redfish_version": root.get("RedfishVersion")
}
        mgr = bmc.get(f"/redfish/v1/Managers/{cfg['manager_id']}")
        healthy = mgr.get("Status", {}).get("Health") == "OK"
        result["checks"]["manager"] = {"ok": healthy, "health": mgr.get("Status",
{}).get("Health")}
        result["firmware_version"] = mgr.get("FirmwareVersion")
        system = bmc.get(f"/redfish/v1/Systems/{cfg['system_id']}")
        result["power_state"] = system.get("PowerState")
    return (0 if healthy else 12), result
def main() -> int:
    ART.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    try:
        cfg = load_config()
        rc, result = check(cfg)
        result["status"] = "healthy" if rc == 0 else "unhealthy"
    except ConfigError as exc:
        rc, result = 13, {"status": "config_error", "error": str(exc)}
    except BMCConnectionError as exc:
        rc, result = 10, {"status": "unreachable", "error": str(exc)}
    except BMCAuthError as exc:
        rc, result = 11, {"status": "auth_failed", "error": str(exc)}
    result["exit_code"] = rc
    (ART / "health.json").write_text(json.dumps(result, indent=2))
    print(json.dumps(result, indent=2))
    return rc
if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())
```

lessons.title: scripts/classify_failures.py
lessons.body:
```code
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Turn JUnit XML + health.json into a short, classified summary for humans.
Categories:
  PRODUCT_FAILURE  assertion failed: the BMC behaved unexpectedly -> investigate firmware
  INFRA_FAILURE    BMC unreachable / timeouts -> investigate lab, network, device state
  AUTH_FAILURE     credentials rejected -> investigate Jenkins credentials / accounts
  TEST_CODE_ERROR  other Python exception in test code -> investigate the test framework
  NO_RESULTS       JUnit file missing or unreadable -> investigate the pipeline itself
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import json
import os
import sys
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET
from collections import Counter
from pathlib import Path
ART = Path(os.environ.get("ARTIFACT_DIR", "artifacts"))
REPORTS = Path(os.environ.get("REPORT_DIR", "reports"))
def classify(message: str) -> str:
    """Classify from the JUnit 'message' attribute, whose first line names the exception.
    Do NOT search the whole traceback: it contains source lines that mention other
    exception names (a real bug found while writing this script)."""
    first = message.splitlines()[0] if message else ""
    if "BMCAuthError" in first:
        return "AUTH_FAILURE"
    if "BMCConnectionError" in first or "Timeout" in first:
        return "INFRA_FAILURE"
    if first.startswith(("AssertionError", "assert")):
        return "PRODUCT_FAILURE"
    return "TEST_CODE_ERROR"
def main() -> int:
    summary = {"health": None, "totals": {}, "failures": [], "categories": {}}
    hp = ART / "health.json"
    if hp.exists():
        summary["health"] = json.loads(hp.read_text()).get("status")
    junit = REPORTS / "junit.xml"
    try:
        root = ET.parse(junit).getroot()
    except (OSError, ET.ParseError) as exc:
        summary["categories"] = {"NO_RESULTS": 1}
        summary["error"] = f"{junit}: {exc}"
    else:
        totals = Counter()
        for case in root.iter("testcase"):
            totals["tests"] += 1
            for tag in ("failure", "error", "skipped"):
                el = case.find(tag)
                if el is not None:
                    totals[tag] += 1
                    if tag != "skipped":
                        summary["failures"].append({
                            "test": f"{case.get('classname')}::{case.get('name')}",
                            "category": classify(el.get("message") or ""),
                            "message": (el.get("message") or "").splitlines()[0][:200]
if el.get("message") else ""})
        summary["totals"] = dict(totals)
        summary["categories"] = dict(Counter(f["category"] for f in summary["failures"]))
    ART.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    (ART / "failure_summary.json").write_text(json.dumps(summary, indent=2))
    lines = [f"Health check: {summary['health']}", f"Totals: {summary['totals']}",
             f"Categories: {summary['categories'] or 'none'}"]
    lines += [f"  [{f['category']}] {f['test']}: {f['message']}" for f in summary["failur
es"]]
    (ART / "failure_summary.txt").write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n")
    print("\n".join(lines))
    return 0
if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())
```

lessons.title: Testing strategy
lessons.body:
- **Unit tests** (tests/unit): config validation, locking (including a killed holder), simulated device, firmware orchestration outcomes, logging/masking, classification, optional-adapter errors. Fast, run on every PR, in parallel with byte-compilation in the pipeline.

- **Device tests** (tests/device): run against whatever target the config selects: simulator in PR/CI, lab device in authorised runs.

- **Fault injection** (ETIF_SIM_FAULTS): proves the framework’s failure paths and classification without hardware.

- **Pre-flight** (etif.diagnostics): separates “lab not ready” from test results.

```code
"""Structured (JSON Lines) logging. One JSON object per line is easy to grep, parse
and attach to a bug report. Secrets are masked before anything is written."""
from __future__ import annotations
import json
import logging
import os
import re
import time
from pathlib import Path
_SECRET_KEYS = re.compile(r"(password|passwd|token|secret|authorization)(\"?\s*[:=]
\s*\"?)([^\s\",}]+)", re.I)
def mask(text: str) -> str:
    text = _SECRET_KEYS.sub(lambda m: f"{m.group(1)}{m.group(2)}", text)
    for var in ("DUT_PASSWORD", "BMC_PASSWORD"):
        val = os.environ.get(var)
        if val and len(val) >= 4:
            text = text.replace(val, "")
    return text
class JsonFormatter(logging.Formatter):
    def format(self, record: logging.LogRecord) -> str:
        entry = {
            "ts": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S", time.gmtime(record.created)) + f".{i
nt(record.msecs):03d}Z",
            "level": record.levelname,
            "logger": record.name,
            "msg": mask(record.getMessage()),
        }
        for key in ("device", "test", "category", "step"):
            if hasattr(record, key):
                entry[key] = getattr(record, key)
        if record.exc_info:
            entry["exc"] = mask(self.formatException(record.exc_info))
        return json.dumps(entry)
def setup(log_file: str | os.PathLike, level: int = logging.INFO) -> logging.Logger:
    Path(log_file).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    logger = logging.getLogger("etif")
    logger.setLevel(level)
    for h in list(logger.handlers):
        if getattr(h, "_etif", False):
            logger.removeHandler(h)
            h.close()
    handler = logging.FileHandler(log_file, encoding="utf-8")
    handler.setFormatter(JsonFormatter())
    handler._etif = True
    logger.addHandler(handler)
    return logger
```

lessons.body:
```code
"""Exclusive device locking for jobs that run on the SAME agent host.
Uses an OS-level advisory lock (fcntl.flock, Linux/macOS). The kernel releases the
lock automatically if the process dies, so a crashed job cannot leave a stale lock.
Limitation: this only coordinates processes on one machine. Jobs on different
agents must use a shared mechanism instead, e.g. the Jenkins Lockable Resources
plugin or a lab reservation service.
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import fcntl
import json
import os
import socket
import time
from pathlib import Path
from .errors import LockTimeoutError
class DeviceLock:
    def __init__(self, device: str, lock_dir: str = "/tmp/etif-locks",
                 timeout_s: float = 600.0, poll_s: float = 0.5):
        Path(lock_dir).mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        self.path = Path(lock_dir) / f"{device}.lock"
        self.device, self.timeout_s, self.poll_s = device, timeout_s, poll_s
        self._fh = None
    def holder(self) -> dict | None:
        try:
            return json.loads(self.path.read_text() or "null")
        except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError):
            return None
    def acquire(self) -> None:
        fh = open(self.path, "a+")
        deadline = time.monotonic() + self.timeout_s
        while True:
            try:
                fcntl.flock(fh, fcntl.LOCK_EX | fcntl.LOCK_NB)
                break
            except BlockingIOError:
                if time.monotonic() >= deadline:
                    fh.close()
                    raise LockTimeoutError(
                        f"device {self.device!r} busy for {self.timeout_s}s;
holder={self.holder()}")
                time.sleep(self.poll_s)
        fh.seek(0)
        fh.truncate()
        fh.write(json.dumps({"pid": os.getpid(), "host": socket.gethostname(),
                             "build": os.environ.get("BUILD_TAG", "local"),
                             "since": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ",
time.gmtime())}))
        fh.flush()
        self._fh = fh
    def release(self) -> None:
        if self._fh:
            self._fh.seek(0)
            self._fh.truncate()
            fcntl.flock(self._fh, fcntl.LOCK_UN)
            self._fh.close()
            self._fh = None
    def __enter__(self):
        self.acquire()
        return self
    def __exit__(self, *exc):
        self.release()

"""LAB ADAPTER - SSH command runner (optional dependency: paramiko, see requirements-
lab.txt).
Not executed during the handbook's verification.
Security notes:
  * Host keys are verified against known_hosts (RejectPolicy). Never use AutoAddPolicy
    in CI: it silently trusts whatever answers on that address.
  * Credentials come from the caller (Jenkins withCredentials), never from files in git.
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import time
from ..errors import CommandTimeoutError, DeviceUnavailableError
from .base import CommandResult
class SSHRunner:
    def __init__(self, host: str, user: str, password: str | None = None, key_file: str
| None = None,
                 port: int = 22, connect_timeout_s: float = 10.0, known_hosts: str |
None = None):
        try:
            import paramiko  # noqa: PLC0415 - optional dependency
        except ImportError as exc:
            raise ImportError("SSH support needs paramiko: pip install -r requirements-
lab.txt") from exc
        self._paramiko = paramiko
        self.client = paramiko.SSHClient()
        self.client.load_system_host_keys()
        if known_hosts:
            self.client.load_host_keys(known_hosts)
        self.client.set_missing_host_key_policy(paramiko.RejectPolicy())
        self.params = dict(hostname=host, port=port, username=user, password=password,
                           key_filename=key_file, timeout=connect_timeout_s,
                           banner_timeout=connect_timeout_s, auth_timeout=connect_timeout
_s)
        self._connected = False
    def connect(self) -> None:
        try:
            self.client.connect(**self.params)
            self._connected = True
        except (OSError, self._paramiko.SSHException) as exc:
            raise DeviceUnavailableError(f"SSH {self.params['hostname']}: {exc}") from
exc
    def run(self, command: str, timeout_s: float) -> CommandResult:
        if not self._connected:
            self.connect()
        start = time.monotonic()
        try:
            _stdin, stdout, stderr = self.client.exec_command(command, timeout=timeout_s)
            out, err = stdout.read().decode(errors="replace"),
stderr.read().decode(errors="replace")
            code = stdout.channel.recv_exit_status()
        except TimeoutError as exc:   # socket.timeout is an alias of TimeoutError
(3.10+)
            raise CommandTimeoutError(f"{command!r} timed out after {timeout_s}s") from
exc
        except (OSError, self._paramiko.SSHException) as exc:
            self._connected = False      # force reconnect next time (e.g. after reboot)
            raise DeviceUnavailableError(f"SSH command failed: {exc}") from exc
        return CommandResult(command, code, out, err, time.monotonic() - start)
    def close(self) -> None:
        self.client.close()
        self._connected = False

"""LAB ADAPTER - serial console capture (optional dependency: pyserial).
Not executed during the handbook's verification.
A serial port can be opened by only one reader at a time. Hold the device lock
(etif.locking or Jenkins lock()) before opening it, and close it in a finally block.
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import time
from pathlib import Path
class UARTConsole:
    def __init__(self, port: str, baud: int = 115200, read_timeout_s: float = 0.5):
        try:
            import serial  # noqa: PLC0415 - optional dependency (package: pyserial)
        except ImportError as exc:
            raise ImportError("UART support needs pyserial: pip install -r requirements-
lab.txt") from exc
        self._serial_mod = serial
        self.port, self.baud, self.read_timeout_s = port, baud, read_timeout_s
        self._ser = None
    def open(self) -> None:
        self._ser = self._serial_mod.Serial(self.port, self.baud, timeout=self.read_timeo
ut_s)
    def capture(self, seconds: float, out_file: str | Path, stop_on: str | None = None) -
> str:
        """Read console output for up to `seconds` (bounded), append it to out_file."""
        if self._ser is None:
            self.open()
        buf = bytearray()
        deadline = time.monotonic() + seconds
        while time.monotonic() < deadline:
            chunk = self._ser.read(4096)
            if chunk:
                buf += chunk
                if stop_on and stop_on.encode() in buf:
                    break
        text = buf.decode(errors="replace")
        with open(out_file, "a", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            fh.write(text)
        return text
    def close(self) -> None:
        if self._ser is not None:
            self._ser.close()
            self._ser = None

"""Firmware update orchestration: pre-checks -> start -> monitor -> reboot -> post-
checks.
Every wait is bounded. Every step is logged and recorded, so a failed update leaves
evidence. The orchestrator refuses to run unless the target explicitly allows
firmware updates (allow_firmware_update: true), which is only set for the simulator
or an authorised, reserved lab device.
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import logging
import time
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from .adapters.base import DeviceAdapter
from .errors import DeviceUnavailableError, EtifError, FirmwareUpdateError
log = logging.getLogger("etif.fwupdate")
@dataclass
class UpdateReport:
    image: str
    version_before: str | None = None
    version_after: str | None = None
    expected_version: str | None = None
    result: str = "NOT_STARTED"            # PASSED | FAILED | NOT_STARTED
    category: str | None = None
    steps: list[dict] = field(default_factory=list)
    def step(self, name: str, **info) -> None:
        entry = {"step": name, "t": round(time.monotonic(), 3), **info}
        self.steps.append(entry)
        log.info("%s %s", name, info, extra={"step": name})
class FirmwareUpdateOrchestrator:
    def __init__(self, device: DeviceAdapter, *, allowed: bool, update_timeout_s: float
= 1800,
                 ready_timeout_s: float = 600, poll_s: float = 5.0):
        self.device, self.allowed = device, allowed
        self.update_timeout_s, self.ready_timeout_s, self.poll_s = update_timeout_s,
ready_timeout_s, poll_s
        self.last_report: UpdateReport | None = None   # kept even when run() raises
    def run(self, image: str, expected_version: str) -> UpdateReport:
        report = UpdateReport(image=image, expected_version=expected_version)
        self.last_report = report
        if not self.allowed:
            raise EtifError("firmware update not allowed for this target
(allow_firmware_update: false)")
        try:
            # 1. Pre-checks: device healthy and version known BEFORE we change anything.
            report.version_before = self.device.firmware_version()
            report.step("precheck", version=report.version_before, power=self.device.powe
r_state())
            if report.version_before == expected_version:
                report.step("precheck_note", note="device already runs the expected
version")
            # 2. Start the update.
            task = self.device.start_firmware_update(image)
            report.step("started", task=task)
            # 3. Monitor until a terminal state or the deadline.
            deadline = time.monotonic() + self.update_timeout_s
            while True:
                status = self.device.update_status(task)
                report.step("status", **status)
                if status["state"] == "Completed":
                    break
                if status["state"] in ("Failed", "Exception", "Cancelled"):
                    raise FirmwareUpdateError(f"update task {task} ended in {status['stat
e']}: "
                                              f"{status.get('message')}")
                if time.monotonic() >= deadline:
                    raise FirmwareUpdateError(f"update task {task} still
{status['state']} after "
                                              f"{self.update_timeout_s}s")
                time.sleep(self.poll_s)
            # 4. Wait for the BMC to come back after the activation reboot.
            waited = self.device.wait_until_ready(self.ready_timeout_s, poll_s=self.poll_
s)
            report.step("ready", waited_s=round(waited, 2))
            # 5. Post-check: the version must actually have changed to the expected one.
            report.version_after = self.device.firmware_version()
            report.step("postcheck", version=report.version_after)
            if report.version_after != expected_version:
                raise FirmwareUpdateError(f"running {report.version_after!r} after
update, "
                                          f"expected {expected_version!r}")
            report.result = "PASSED"
        except EtifError as exc:
            report.result = "FAILED"
            report.category = exc.category
            report.step("error", category=exc.category, error=str(exc))
            if isinstance(exc, DeviceUnavailableError):
                report.step("recovery_hint", hint="device did not return: check console
log, "
                            "power-cycle via lab PDU, follow platform recovery
procedure")
            raise
        finally:
            report.step("console_tail", lines=self.device.console_log().splitlines()[-5:]
)
        return report

"""Cheap pre-flight checks: is the device there at all, before any test runs?"""
from __future__ import annotations
import socket
import time
def tcp_port_open(host: str, port: int, timeout_s: float = 3.0) -> tuple[bool, str]:
    start = time.monotonic()
    try:
        with socket.create_connection((host, port), timeout=timeout_s):
            return True, f"connected in {time.monotonic() - start:.3f}s"
    except socket.gaierror as exc:
        return False, f"DNS failure: {exc}"
    except TimeoutError:
        return False, f"timeout after {timeout_s}s"
    except ConnectionRefusedError:
        return False, "connection refused (host up, service down?)"
    except OSError as exc:
        return False, f"{exc.__class__.__name__}: {exc}"

"""Failure classification shared by the pytest plugin and the pipeline summary."""
from __future__ import annotations
from .errors import EtifError
CATEGORIES = {
    "PRODUCT_FAILURE": "Assertion failed: device behaved unexpectedly. Owner: firmware/
product team.",
    "FIRMWARE_REGRESSION": "Firmware update or post-update check failed. Owner: firmware
team.",
    "DEVICE_COMMUNICATION":
"Device reachable but a transfer/command failed or timed out. Owner: test infra +
firmware.",
    "LAB_UNAVAILABLE": "Device unreachable or reserved by another job. Owner: lab/
infra.",
    "AUTH_FAILURE": "Credentials rejected. Owner: whoever manages the Jenkins credential/
BMC account.",
    "CONFIG_ERROR": "Bad or missing configuration. Owner: pipeline/test owner.",
    "TEST_CODE_ERROR": "Unexpected Python exception in test or framework code. Owner:
test author.",
    "FRAMEWORK_ERROR": "Framework raised a generic error. Owner: test infra.",
}
def classify_exception(exc: BaseException) -> str:
    if isinstance(exc, AssertionError):
        return "PRODUCT_FAILURE"
    if isinstance(exc, EtifError):
        return exc.category
    return "TEST_CODE_ERROR"

"""Pre-flight diagnostics: `python -m etif.diagnostics --out artifacts/preflight.json`
Exit codes: 0 ready | 10 device unavailable | 11 auth | 13 config error
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import argparse
import json
import platform
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from . import config as config_mod
from .adapters import factory
from .availability import tcp_port_open
from .errors import AuthenticationError, ConfigError, DeviceUnavailableError, EtifError
EXIT = {"LAB_UNAVAILABLE": 10, "DEVICE_COMMUNICATION": 10, "AUTH_FAILURE": 11, "CONFIG_ER
ROR": 13}
def run(cfg_path: str | None) -> tuple[int, dict]:
    out = {"python": sys.version.split()[0], "platform": platform.platform()}
    try:
        cfg = config_mod.load(cfg_path)
        out.update(target=cfg.name, adapter=cfg.adapter)
        if not cfg.is_simulated:
            ok, detail = tcp_port_open(cfg.host, cfg.port, timeout_s=cfg.request_timeout_
s)
            out["tcp_check"] = {"ok": ok, "detail": detail}
            if not ok:
                raise DeviceUnavailableError(f"{cfg.host}:{cfg.port} {detail}")
        dev = factory.create(cfg)
        try:
            if not dev.is_reachable():
                raise DeviceUnavailableError(f"{cfg.name} not reachable")
            out["firmware_version"] = dev.firmware_version()
            out["power_state"] = dev.power_state()
            out["firmware_matches_expected"] = out["firmware_version"] ==
cfg.expected_firmware
        finally:
            dev.close()
        out["status"] = "ready"
        return 0, out
    except (ConfigError, DeviceUnavailableError, AuthenticationError, EtifError) as exc:
        out.update(status="not_ready", category=exc.category, error=str(exc))
        return EXIT.get(exc.category, 1), out
def main(argv=None) -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="etif pre-flight diagnostics")
    ap.add_argument("--config", default=None)
    ap.add_argument("--out", default="artifacts/preflight.json")
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
    rc, result = run(args.config)
    result["exit_code"] = rc
    Path(args.out).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    Path(args.out).write_text(json.dumps(result, indent=2))
    print(json.dumps(result, indent=2))
    return rc
if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

"""These tests change device state. pytest runs files in name order, so this file
(test_state_changing.py) runs after test_identity.py and test_sensors.py. They only
run when the target config allows power actions / firmware updates."""
import json
import pytest
from etif.fwupdate import FirmwareUpdateOrchestrator
@pytest.mark.regression
@pytest.mark.power
def test_bmc_reboot_recovers(device, etif_config):
    device.reboot_bmc()
    waited = device.wait_until_ready(etif_config.ready_timeout_s, poll_s=0.05)
    assert device.firmware_version() == etif_config.expected_firmware
    assert waited < etif_config.ready_timeout_s
@pytest.mark.firmware_update
def test_firmware_update_to_next_version(device, etif_config, evidence_dir):
    target_version = etif_config.sim.get("next_firmware", "UNSET")
    orch = FirmwareUpdateOrchestrator(device, allowed=etif_config.allow_firmware_update,
                                      update_timeout_s=5, ready_timeout_s=etif_config.rea
dy_timeout_s,
                                      poll_s=0.05)
    try:
        report = orch.run("images/bmc-next.static.mtd.tar", expected_version=target_versi
on)
    finally:
        # Write the step-by-step record whether the update passed or failed: it is the
evidence.
        if orch.last_report is not None:
            (evidence_dir / "update_report.json").write_text(
                json.dumps(orch.last_report.__dict__, indent=2, default=str))
    assert report.result == "PASSED"

lessons.body:
```code
import pytest
from etif.adapters.simulated import SimulatedDevice
from etif.errors import DeviceUnavailableError, EtifError, FirmwareUpdateError
from etif.fwupdate import FirmwareUpdateOrchestrator
def orch(dev, **kw):
    kw.setdefault("allowed", True)
    return FirmwareUpdateOrchestrator(dev, update_timeout_s=1, ready_timeout_s=1,
poll_s=0.02, **kw)
def test_successful_update_changes_version():
    dev = SimulatedDevice("d", update_step_s=0.02, reboot_s=0.05)
    report = orch(dev).run("image-2.17.0.tar", expected_version="2.17.0-sim")
    assert report.result == "PASSED"
    assert (report.version_before, report.version_after) == ("2.16.0-sim", "2.17.0-sim")
    assert [s["step"] for s in report.steps][-1] == "console_tail"
def test_update_refused_when_not_allowed():
    with pytest.raises(EtifError, match="not allowed"):
        orch(SimulatedDevice("d"), allowed=False).run("img", "2.17.0-sim")
def test_failed_update_is_a_firmware_regression():
    dev = SimulatedDevice("d", faults=["update_fails"], update_step_s=0.01)
    with pytest.raises(FirmwareUpdateError) as ei:
        orch(dev).run("img", "2.17.0-sim")
    assert ei.value.category == "FIRMWARE_REGRESSION"
def test_report_is_kept_when_update_fails():
    dev = SimulatedDevice("d", faults=["update_fails"], update_step_s=0.01)
    o = orch(dev)
    with pytest.raises(FirmwareUpdateError):
        o.run("img", "2.17.0-sim")
    assert o.last_report.result == "FAILED"
    assert any(s["step"] == "error" for s in o.last_report.steps)
def test_hanging_update_is_bounded():
    dev = SimulatedDevice("d", faults=["update_hangs"], update_step_s=0.01)
    with pytest.raises(FirmwareUpdateError, match="still Running"):
        orch(dev).run("img", "2.17.0-sim")
def test_device_not_returning_after_update():
    dev = SimulatedDevice("d", faults=["no_ready_after_reboot"], update_step_s=0.01)
    with pytest.raises(DeviceUnavailableError):
        orch(dev).run("img", "2.17.0-sim")
def test_wrong_version_after_update():
    dev = SimulatedDevice("d", update_step_s=0.01, reboot_s=0.02, next_firmware="2.16.1-
sim")
    with pytest.raises(FirmwareUpdateError, match="expected"):
        orch(dev).run("img", "2.17.0-sim")
```

lessons.title: tests/unit/test_locking.py
lessons.body:
```code
import multiprocessing as mp
import time
import pytest
from etif.errors import LockTimeoutError
from etif.locking import DeviceLock
def _hold(lock_dir, seconds, ready):
    with DeviceLock("dut", lock_dir):
        ready.set()
        time.sleep(seconds)
def test_second_holder_times_out(tmp_path):
    ready = mp.Event()
    p = mp.Process(target=_hold, args=(str(tmp_path), 2.0, ready))
    p.start()
    try:
        assert ready.wait(5)
        lock = DeviceLock("dut", str(tmp_path), timeout_s=0.3, poll_s=0.05)
        with pytest.raises(LockTimeoutError, match="busy"):
            lock.acquire()
    finally:
        p.join()
def test_lock_is_released_when_holder_dies(tmp_path):
    ready = mp.Event()
    p = mp.Process(target=_hold, args=(str(tmp_path), 30.0, ready))
    p.start()
    assert ready.wait(5)
    p.kill()                       # simulate a crashed job
    p.join()
    with DeviceLock("dut", str(tmp_path), timeout_s=1.0, poll_s=0.05) as lock:
        assert lock.holder()["build"] == "local"
```

lessons.title: Known limitations
lessons.body:
- DeviceLock uses fcntl (Linux/macOS); it coordinates processes on one machine only.

- SimulatedDevice is a behavioural model; timings are artificial.

- RedfishAdapter.sensors() follows the DMTF Sensor schema (Thresholds.*.Reading); platforms may differ.

- Lab adapters are untested here; pin paramiko/pyserial versions after testing in your lab.

**29.1** Add an IPMIAdapter skeleton for a lab that uses ipmitool. **Solution:** subclass `DeviceAdapter; implement firmware_version() by running ipmitool -I lanplus -H host -U` user -E mc info (-E reads the password from the IPMI_PASSWORD environment variable) with subprocess.run(..., timeout=...) and parsing “Firmware Revision”; map non-zero `exits and timeouts to DeviceCommunicationError/DeviceUnavailableError; register adapter:` ipmi in config.VALID_ADAPTERS and factory.create(). Mark it LAB-ONLY.

**29.2** Write a unit test proving DeviceLock records the holder’s build tag. **Solution:**

assert lock.holder()["build"] == "jenkins-x-1"; release.

lessons.title: Verifying project completeness
lessons.body:
Checklist used for this handbook’s projects:

• Fresh clone + documented commands works on a clean machine/container. • Dependencies pinned; pip freeze recorded. • Unit tests for framework code; tests for pipeline helper scripts. • Failure paths demonstrated (fault injection), not just the happy path. • Reports produced (JUnit + human-readable) and archived. • No secrets, internal hostnames, real logs or employer code. • Each untested part labelled as such.

lessons.title: Writing useful READMEs
lessons.body: Order: one-line purpose → quick start (copy-paste) → what it demonstrates → architecture diagram → how to run variants (faults, suites) → verification status table → limitations → how to extend. See the three project READMEs.

lessons.title: Architecture diagrams
lessons.body: One diagram per project showing layers and boundaries (Chapter 29), plus the pipeline stage map (Chapter 23). ASCII or a simple drawing tool is fine; clarity beats decoration.

lessons.title: Sample reports
lessons.body: Commit **generated examples** to docs/samples/ from simulated runs (JUnit XML, failure_summary.txt, an HTML report) so reviewers see output without running anything. Mark them as samples from the simulator.

lessons.title: Unit and integration tests
lessons.body: Show you test your tooling, not only the product: Project 2’s selftest/ and Project 3’s tests/unit/ are strong interview talking points (“the classifier had a bug; the self-test now covers it”).

lessons.title: Documenting limitations
lessons.body: Honest limitations increase credibility: “The Jenkinsfile was reviewed but not run on a server”, “lab adapters untested without hardware”, “simulator timings are artificial”.

lessons.title: Demonstrating failure handling
lessons.body: Record a short screencast or include console excerpts for: product failure, auth failure stopped by health gate, unreachable device, hanging firmware update hitting its deadline, missing report handling.

lessons.title: Protecting employer intellectual property
lessons.body:
- Never publish employer source, test cases, internal tool names, hostnames, IP plans, logs, firmware, or customer/platform names under NDA.

- Recreate concepts from scratch with synthetic data and public standards (Redfish).

- Check your employment contract and company policy; when in doubt, ask.

- Talk about what you did and learned at work, not the confidential content.

lessons.title: Preparing project explanations for interviews
lessons.body:
Use a **problem → design → evidence → result → lesson** structure, 2 minutes each:

“Embedded regression results were hard to trust because lab outages looked like test failures. I built a pipeline where a health gate runs first and every failure is classified from typed exceptions at the adapter boundary. With the simulator I can inject faults: an auth failure stops the run with exit 11 instead of producing eleven fake failures. A bug I found: my classifier read whole tracebacks and misclassified auth errors as infrastructure; I fixed it to use the exception line and added self-tests. Everything runs locally and in Jenkins with the same scripts.” Prepare for follow-ups: “How would this scale to 20 boards?” (label locks, pools, matrix), “What if the device bricks?” (recovery procedure, health gate, notification), “Why pytest over Robot Framework?” (Python ecosystem, fixtures, plugins; note that OpenBMC’s own test-automation repository uses Robot Framework, and the pipeline principles are the same).

lessons.title: Exercises
lessons.body:
**30.1** Write a 5-line README “Verification status” table for Project 1. **Solution:** see the table in Project 3’s README; rows: unit tests (executed), local pipeline script (executed), Jenkinsfile (reviewed), HTML report (executed), GitHub Actions workflow (reviewed/executed if you ran it).

**30.2** Turn your current job experience into a portfolio idea without IP risk. **Solution (example):** “Redfish sensor regression with simulator and fault injection” using public Redfish schemas and synthetic data, not your company’s tests.

lessons.title: Branching and merging
lessons.body:
**Q1. What is a branch in Git, internally?** A movable pointer (a small file containing a commit hash) to a commit. Creating one is instant; commits on it move the pointer forward. HEAD points to the current branch.

**Q2. Fast-forward vs three-way merge?** Fast-forward moves the target pointer when it has no new commits; no merge commit. Three-way merge combines two diverged histories using their common ancestor and records a merge commit with two parents. git merge --no-ff forces a merge commit to keep a visible feature boundary.

**Q3. How do you keep a feature branch up to date with main?** git fetch then git rebase origin/main for a private branch (clean history), or git merge origin/main for a shared branch. Do it frequently to keep conflicts small.

**Q4. What branching strategy suits a firmware validation team?** Trunk-based development on main with short-lived feature branches and PR checks, plus release/<fw-version> branches for test suites that qualify released firmware; fixes cherry-picked to release branches.

lessons.title: Rebase versus merge
lessons.body:
**Q5. Rebase vs merge?** Rebase replays your commits on a new base, producing a linear history with new hashes. Merge keeps history as it happened and adds a merge commit. Rebase private work; merge shared work.

**Q6. What is the golden rule of rebasing?** Never rebase commits that others have based work on (published shared branches).

**Q7. What is interactive rebase used for?** Cleaning up your own commits before review: squash, reorder, reword, drop.

**Q8. Why use --force-with-lease instead of --force?** It refuses to overwrite the remote branch if it changed since you last fetched, so you do not destroy someone else’s commits.

lessons.title: Reset versus revert
lessons.body:
**Q9. Reset vs revert?** revert creates a new commit undoing a previous one: safe for shared history. reset moves the branch pointer (soft/mixed/hard), removing commits from the branch: only for local/private history.

**Q10. Difference between reset --soft, --mixed, --hard?** All move the branch pointer. Soft keeps changes staged; mixed keeps them in the working directory unstaged; hard discards them.

**Q11. How do you undo a pushed merge commit?** git revert -m 1 <merge-commit>; -m 1 keeps the first parent (mainline). Note that re-merging the same branch later requires reverting the revert.

lessons.title: Conflicts
lessons.body:
**Q12. What causes a merge conflict and how do you resolve it?** Both sides changed the same lines (or one deleted a file the other changed). Open the file, decide the correct content (talk to the author if unsure), remove markers, run tests, git add, `git commit (or rebase --continue). --abort to back out.`

**Q13. How do you reduce conflicts in a test repository?** Small PRs, frequent syncing, one topic per file, configuration in structured files with stable ordering, formatter run by everyone.

lessons.title: Pull requests
lessons.body:
**Q14. What makes a good PR?** Single purpose, small, clear description with how it was tested, CI green, no secrets, reviewers from CODEOWNERS.

**Q15. What do you check when reviewing a test PR?** Meaningful assertions with messages, bounded waits, cleanup in fixtures, markers for hardware/destructive needs, no hardcoded hosts/credentials, stable in CI.

**Q16. What is cherry-pick and when do you use it?** Applying one commit’s change onto another branch as a new commit, e.g. porting a test fix to a release branch. Use -x to record the source.

lessons.title: Authentication
lessons.body:
**Q17. HTTPS vs SSH for Git?** HTTPS uses tokens (passwords are no longer accepted by major hosts); SSH uses key pairs. SSH is convenient for developers; CI often uses deploy keys or app tokens with minimal scope.

**Q18. Permission denied (publickey) — what do you check?** Is the public key added to the account/deploy keys; is the right key offered (ssh -vT git@host, ~/.ssh/config); right user; agent loaded (ssh-add -l).

**Q19. What is a deploy key?** An SSH key attached to one repository, often read-only, used by automation. Least privilege compared with a personal key.

lessons.title: Repository security
lessons.body:
**Q20. A password was pushed. What do you do?** Rotate it immediately; check for misuse; then remove it from history (git-filter-repo), force-push with coordination, have collaborators re-clone; add secret scanning to prevent recurrence.

**Q21. Is .gitignore a security control?** No. It prevents accidental adds of untracked files only; git add -f overrides it and tracked files are unaffected. Use scanning and review.

**Q22. Why not store firmware images in Git?** History keeps every version forever; clones and CI checkouts grow huge. Use an artifact store or Git LFS.

lessons.title: Troubleshooting
lessons.body:
**Q23. How do you recover a deleted branch?** git reflog to find the last commit, then `git branch <name> <hash>.`

**Q24. What is detached HEAD?** HEAD points to a commit, not a branch. Safe to inspect; create a branch before committing there. CI uses it to build exact commits.

**Q25. How do you find which commit broke a test?** git bisect start; git bisect bad; `git bisect good <tag>, then test each step (or git bisect run python -m pytest tests/` test_x.py) until Git names the first bad commit.

**Q26. Jenkins checkout fails but your laptop works. Why?** Different credentials (deploy key vs personal), missing host key on the agent, Git missing on the agent, wrong branch specifier, network/proxy differences.

**Q27. How do you see what will be committed?** git diff --staged (and git status).

lessons.title: Practical example to rehearse
lessons.body:
```code
# Find the commit that changed a timeout and broke a test
git log -S "REDFISH_TIMEOUT_S" --oneline -- config.py
git bisect start HEAD v1.0.0
git bisect run python -m pytest -q tests/test_power.py
git bisect reset
```

git log -S finds commits that added or removed the string; bisect run uses the command’s exit code (0 = good, 1–127 except 125 = bad, 125 = skip).

lessons.title: Jenkins architecture
lessons.body:
**Q1. Explain Jenkins architecture.** A controller schedules builds, stores configuration, credentials and results, and serves the UI; agents connected over a remoting channel execute the steps in workspaces; plugins provide most features; builds wait in a queue for an executor on a node whose labels match.

**Q2. What is in JENKINS_HOME and why back it up?** Global and job configuration, build history, archived artifacts, plugins and encrypted credentials with their keys. Losing it loses the CI system.

**Q3. Why zero executors on the controller?** Security (build code could access all secrets and configuration) and stability.

lessons.title: Agents and executors
lessons.body:
**Q4. Executor vs agent?** An agent is a machine connected to the controller; an executor is one concurrent build slot on a node.

**Q5. How does Jenkins choose where to run a stage?** The agent/label expression; the scheduler picks an online node with matching labels and a free executor.

**Q6. SSH agent vs inbound agent?** SSH: controller connects to the agent. Inbound: the agent connects to the controller (TCP or WebSocket), useful behind firewalls/NAT, e.g. in labs.

**Q7. An agent shows offline. What do you check?** Agent log on the node page, Java version compatibility, network/URL/secret, disk space, memory, whether the machine is up.

lessons.title: Freestyle vs Pipeline
lessons.body: **Q8. Freestyle vs Pipeline?** Freestyle is UI-configured, simple, not versioned with code; Pipeline is code (Jenkinsfile), versioned and reviewed, supports stages, parallelism, error handling, and survives controller restarts.

lessons.title: Declarative Pipeline syntax
lessons.body:
**Q9. Name the main Declarative sections.** pipeline, agent, stages/stage/steps, `environment, options, parameters, triggers, tools, when, post, plus parallel and matrix.`

**Q10. What does when { beforeAgent true } do?** Evaluates the condition before allocating the stage’s agent, so a skipped stage does not occupy an executor.

**Q11. Post conditions you use and why?** always (publish reports/archive), failure/ unstable (notify), fixed/regression (state-change notifications), cleanup (workspace cleanup, runs last).

**Q12. How do you set a build to UNSTABLE deliberately?** unstable('reason'), `warnError, catchError(buildResult: 'UNSTABLE', ...), or the junit step when reports` contain failures.

**Q13. How do you capture a command’s exit code or output?** sh(returnStatus: true, `script: ...) or sh(returnStdout: true, script: ...).trim().`

**Q14. Why can PIPESTATUS fail inside sh?** Jenkins runs sh with /bin/sh (often dash); add #!/bin/bash as the first line.

lessons.title: Jenkinsfiles
lessons.body:
**Q15. Why keep the Jenkinsfile in the repository?** Versioned with the code it builds, reviewed in PRs, reproducible, branch-specific.

**Q16. How do you validate a Jenkinsfile?** Declarative linter (CLI/HTTP), Replay for experiments, Snippet Generator for syntax, small test jobs.

**Q17. What are shared libraries and how do you version them?** Reusable pipeline code in a separate repo (vars/, src/), loaded with @Library('name@tag'); pin to tags to avoid surprise changes.

lessons.title: Credentials
lessons.body:
**Q18. How do pipelines use credentials safely?** Credentials store + withCredentials (or credentials() in environment), smallest scope, single-quoted shell strings, never echo, least-privilege accounts, folder-scoped credentials.

**Q19. What does Jenkins do if you interpolate a secret into sh with Groovy?** Prints a warning that a secret was passed using Groovy string interpolation, which is insecure; the secret is part of the script text.

lessons.title: Parallel execution
lessons.body:
**Q20. How do you run stages in parallel and what are the pitfalls?** parallel { stage ... } or matrix; pitfalls: shared workspace files, limited executors, shared hardware needing locks, failFast choices.

**Q21. How do you prevent two builds using the same BMC?** Lockable Resources: lock(resource: 'bmc-x') or label pools with quantity; keep lock scope tight; release automatically at block end.

lessons.title: Reports and artifacts
lessons.body:
**Q22. How do test results appear in Jenkins?** pytest writes JUnit XML; the junit step (JUnit plugin) parses it, shows results and trends, and marks the build UNSTABLE on failures.

**Q23. What do you archive for embedded test runs?** JUnit/HTML reports, console logs, device snapshots, console/UART and journal logs, environment metadata, pip freeze, classification summary.

**Q24. A JUnit report is missing. How should the pipeline behave?** Fail with a clear message (allowEmptyResults: false where tests must run), because missing results mean the run is broken, not passed.

lessons.title: Failure handling
lessons.body:
**Q25. How do you distinguish test failures from pipeline failures?** Map exit codes (pytest 1 → UNSTABLE; 2–5 → FAILURE), health gates before tests, typed exceptions and classification per test.

**Q26. When is retry appropriate?** Idempotent, transient operations (checkout, pip install, readiness polling), and agent-loss conditions; not for test suites or non-idempotent device actions.

**Q27. How do you design timeouts?** Operation timeouts < per-test < stage < pipeline; inactivity timeouts for hangs; every wait is a poll with a deadline.

lessons.title: Pipeline security
lessons.body:
**Q28. Risks of building pull requests?** PR code runs on your agents with whatever credentials and network access the build has. Use trusted Jenkinsfiles for untrusted PRs, isolated agents, no secrets, manual approval for hardware.

**Q29. How do you harden a Jenkins controller?** Authentication + authorisation, no controller executors, updated core/plugins, few plugins, HTTPS, restricted Script Console, backups, sandboxed pipelines.

**Q30. CI vs CD vs continuous deployment?** CI: integrate and test every change; continuous delivery: every change releasable with a manual release decision; continuous deployment: automatic release.

**Q31. How would you migrate Freestyle jobs to Pipeline?** Inventory jobs, write equivalent Jenkinsfiles (one stage per build step, post for publishers), run both in parallel for a while, compare results, switch triggers, archive the old jobs.

**Q32. How does a webhook-triggered PR build report back to GitHub?** Branch source plugin builds the PR, then posts a commit status/check; branch protection requires it before merging.

lessons.title: Scenario 1 — Jenkins job works on one agent, fails on another
lessons.body:
- **Symptoms:** Same commit passes on linux-01, fails on linux-02 with ModuleNotFoundError or different results.

- **Likely causes:** different Python versions/system packages; dependencies leaking from system site-packages; missing tools; permissions.

- **Investigation:** compare python --version, pip freeze artifacts, agent labels, environment dumps.

- Commands: sh 'python3 --version; which python3; python3 -m pip --version; env |

```code
sort'
```

- **Expected:** version or package differences.

- **Corrective:** fresh venv from pinned requirements; or container agent.

- **Prevention:** agent provisioning as code; env-check stage; archive pip freeze.

- **Answer:** “I compared the archived environments of both builds, found the agents had different Python and packages, and made the pipeline build its own pinned venv so agents can’t differ silently.”
